children.translated_text: <s>Rasendracūḍāmaṇi</s>, Chapter 3
One should construct the alchemical laboratory (<s>rasaśālā</s>) in a place free from all disturbances,
in a land rich in all medicinal herbs, pleasant, and furnished with a well. // Rcūm 3.1 //
In a beautiful quarter facing the directions presided over by <s>Yakṣarāja</s> and <s>Sahasrākṣa</s> (Indra),
equipped with various implements and adorned with a surrounding wall. // Rcūm 3.2 //
{What should be placed where in the alchemical laboratory?}
In the eastern quarter of the laboratory one should install <s>Rasabhairava</s>;

children.text: vahnikarmāṇi cāgneye yāmye pāṣāṇakarma ca // Rcūm_3.3 //
children.translated_text: fire-related operations in the southeast, stone-work in the south. // Rcūm 3.3 //
Cutting operations with instruments in the southwest, washing and the like in the west,

children.text: śoṣaṇaṃ vāyukoṇe ca vedhakarmottare tathā // Rcūm_3.4 //
children.translated_text: drying in the northwest corner, and transmutation operations in the north. // Rcūm 3.4 //
Storage of perfected substances should be arranged in the northeast corner;
a collection of materials should be made for the purpose of alchemical operations. // Rcūm 3.5 //
{Collection of equipment for the alchemical laboratory}
A furnace for extracting metallic essences (<s>sattvapātana-koṣṭhī</s>), a fine calcination furnace (<s>gāra-koṣṭhī</s>),
an underground furnace (<s>bhūmi-koṣṭhī</s>), a portable furnace (<s>calat-koṣṭhī</s>), and water troughs in abundance. // Rcūm 3.6 //
A pair of bellows, likewise tubes of bamboo and iron,
crucibles made of gold alloy, bell-metal, copper, stone, and leather. // Rcūm 3.7 //
One should gather all manner of diverse instruments:

children.text: manthānaḥ peṣaṇī khalvā droṇīrūpāśca vartulāḥ // Rcūm_3.8 //
children.translated_text: churning rods, grinding stones, mortars, and round vessel-shaped troughs. // Rcūm 3.8 //
Iron heated mortars and grinders of similar kind,
perforated with thousands of fine holes for the purpose of sifting substances. // Rcūm 3.9 //

children.text: cālanī ca kaṭatrāṇī śilā laulī ca kaṇḍanī /
children.translated_text: A sieve (<s>cālanī</s>), a shield (<s>kaṭatrāṇī</s>), a grinding slab (<s>śilā</s>), a stirring rod (<s>laulī</s>), and a scratcher (<s>kaṇḍanī</s>);
crucibles (<s>mūṣā</s>), clay, borax, cotton, and dried cow-dung cakes. // Rcūm 3.10 //
Medicines are of three kinds: mineral, animal, and plant-based;

children.text: śikhitrā govaraṃ caiva śarkarā ca sitopalā // Rcūm_3.11 //
children.translated_text: also charcoal (<s>śikhitrā</s>), cow dung (<s>govaraṃ</s>), raw sugar (<s>śarkarā</s>), and rock candy (<s>sitopalā</s>). // Rcūm 3.11 //
Bottles made of glass, iron, clay, and cowrie shells, as well as cups;
winnowing fans and bamboo vessels, small quick-pourers and conch-shells. // Rcūm 3.12 //
Also razors and ladles, and whatever else is suitable there;
a small pan (<s>pālikā</s>), a pair of tongs (<s>karṇikā</s>), and a vegetable-cutting knife. // Rcūm 3.13 //
Indeed, for the purpose of sweeping the laboratory, and whatever work comes between alchemical preparations,
whatever else is useful therein — all that by the supreme science, // Rcūm 3.14 //
having consecrated everything with the sacred <s>Rasāṅkuśā</s> mantra, one should collect it;

children.text: anyathā tadgataṃ tejaḥ parigṛhṇāti bhairavaḥ // Rcūm_3.15 //
children.translated_text: otherwise, <s>Bhairava</s> seizes the potency contained therein. // Rcūm 3.15 //
{Sieve}

children.text: cālinī trividhā proktā tatsvarūpaṃ ca kathyate /
children.translated_text: The sieve (<s>cālinī</s>) is said to be of three kinds; its form is now described:
one made with bamboo rods, tied together with cords. // Rcūm 3.16 //

children.text: kīrtitā sā sadā sthūladravyāṇāṃ gālane hitā /
children.translated_text: That is always recommended for straining coarse substances;
for sifting powders, another sieve also made of bamboo. // Rcūm 3.17 //
Made with the wood of <s>karṇikāra</s>, <s>śālmalī</s> (silk-cotton tree), <s>pārijāta</s>, and <s>kamba</s>,
auspiciously constructed with a width of four fingers. // Rcūm 3.18 //
Having the width of a bracelet-ring, covered with goat-skin,
with a bottom stretched with horse-tail hair cloth — that is the superior sieve. // Rcūm 3.19 //
With that one should perform the sifting, to retain the finest powder.
{Charcoal}

children.text: śikhitrāḥ pāvakocchiṣṭā aṅgārāḥ kokilāḥ matāḥ // Rcūm_3.20 //
children.translated_text: Charcoal (<s>śikhitrā</s>) — the remnants of fire — the embers are called <s>kokilā</s>. // Rcūm 3.20 //
Those called <s>kokilā</s> are embers that have been extinguished without water.
{Cow-dung cake}

children.text: piṣṭakaṃ chagaṇaṃ chāṇamupalaṃ cotpalaṃ tathā // Rcūm_3.21 //
children.translated_text: Cake (<s>piṣṭaka</s>), cow-dung (<s>chagaṇa</s>), cow-dung chip (<s>chāṇa</s>), cow-dung cake (<s>upala</s>), and <s>utpala</s> — // Rcūm 3.21 //
also <s>karaṇḍa</s>, <s>upalasārī</s>, and dried cow-dung — these are synonyms.
{Bottle}

children.text: kūpikā champikā siddhā golā caiva karaṇḍikā // Rcūm_3.22 //
children.translated_text: Bottle (<s>kūpikā</s>), <s>champikā</s>, <s>siddhā</s>, <s>golā</s>, and <s>karaṇḍikā</s> — // Rcūm 3.22 //
{Cup}

children.text: caṣakā ca kaṭorī ca vāṭikā ghoṭikā tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Caṣaka</s>, <s>kaṭorī</s>, <s>vāṭikā</s>, <s>ghoṭikā</s>,

children.text: kacolī grāhikā ceti nāmānyekārthakāni hi // Rcūm_3.23 //
children.translated_text: <s>kacolī</s>, and <s>grāhikā</s> — these names are synonymous. // Rcūm 3.23 //
{What kind of physician should be employed in alchemical work?}
Physicians learned in alchemical texts (<s>rasasaṃhitā</s>), knowledgeable in lexicons (<s>nighaṇṭu</s>), and skilled in commentary,
knowing the languages of all regions — such practitioners should also be engaged. // Rcūm 3.24 //
Righteous, truthful, learned, a worshipper of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Keśava</s>,
compassionate, and with lotus-like hands — such a one should be employed in alchemical medicine. // Rcūm 3.25 //
One whose palm bears the marks of a banner, pot, lotus, fish, bow, and hook,
whose ring finger is lower than the others — he is said to possess the hand of immortality (<s>amṛtahasta</s>). // Rcūm 3.26 //
{Alchemist: disqualifying traits}
One without a preceptor, devoid of compassion, greedy, lacking in reasoning,
a physician whose hand has black lines — such a 'burnt-handed' one should be rejected. // Rcūm 3.27 //
At the conclusion of alchemical preparation, one should always recite the fierce mantra (<s>ghora</s>).
{Assistant}

children.text: sodyamāḥ śucayaḥ śūrāḥ baliṣṭhāḥ paricārakāḥ // Rcūm_3.28 //
children.translated_text: Diligent, pure, brave, and strong should be the attendants. // Rcūm 3.28 //
Those skilled in spirit-forms and mantras should be employed in the pursuit of treasure (<s>nidhisādhana</s>);
strong, courageous, red-eyed, and dark-bodied — // Rcūm 3.29 //
those versed in the science of frightening spirits should be employed in offering-rituals (<s>balisādhana</s>);
free from greed, truthful, worshippers of gods and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, // Rcūm 3.30 //
self-controlled and eating wholesome food — such should be employed in alchemical elixir-making (<s>rasāyana</s>);
wealthy, generous, and equipped with all requisite apparatus — // Rcūm 3.31 //
ever devoted to the guru's word — these are the auspicious ones in metallurgical transmutation (<s>dhātuvāda</s>).
{Collectors of drugs}
Those who know the names of all the respective medicines, who are pure and free from deceit, // Rcūm 3.32 //
knowing the languages of various regions — they are regarded as fit for collecting medicines.
For those who are pure, truthful, faithful, and wise, // Rcūm 3.33 //
whose minds are free from doubt — for them alone does mercury succeed, not otherwise.
When mercury is perfected through the eighteen processes, that practitioner is supreme. // Rcūm 3.34 //
Declaring 'This is the great mercury,' one should employ that mercury elsewhere;

children.text: rasasiddho bhavenmartyo dātā bhoktā na yācakaḥ /
children.translated_text: the mortal who has perfected mercury becomes a giver, an enjoyer, never a beggar,

children.text: jarāmukto jagatpūjyo divyakāntiḥ sadā sukhī // Rcūm_3.35 //
children.translated_text: freed from old age, worshipped by the world, of divine radiance, and ever happy. // Rcūm 3.35 //
<s>Rasendracūḍāmaṇi</s>, Chapter 4
<s>Somadeva</s> speaks for the awakening of ignorant physicians:

children.text: paribhāṣā rasendrasya śāstraiḥ siddhaiśca bhāṣitā // Rcūm_4.1 //
children.translated_text: the technical terminology of the lord of mercury (<s>rasendra</s>) as spoken in the treatises and by the <s>Siddhas</s>. // Rcūm 4.1 //
{The Dhanvantari share}

children.text: ardhaṃ siddharasasya tailaghṛtayorlehasya bhāgo'ṣṭamaḥ saṃsiddhākhilalohacūrṇavaṭakādīnāṃ tathā saptamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Half of the perfected mercury; one-eighth of oils, ghee, and electuaries; one-seventh of all perfected metal powders, pills, and the like —

children.text: yo dīyeta bhiṣagvarāya gadibhirnirdiśya dhanvantariṃ sarvārogyasukhāptaye nigadito bhāgaḥ sa dhānvantaraḥ // Rcūm_4.2 //
children.translated_text: that which is given by the patient to the best of physicians, invoking <s>Dhanvantari</s>, for the attainment of complete health and happiness, is called the <s>Dhānvantara</s> share. // Rcūm 4.2 //
{The Rudra share}
That one-eleventh portion of the cost of medicines purchased

children.text: vaṇigbhyo gṛhyate vaidyai rudrabhāgaḥ sa ucyate // Rcūm_4.3 //
children.translated_text: which is taken from merchants by physicians — that is called the <s>Rudra</s> share. // Rcūm 4.3 //
A greedy-minded physician who takes more than the <s>Rudra</s> share
and causes patients to receive improper medicine — he becomes a betrayer of trust. // Rcūm 4.4 //
In the scriptures, purification is prescribed even for one who has committed the killing of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>,

children.text: viśvāsaghātināṃ puṃsāṃ na śuddhirmaraṇaṃ vinā // Rcūm_4.5 //
children.translated_text: but for those who betray trust, there is no purification except death. // Rcūm 4.5 //
{<s>Kajjalī</s>}
Mercury ground with dry minerals such as sulphur and the like,
very smooth and having the appearance of collyrium — that is called <s>kajjalī</s>. // Rcūm 4.6 //

children.text: sadravā marditā saiva rasapaṅka iti smṛtaḥ // Rcūm_4.7 //
children.translated_text: The same when ground with liquids is known as <s>rasapaṅka</s> (mercury paste). // Rcūm 4.7 //

body.translated_text: {<s>Rasapaṅka</s> (mercury paste)}

children.translated_text: {Butter-like <s>piṣṭī</s>}
From mercury equal to the <s>arka</s> portion, and from sulphur equal to half a <s>niṣka</s>, grinding minutely in a mortar,

children.text: arkātape tīvratare sagharme piṣṭī bhavetsā navanītarūpā // Rcūm_4.8 //
children.translated_text: in intense sunlight with heat — a <s>piṣṭī</s> (paste) of butter-like form is produced. // Rcūm 4.8 //
{<s>Piṣṭī</s>}

children.text: khalve vimardya gandhena dugdhena saha pāradam /
children.translated_text: By grinding mercury with sulphur and milk in a mortar,

children.text: peṣaṇāt piṣṭatāṃ yāti sāpi piṣṭī matā paraiḥ // Rcūm_4.9 //
children.translated_text: through trituration it attains a paste-like state — that too is regarded as <s>piṣṭī</s> by others. // Rcūm 4.9 //
{<s>Pātana-piṣṭī</s> (distillation paste)}
A <s>piṣṭī</s> prepared with mercury and one-fourth part gold
becomes <s>pātana-piṣṭī</s> — it bestows the highest perfection upon mercury. // Rcūm 4.10 //
{<s>Kṛṣṭī</s> of gold and silver}
Silver or gold, struck with mercury, sulphur, and the like,

children.text: samutthitaṃ hi bahuśaḥ sā kṛṣṭī hematārayoḥ // Rcūm_4.11 //
children.translated_text: and repeatedly raised up — that is the <s>kṛṣṭī</s> of gold and silver. // Rcūm 4.11 //
{Gold <s>kṛṣṭī</s>}

children.text: kṛṣṭī kṣiptā suvarṇāntarna varṇo hīyate tayā /
children.translated_text: The <s>kṛṣṭī</s> when introduced into gold does not diminish its color;

children.text: svarṇakṛṣṭyā kṛtaṃ bījaṃ rasasya parirañjanam // Rcūm_4.12 //
children.translated_text: the seed made by the gold <s>kṛṣṭī</s> serves to tinge mercury. // Rcūm 4.12 //
{<s>Varalohaka</s> (superior alloy)}
Copper combined with <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (iron/steel), melted and immersed repeatedly
in a decoction of <s>lakuca</s> with sulphur — what emerges is <s>varalohaka</s> (superior alloy). // Rcūm 4.13 //
{Gold <s>raktī</s> (tincture)}
Gold tinged by that is called <s>svarṇa-raktī</s> (gold tincture);
when it is introduced into molten gold, it enhances the color,
and it also tinges silver and imparts color to seed-preparations. // Rcūm 4.14 //
{Silver <s>raktī</s>}
In the same manner, the beautiful silver <s>raktī</s> (tincture) should be prepared;

children.text: rañjanī khalu rūpyasya bījānāmapi rañjanī // Rcūm_4.15 //
children.translated_text: it tinges silver indeed, and also tinges seed-preparations. // Rcūm 4.15 //
{Leaf of moon and fire (<s>candrānala</s>)}

children.text: mṛtena vā baddharasena vānyallohena vā sādhitamanyaloham /
children.translated_text: A metal processed with either killed mercury or bound mercury, or with another metal,

children.text: sitatvapītatvamupāgataṃ taddalaṃ hi candrānalayoḥ prasiddham // Rcūm_4.16 //
children.translated_text: attaining whiteness or yellowness — that is well-known as the leaf (<s>dala</s>) of moon and fire. // Rcūm 4.16 //
{White and yellow leaf}
That which is joined with mercury bound by the semblance-method,

children.text: sādhitaṃ cānyalohena sitaṃ pītaṃ hi taddalam // Rcūm_4.17 //
children.translated_text: and processed with another metal — that leaf is white or yellow. // Rcūm 4.17 //
{<s>Ayonāga</s> (iron-lead alloy)}
<s>Kānta</s> (magnetic iron) struck with <s>tāpya</s> (pyrites), raised seven times,

children.text: śilayāpyāhataṃ nāgaṃ vāraṃ vāraṃ samutthitam // Rcūm_4.18 //
children.translated_text: and lead (<s>nāga</s>) struck with a stone, raised again and again — // Rcūm 4.18 //

children.text: tad dvayaṃ dvipalaṃ cātha tāpyabhasma paladvayam /
children.translated_text: those two, two <s>palas</s> each, and two <s>palas</s> of <s>tāpya</s> ash,

children.text: sarvaṃ nikṣipya mūṣāyāṃ saptavāraṃ dhamed dṛḍham // Rcūm_4.19 //
children.translated_text: all placed in a crucible and blown firmly seven times — // Rcūm 4.19 //
that is called <s>ayonāga</s>, efficacious for body and metals alike;

children.text: rasena sāraṇāyantre tadīyā guṭikā kṛtā // Rcūm_4.20 //
children.translated_text: with mercury, a pill is made from it in the <s>sāraṇā</s> apparatus. // Rcūm 4.20 //
Held in the mouth, it destroys the entire group of urinary diseases (<s>meha</s>),
produces firmness of teeth, and vision like that of a vulture,

children.text: tathānyān netrajān rogān rogān jatrūrdhvasambhavān // Rcūm_4.21 //
children.translated_text: as well as other eye diseases and diseases arising above the clavicle. // Rcūm 4.21 //
{<s>Śulbanāga</s> (copper-lead alloy)}
Copper struck with <s>mākṣika</s> (iron pyrites), raised ten times,
and likewise purified lead — those two together, four <s>palas</s> — // Rcūm 4.22 //
struck again with <s>nīlāñjana</s> (antimony) and raised seven times,
thus perfected — this is proclaimed as <s>śulbanāga</s> (copper-lead alloy). // Rcūm 4.23 //
Mercury processed with it, held in the mouth by people,
destroys the entire group of urinary diseases within a month. // Rcūm 4.24 //
With wholesome diet, within a year, grey hair along with wrinkles disappears,
vision becomes like a vulture's, radiant nourishment, and one becomes endowed with complete health. // Rcūm 4.25 //
{<s>Piñjarī</s>}

children.text: lohaṃ lohāntare kṣiptaṃ dhmātaṃ nirvāpitaṃ drave /
children.translated_text: A metal introduced into another metal, heated, and quenched in a liquid,
becoming pale-yellow in luster — that is called <s>piñjarī</s>. // Rcūm 4.26 //
{<s>Candrārka</s> (moon-sun alloy)}

children.text: bhāgāḥ ṣoḍaśa tārasya tathā dvādaśa bhāskaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Sixteen parts of silver and twelve parts of gold (<s>bhāskara</s>),
combined together — that is called <s>candrārka</s> (moon-sun alloy). // Rcūm 4.27 //
When another metal is introduced into the target metal through a curved tube,

children.text: nirvāpaṇaṃ tu yatproktaṃ vaidyairnirvāhaṇaṃ khalu // Rcūm_4.28 //
children.translated_text: that which is called <s>nirvāpaṇa</s> (quenching) is indeed known as <s>nirvāhaṇa</s> by physicians. // Rcūm 4.28 //

body.translated_text: {<s>Nirvāhaṇa</s> / <s>Nirvāpaṇa</s> (quenching/immersion)}

children.translated_text: The substance to be immersed (<s>nirvāhaṇa</s>) should be equal in quantity to the substance receiving it;

children.text: āvāpyaṃ vāpanīye ca bhāge diṣṭe ca diṣṭavat // Rcūm_4.29 //
children.translated_text: the substance to be added (<s>āvāpya</s>) should be in the prescribed proportion to the receiver. // Rcūm 4.29 //

children.text: mṛtaṃ tarati tattoye lohaṃ vāritaraṃ hi tat // Rcūm_4.30 //
children.translated_text: A killed (calcined) metal that floats on water — that is called <s>vāritara</s>. // Rcūm 4.30 //

body.translated_text: {<s>Vāritara</s> (water-floater)}

children.translated_text: {<s>Rekhāpūrṇa</s> (line-filler)}
That which, when rubbed between thumb and forefinger, enters the lines of the fingers —
a killed metal so described is designated by the name <s>rekhāpūrṇa</s>. // Rcūm 4.31 //
{<s>Apunarbhava</s> (irreversible)}
When combined with jaggery, <s>guñjā</s>, a pleasant-feeling substance, honey, and ghee,
it does not revert to its original form upon heating — that is called <s>apunarbhava</s> (irreversible). // Rcūm 4.32 //
{<s>Niruttha</s> (non-adhering)}

children.text: rūpyeṇa saha saṃyuktaṃ dhmātaṃ rūpyeṇa no laget /
children.translated_text: When combined with silver and heated, if it does not adhere to the silver,
then that irreversible metal is called <s>niruttha</s> (non-adhering). // Rcūm 4.33 //

children.text: evaṃ rūpyaṃ sanāgaṃ ced dhmātaṃ tāmre lagenna hi /
children.translated_text: Similarly, if silver with lead, when heated, does not adhere to copper,

children.text: tadā nirutthaṃ mantavyaṃ rañjanaṃ ca bhiṣagvaraiḥ // Rcūm_4.34 //
children.translated_text: then it should be considered <s>niruttha</s> by the best physicians, and suitable for tinging. // Rcūm 4.34 //
{Seed (<s>bīja</s>)}
When by a particular quenching process (<s>nirvāhaṇa</s>) a particular color is produced —
That which is soft and of variegated preparation is called its <s>bīja</s> (seed). [Rcūm 4.35]
{<s>Tāḍana</s> (striking)}
The destruction of one metal from two combined metals,
by blowing through a bamboo tube (<s>vaṅkanāla</s>), is called <s>tāḍana</s> (striking). [Rcūm 4.36]

body.translated_text: This indeed has been specified by physicians as the <s>uttaraṇa</s> (extraction process).

children.translated_text: {<s>Dhānyābhra</s> (grain-mica)}

children.text: cūrṇābhraṃ śālisaṃyuktaṃ vastre baddhaṃ tu kāñjike /
children.translated_text: Powdered mica mixed with rice, bound in a cloth and placed in sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>),
that which emerges from the cloth by rubbing is called <s>dhānyābhra</s> (grain-mica). [Rcūm 4.37]
{<s>Sattva</s> (essence)}
Combined with alkaline and acidic solvents and smelted in a mineral furnace (<s>ākarakoṣṭhaka</s>),
the essence that emerges therefrom is called <s>sattva</s> (metallic essence). [Rcūm 4.38]
{<s>Ekakoliśikha</s> (single charcoal peak)}
A furnace filled to the peak with charcoal pieces (<s>koliśa</s>) through the process of blowing,
reaching up to the neck of the crucible (<s>mūṣā</s>) — this is known as <s>ekakoliśikha</s>. [Rcūm 4.39]
{Charcoal (synonyms)}
<s>Śikhitrā</s>, <s>pāvakocchiṣṭā</s>, <s>mṛtāṅgāra</s>, and <s>kokilā</s>,
<s>kṛṣṇāṅga</s> and <s>koliśa</s> — these are mutual synonyms [for charcoal]. [Rcūm 4.40]

children.text: drāvaṇe sattvapāte ca mādhukāḥ khādirāḥ śubhāḥ /
children.translated_text: For melting and essence-extraction, <s>mādhuka</s> (mahua) and <s>khādira</s> (acacia) charcoals are excellent.

children.text: uddrāve vaṃśajāste tu svedane bādarāḥ śubhāḥ // Rcūm_4.41 //
children.translated_text: For sublimation, bamboo charcoals; for sudation (<s>svedana</s>), <s>bādara</s> (jujube) charcoals are excellent. [Rcūm 4.41]
{<s>Hiṅgulākṛṣṭa</s> (cinnabar-extracted)}
Mercury that is extracted from cinnabar placed in the apparatus called <s>Vidyādhara</s>, rubbed with ginger juice,

children.text: samākṛṣṭo raso yo'sau hiṅgulākṛṣṭa ucyate // Rcūm_4.42 //
children.translated_text: that mercury so extracted is called <s>hiṅgulākṛṣṭa</s> (cinnabar-extracted). [Rcūm 4.42]
{<s>Ghoṣākṛṣṭa</s> (bell-metal extracted)}
Bell-metal (<s>kāṃsya</s>) mixed with a small amount of palm toddy, struck with a bamboo tube,

children.text: muktavaṅgaṃ hi tattāmraṃ ghoṣākṛṣṭam udāhṛtam // Rcūm_4.43 //
children.translated_text: from which the tin is released — that copper is called <s>ghoṣākṛṣṭa</s> (bell-metal extracted). [Rcūm 4.43]
{<s>Guhyanāga</s> (secret lead)}
Twenty <s>palas</s> of purified lead, made into discs,
coated with orpiment ground with silver-plant milk. [Rcūm 4.44]
Sealing in a saucer-pair (<s>śarāvasampuṭa</s>), one should heat it with a <s>kroḍapuṭa</s> (pig-dung cake fire),
heating carefully so many times until it turns to ash. [Rcūm 4.45]
Rubbing that [ash] with jaggery, <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium), <s>guñjā</s> (rosary pea), ghee, and iron filings,
confining it in a crucible and then raising [the metal] by blowing. [Rcūm 4.46]
Again making it into discs, smearing with mercury of one <s>pala</s> weight,

children.text: liptvā limpetsitārkasya payasā śilayāpi ca // Rcūm_4.47 //
children.translated_text: one should coat it with the milk of white <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) plant and with orpiment. [Rcūm 4.47]
One should heat this with elephant-dung cakes (<s>gajapuṭa</s>) indeed twenty times.

children.text: puṭe puṭe hi nāgasya kuryādutthānaṃ khalu // Rcūm_4.48 //
children.translated_text: At each firing, one should perform the raising of the lead. [Rcūm 4.48]
One should quench it properly ten times with blue-flame liquids.

children.text: iti siddhaṃ tataḥ sīsaṃ karṣamātrāvaśeṣitam // Rcūm_4.49 //
children.translated_text: Thus perfected, the lead is reduced to one <s>karṣa</s> in weight. [Rcūm 4.49]
This is proclaimed by the name <s>guhyanāga</s> (secret lead), the finest <s>rasarasāyana</s> (mercurial elixir).
{<s>Guhyanāga</s>: capacity to consume gold}

children.text: niṣkamātre tu nāge 'smin lohakhāryāṃ drute sati // Rcūm_4.50 //
children.translated_text: When this lead of one <s>niṣka</s> weight is melted in a metal pot, [Rcūm 4.50]

children.text: svato lakṣaguṇāṃ haimīṃ śalākāṃ grasati dhruvam /
children.translated_text: it certainly consumes a gold rod a hundred-thousand times its own [weight].

children.text: kusumbhatailataptaṃ tat svarṇam udgariti dhruvam // Rcūm_4.51 //
children.translated_text: That gold, heated with safflower oil, certainly disgorges [the consumed substance]. [Rcūm 4.51]
This secret method has been taught by <s>Svacchandabhairava</s>.
{<s>Varanāga</s> (superior lead)}

children.text: tīkṣṇaṃ nīlāñjanopetaṃ dhmātaṃ hi bahuśo dṛḍham // Rcūm_4.52 //
children.translated_text: Lead combined with <s>nīlāñjana</s> (antimony/collyrium), smelted many times firmly, [Rcūm 4.52]
that which is soft, black, and melts readily is called <s>varanāga</s> (superior lead).
{<s>Utthāpana</s> (revivification, definition)}
The re-emergence of a dead [calcined metal] is called by the name <s>utthāpana</s> (revivification). [Rcūm 4.53]
{<s>Ḍhālana</s> (quenching)}
The casting of a molten substance into a liquid is considered <s>ḍhālana</s> (quenching).
{<s>Nāgasambhūtacapala</s> (lead-born mobile substance)}
Thirty <s>palas</s> of lead, rubbed with <s>bhānu</s> (sun-plant) milk, [Rcūm 4.54]
should be rubbed and calcined repeatedly until reduced to one <s>karṣa</s>.
This does not diminish even by a thousand firings. [Rcūm 4.55]
This mobile substance (<s>capala</s>) is described by the practitioners as born from lead.
{<s>Vaṅgasambhūtaś capalaḥ</s> (tin-born mobile substance)}

children.text: itthaṃ ca capalaḥ kāryo vaṅgasyāpi na saṃśayaḥ // Rcūm_4.56 //
children.translated_text: In the same way, a <s>capala</s> should be made from tin as well, without doubt. [Rcūm 4.56]
Mercury touched by the hand that has touched this [capala] becomes bound by itself alone.

children.text: sa raso dhātuvādeṣu śasyate na rasāyane // Rcūm_4.57 //
children.translated_text: Such mercury is praised in <s>dhātuvāda</s> (metallic transmutation) but not in <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation therapy). [Rcūm 4.57]
This has been declared by <s>Lokanātha</s> known as <s>Kharpaṇa</s>.
{<s>Capala</s>: preparation}
Fine powder of loadstone (<s>bhrāmakāśman</s>), combined with one-fifth [its weight of] mercury, [Rcūm 4.58]
should be rubbed for one day with the root-water of <s>kumārī</s> (aloe),
and for one day continuously with the juice of <s>cāṅgerī</s> (sorrel). [Rcūm 4.59]
Thus, one should rub for three days with <s>bhūnāga</s>-washed [liquid].
Then, with one <s>pala</s> of lead and an equal amount of tin, [Rcūm 4.60]
and ten <s>niṣkas</s> of the best mercury, one should prepare a smooth paste.
Having combined it with the paste, one should rub as before. [Rcūm 4.61]
Then, with the finest mercury and the essence of <s>rasaka</s> (calamine/zinc),

children.text: piṣṭīṃ kṛtvā tu pūrveṇa pūrvakalkena yojayet // Rcūm_4.62 //
children.translated_text: having made a paste, one should combine it with the previous paste. [Rcūm 4.62]
Kindling the fire, one should dry it with warm sour gruel.
With half a <s>pala</s> of purified tin and the juice of roasted <s>guñjā</s>, [Rcūm 4.63]
rubbing with sour gruel, one should make pills the size of peppercorns.

children.text: nirudhya vajramūṣāyāṃ saṃdhibandhaṃ vidhāya ca // Rcūm_4.64 //
children.translated_text: Confining them in a diamond-crucible (<s>vajramūṣā</s>) and sealing the joints, [Rcūm 4.64]
one should blow properly with bellows using nine [measures of] charcoal.

children.text: tato mūṣāgataṃ sattvaṃ samādāya samantataḥ // Rcūm_4.65 //
children.translated_text: Then, collecting the essence (<s>sattva</s>) that has entered the crucible from all sides, [Rcūm 4.65]
one should smelt it in an open crucible with a bamboo tube for purification.

children.text: daśaśāṇaṃ hi tatsattvaṃ bhasmanā lavaṇena ca // Rcūm_4.66 //
children.translated_text: That essence of ten <s>śāṇa</s> weight, with ash and salt, [Rcūm 4.66]
wrapping it with sour gruel, one should dry it by the <s>puṭa</s> (firing) method.
In two <s>niṣkas</s> of that [substance], with the ash described earlier, [Rcūm 4.67]
one should smelt eighty-fold lead and carry it through to completion.

children.text: iyatā pūrvasūto'sau jāryate na kathaṃcana // Rcūm_4.68 //
children.translated_text: By this much, the previously [described] mercury is digested — [it is] not [possible] otherwise. [Rcūm 4.68]
This <s>capala</s> (mobile substance) has been taught by <s>Lokanātha Śambhu</s>.

children.text: anenāpi rasaḥ śīghraṃ badhyate pūrvavat sukham // Rcūm_4.69 //
children.translated_text: By this too, mercury is quickly bound as before, easily. [Rcūm 4.69]
That [mercury], fired ten times with the powder of <s>kāravallī</s> (bitter gourd) roots,
becomes freed from lead and consumes [other metals] completely as <s>grāsa</s> (food). [Rcūm 4.70]
Its face [appearance] in the open crucible becomes of exceedingly superior quality.
This mercury, having digested its food, becomes a maker of <s>dehaloha</s> (body-metal).
This has been described by the illustrious <s>Somadeva</s> with great certainty. [Rcūm 4.71]
{<s>Dhauta</s> (washed)}
The impurity removed by washing with earthworm excrement-water,

children.text: kṛṣṇavarṇaṃ hi tatproktaṃ dhautākhyaṃ rasavādibhiḥ // Rcūm_4.72 //
children.translated_text: [the substance] which is black in color is called <s>dhauta</s> (washed) by the alchemists (<s>rasavādin</s>). [Rcūm 4.72]
{<s>Dvaṃdvana</s> (pairing/alloying)}
The fusion of two substances by smelting is called <s>dvaṃdvana</s> (alloying).
{[Unclear heading]}
The addition of a portion of silver or the like into gold or similar [metals]. [Rcūm 4.73]
{<s>Bhañjinī</s> (breaking agent)}
The reduction of color by [adding] parts [of another metal] is considered <s>bhañjinī</s> (breaking agent) by practitioners.
{<s>Pataṅgī</s> (moth-like transformation)}
The attainment of silver-ness or gold-ness in a metal through the application of <s>pataṅgī</s>-paste. [Rcūm 4.74]

body.text:
{palikā}
dināni katicit sthitvā yātyasau palikā matā /

children.translated_text: {<s>Pataṅgīrāga</s> (moth-like color)}
That which is colored from mercury or metal by smelting, and after a long time
comes out [fades away] — that is designated by the name <s>pataṅgīrāga</s> (transient color). [Rcūm 4.75]

body.translated_text:
{<s>Palikā</s> (transient color)}
That which remains for some days and then fades is considered <s>palikā</s> (transient color).

children.translated_text: {<s>Āvāpa</s>, <s>Pratīvāpa</s>, <s>Ācchādana</s> (addition, counter-addition, covering)}

children.text: drute dravyāntare kṣepo lohādyaiḥ kriyate hi yaḥ /
children.translated_text: The addition of metals and other substances into another substance while molten,

children.text: sa āvāpaḥ pratīvāpaḥ sa evācchādanaṃ matam // Rcūm_4.76 //
children.translated_text: that is <s>āvāpa</s> (addition); <s>pratīvāpa</s> (counter-addition) is the same as <s>ācchādana</s> (covering). [Rcūm 4.76]
{<s>Abhiṣeka</s> (sprinkling)}
When a metal standing in fire [is taken out] and after pausing for eight blinks of the eye,
the pouring of water [over it] — that is called <s>abhiṣeka</s> (sprinkling/annealing). [Rcūm 4.77]
{<s>Nirvāpa</s> (quenching)}

children.text: taptasyāpsu vinikṣepo nirvāpaḥ snapanaṃ ca tat /
children.translated_text: The casting of a heated [metal] into water is <s>nirvāpa</s> (quenching), also called <s>snapana</s> (bathing).
{Timing for <s>pratīvāpa</s> etc.}
The operations of <s>pratīvāpa</s> and so forth should be performed when the metal is molten and very pure. [Rcūm 4.78]
{<s>Śuddhāvarta</s> (pure turn)}
When the fire has bright flames accompanied by a white rising,

children.text: śuddhāvartastadā jñeyaḥ sa kālaḥ sattvanirgame // Rcūm_4.79 //
children.translated_text: that should be known as <s>śuddhāvarta</s> (pure turn) — that is the time for the emergence of the essence. [Rcūm 4.79]
{<s>Bījāvarta</s> (seed turn)}
When a flame resembling the substance to be melted is seen during blowing,

children.text: drāvasyonmukhatā seyaṃ bījāvartaḥ sa ucyate // Rcūm_4.80 //
children.translated_text: that is the readiness of the flux — this is called <s>bījāvarta</s> (seed turn). [Rcūm 4.80]
{<s>Svāṅgaśītala</s> (self-cooled)}
That which is cooled while still in the fire is called <s>svāṅgaśītala</s> (self-cooled).
{<s>Bahiḥśītala</s> (externally cooled)}
That which is removed from the fire and cooled is called <s>bahiḥśītala</s> (externally cooled). [Rcūm 4.81]
{<s>Svedana</s> (sudation)}
The heating of [a substance] placed in a <s>dolāyantra</s> (swing apparatus) with alkalis, acids, and herbs —
this is called <s>svedana</s> (sudation), which causes the loosening of impurities. [Rcūm 4.82]
{<s>Mardana</s> (grinding)}
Grinding with the specified herbs along with all acids and sour gruel —
this is called <s>mardana</s> (grinding), which destroys external impurities. [Rcūm 4.83]
{<s>Mūrchana</s> (fainting/solidification)}
That which causes the state of <s>naṣṭapiṣṭa</s> (destroyed-ground) by means of the medicines specified for grinding —
that is <s>mūrchana</s> (solidification), which destroys the coating [produced by] tin, minerals, and <s>bhūja</s> (birch). [Rcūm 4.84]
{<s>Naṣṭapiṣṭa</s> (destroyed and ground)}
That which brings about a ground state through the destruction of the [original] form —

children.text: vidvadbhirnirjitaḥ sūto naṣṭapiṣṭaḥ sa ucyate // Rcūm_4.85 //
children.translated_text: mercury so conquered by the learned is called <s>naṣṭapiṣṭa</s> (destroyed and ground). [Rcūm 4.85]
{<s>Utthāpana</s> (revivification)}
That which restores the [original] form through the application of heat, sunlight, and the like —
that is called <s>utthāpana</s> (revivification), which destroys the damage caused by <s>mūrchana</s> (solidification). [Rcūm 4.86]
{<s>Pātana</s> (distillation)}
The extraction of mercury — rubbed with the specified herbs — placed in an apparatus, upward, downward, or sideways,
is called by the name <s>pātana</s> (distillation), which destroys the coating caused by contact with tin and serpent [metals]. [Rcūm 4.87]
{<s>Rodhana</s> (restraining)}
The confinement of mercury combined with water and rock-salt for three days
in a pot — that which is its stabilization — is called <s>rodhana</s> (restraining). [Rcūm 4.88]
{<s>Niyamana</s> (controlling)}
For the cessation of the volatility of mercury that has gained potency through <s>rodhana</s>,

children.text: kriyate yo ghaṭe svedaḥ proktaṃ niyamanaṃ hi tat // Rcūm_4.89 //
children.translated_text: the sweating that is performed in a pot — that is called <s>niyamana</s> (controlling). [Rcūm 4.89]
{<s>Dīpana</s> (kindling/activating)}
Combined with minerals, stones, and roots, placed inside a pot,

children.text: grāsārthaṃ tridinaṃ svedo dīpanaṃ tanmataṃ budhaiḥ // Rcūm_4.90 //
children.translated_text: sweating for three days for the purpose of [enhancing its] consuming capacity — the wise consider that <s>dīpana</s> (activation). [Rcūm 4.90]
{<s>Grāsamāna</s> (dosage measure)}
The measure of the substance to be consumed (<s>grāsa</s>) proportionate to a given quantity of mercury —
the quantity that is specified — that is called <s>grāsamāna</s> (consumption measure). [Rcūm 4.91]
{<s>Jāraṇā</s> (digestion)}

children.text: grāsasya cāraṇaṃ garbhe drāvaṇaṃ jāraṇaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: The movement (<s>cāraṇa</s>) of the consumed substance within the body [of mercury], its dissolution (<s>drāvaṇa</s>), and digestion (<s>jāraṇa</s>) —

children.text: iti trirūpā nirdiṣṭā jāraṇā varavārttikaiḥ // Rcūm_4.92 //
children.translated_text: thus <s>jāraṇā</s> has been described in three forms by the excellent practitioners. [Rcūm 4.92]

children.text: grāsaḥ piṇḍaḥ parīṇāmaḥ tisraścākhyāḥ parāḥ smṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Grāsa</s> (consumption), <s>piṇḍa</s> (mass), and <s>parīṇāma</s> (transformation) — these three are considered the higher designations.

children.text: samukhā nirmukhā ceti jāraṇā dvividhā punaḥ // Rcūm_4.93 //
children.translated_text: <s>Samukhā</s> (with mouth) and <s>nirmukhā</s> (without mouth) — <s>jāraṇā</s> is again of two kinds. [Rcūm 4.93]
{<s>Jāraṇa</s>: <s>nirmukhajāraṇā</s> (mouthless digestion)}
<s>Nirmukhā jāraṇā</s> (mouthless digestion) is described as [proceeding] by the addition of <s>bīja</s> (seed) in portions.
{<s>Bīja</s> (seed, in the context of <s>jāraṇā</s>)}

children.text: śuddhaṃ svarṇaṃ ca rūpyaṃ ca bījamityabhidhīyate // Rcūm_4.94 //
children.translated_text: Purified gold and silver are called <s>bīja</s> (seed). [Rcūm 4.94]
The addition of <s>bīja</s> (seed) in a one-sixty-fourth portion is called <s>mukha</s> (mouth).
{<s>Samukharasa</s> (mercury with a mouth)}

children.text: evaṃ kṛte raso grāsalolupo mukhavānbhavet // Rcūm_4.95 //
children.translated_text: When done thus, mercury becomes desirous of consuming (<s>grāsa</s>) and possesses a mouth. [Rcūm 4.95]

body.translated_text: {<s>Mukha</s>/<s>samukhajāraṇā</s> (with-mouth digestion)}

children.translated_text: It becomes capable of devouring even hard metals.

children.text: iyaṃ hi samukhā proktā jāraṇā mṛgacāriṇā // Rcūm_4.96 //
children.translated_text: This is called <s>samukhā jāraṇā</s> (with-mouth digestion) by <s>Mṛgacārin</s> (the deer-wanderer). [Rcūm 4.96]
{<s>Rākṣasamukha</s> (demon-mouth)}
By the combination of divine herbs, placed in open furnaces,
[mercury] that devours all metals and the like — that possesses a demon-mouth (<s>rākṣasavaktra</s>). [Rcūm 4.97]
{<s>Cāraṇā</s> (impelling)}
The casting of consumed material into the mouth of mercury is considered <s>cāraṇā</s> (impelling).
{<s>Garbhadruti</s> (internal liquefaction)}
The liquefaction of the consumed [substance] within the body [of mercury] is called <s>garbhadruti</s> (internal liquefaction). [Rcūm 4.98]
{<s>Bāhyadruti</s> (external liquefaction)}
Liquefying externally the solid essence and the like

children.text: jāraṇāya rasendrasya sā bāhyā drutirucyate // Rcūm_4.99 //
children.translated_text: for the purpose of digestion by the king of mercury — that is called <s>bāhyadruti</s> (external liquefaction). [Rcūm 4.99]
{<s>Druti</s> (liquefied substance)}

children.text: nirlepatvaṃ dravatvaṃ ca tejastvaṃ laghutā tathā /
children.translated_text: Freedom from adhesion, fluidity, brilliance, and lightness,

children.text: drutaṃ yogaśca sūtena pañcadhā drutilakṣaṇam // Rcūm_4.100 //
children.translated_text: and union with mercury — these five are the characteristics of <s>druti</s> (the liquefied state). [Rcūm 4.100]
{<s>Druti</s> (process)}
By the application of rice-husk, grain, and the like, metals, minerals, and the like

children.text: saṃtiṣṭhate dravākāraṃ sā drutiḥ parikīrtitā // Rcūm_4.101 //
children.translated_text: always assume a liquid form — that is called <s>druti</s> (liquefaction). [Rcūm 4.101]
{<s>Jāraṇā</s> (digestion)}
The transformation of the liquefied consumed substance through the application of <s>viḍa</s>-apparatus and the like

children.text: jāraṇetyucyate tasyāḥ prakārāḥ santi koṭiśaḥ // Rcūm_4.102 //
children.translated_text: is called <s>jāraṇā</s> (digestion); its varieties are innumerable. [Rcūm 4.102]
{<s>Viḍa</s> (definition)}
With alkalis, acids, sulphur and the like, and with sharp urines,
for the purpose of digesting the bolus of mercury — that is designated as <s>viḍa</s> (auxiliary substance). // Rcūm 4.103 //
{<s>Rañjana</s> (tinging)}
By the assimilation (<s>jāraṇa</s>) of well-perfected seed, metals, and the like into mercury,
the production of yellow and other colors — that is designated as <s>rañjana</s> (tinging). // Rcūm 4.104 //
{<s>Sāraṇā</s> (streaming)}
The introduction of gold and other metals into mercury placed in an oil-apparatus,

children.text: vedhādhikyakaraṃ lohe sāraṇā sā prakīrtitā // Rcūm_4.105 //
children.translated_text: which increases its power of transmutation in metals — that is proclaimed as <s>sāraṇā</s> (streaming). // Rcūm 4.105 //
{<s>Vedha</s> (transmutation/penetration)}
Mercury, endowed with penetrating medicines, when introduced into a substance —

children.text: vedha ityucyate tajjñaiḥ sa cānekavidhaḥ smṛtaḥ // Rcūm_4.106 //
children.translated_text: that is called <s>vedha</s> (transmutation) by the experts; it is remembered to be of many kinds. // Rcūm 4.106 //
{Types of transmutation}
<s>Lepa</s> (smearing), <s>kṣepa</s> (throwing), <s>kunta</s> (piercing), <s>dhūma</s> (fumigation), and <s>śabda</s> (sound).
{Smearing transmutation}

children.text: lepena kurute lohaṃ svarṇaṃ vā rajataṃ tathā // Rcūm_4.107 //
children.translated_text: By smearing, one converts a metal into gold or silver. // Rcūm 4.107 //

children.text: lepavedhaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ puṭamatra ca saukaram /
children.translated_text: That is to be known as <s>lepavedha</s> (smearing transmutation); the <s>puṭa</s> (heating) here is of the mild (<s>saukara</s>) type.
{Throwing transmutation}

children.text: prakṣepaṇaṃ drute lohe vedhaḥ syāt kṣepasaṃjñitaḥ // Rcūm_4.108 //
children.translated_text: Casting into molten metal — that is the transmutation called <s>kṣepa</s> (throwing). // Rcūm 4.108 //
{Piercing transmutation}
The extraction of molten substance with mercury held in tongs,
producing conversion to gold and the like — that is called <s>kuntavedha</s> (piercing transmutation). // Rcūm 4.109 //
{Fumigation transmutation}
When mercury smokes inside a fire, from the fumes of the cast mercury,

children.text: svarṇādyāpādanaṃ lohe dhūmavedhaḥ sa ucyate // Rcūm_4.110 //
children.translated_text: the conversion of a metal to gold and the like — that is called <s>dhūmavedha</s> (fumigation transmutation). // Rcūm 4.110 //
{Sound transmutation}
By blowing a small quantity of metal with mercury held in the mouth,
producing conversion to gold or silver — that is proclaimed as <s>śabdavedha</s> (sound transmutation). // Rcūm 4.111 //
{<s>Udghāṭana</s> (revealing)}
The removal of turbidity and other defects from a substance transmuted by mercury,
and the revealing of its true color — that is called <s>udghāṭana</s> (revealing). // Rcūm 4.112 //
{<s>Svedana</s> (sweating/steaming)}
When mercury with alkalis, acids, and medicines is carefully sealed in a vessel
and buried in the ground — that is proclaimed as <s>svedana</s> (sweating). // Rcūm 4.113 //
{<s>Saṃnyāsa</s> (depositing)}
When mercury combined with medicines is carefully sealed in a vessel
and placed inside a constantly fire-fed furnace — that depositing is called <s>saṃnyāsa</s>. // Rcūm 4.114 //
{Virtues of sweating and depositing}
These two — sweating and depositing — are certain for the king of mercury;
they produce enhancement of qualities and rapid permeation. // Rcūm 4.115 //

children.text: rasanigamamahābdheḥ somadevaḥ samantātsphuṭataraparibhāṣā nāma ratnāni hṛtvā /
children.translated_text: <s>Somadeva</s>, from the great ocean of alchemical scriptures, having gathered from all sides the gems of most lucid technical terminology,

children.text: vyaracayadatiyatnāttair imāṃ kaṇṭhamālāṃ kalayati bhiṣagagryo maṇḍanārthaṃ sabhāyām // Rcūm_4.116 //
children.translated_text: has with great effort composed this necklace; may the foremost of physicians wear it for adornment in the assembly. // Rcūm 4.116 //
An alchemist who reads and studies this chapter,

children.text: rasakarmāṇi kurvāṇo na sa muhyati kutracit // Rcūm_4.117 //
children.translated_text: while performing alchemical operations, shall never be confused anywhere. // Rcūm 4.117 //
<s>Rasendracūḍāmaṇi</s>, Chapter 5
Now the apparatuses (<s>yantra</s>) of the alchemical science shall be described, many in number,
surveyed in brief by <s>Somadeva</s> at this time. // Rcūm 5.1 //
For the purpose of performing operations such as steaming and the like, by master practitioners,
mercury is controlled (<s>yantryate</s>) by means of them — hence they are called <s>yantra</s> (apparatus). // Rcūm 5.2 //
{<s>Dolāyantra</s> (swing apparatus)}
Tying mercury with medicines in a triple-layered cloth with <s>bhūrja</s> (birch-bark),

children.text: rasapoṭṭalikāṃ kāṣṭhe dṛḍhaṃ baddhvā guṇena hi // Rcūm_5.3 //
children.translated_text: binding the mercury-bundle firmly to a wooden stick with cord, // Rcūm 5.3 //
suspending it inside a pot filled with decoction, hanging freely,
one should kindle fire below, following the prescribed procedure in each case;

children.text: dolāyantramidaṃ proktaṃ svedanākhyaṃ tadeva hi // Rcūm_5.4 //
children.translated_text: this is described as the <s>dolāyantra</s> (swing apparatus), which is itself called the sweating apparatus. // Rcūm 5.4 //
{<s>Khalvayantra</s> (mortar apparatus)}
The mortar apparatus is said to be of three kinds, for grinding and other operations:
one is a non-porous stone mortar, another is made of metal. // Rcūm 5.5 //
{Half-moon shaped mortar}
Ten <s>aṅgulas</s> in height, with length equal to its fractions of <s>aṅgulas</s>,
nine <s>aṅgulas</s> in width, and depth measured by the same <s>aṅgulas</s> of mercury, // Rcūm 5.6 //
the neck two <s>aṅgulas</s> wide, very smooth, the trough of half-moon shape,

children.text: gharṣaścaiva daśāṅgulastu yadidaṃ khalvākhyayantraṃ smṛtam // Rcūm_5.7 //
children.translated_text: and the pestle ten <s>aṅgulas</s> — this is known as the mortar apparatus (<s>khalvayantra</s>). // Rcūm 5.7 //
In this, five <s>palas</s> of mercury should be ground for purification;
in other mortars, one should purify according to the appropriate proportion in each case. // Rcūm 5.8 //
{Round mortar}
The round mortar is twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> in width,
four <s>aṅgulas</s> deep, and very smoothly finished in the center. // Rcūm 5.9 //
The pestle is flat at the bottom and has a grip-handle on top.
{Heated mortar}

children.text: lauho navāṅgulaḥ khalvo nimnatvena ṣaḍaṅgulaḥ // Rcūm_5.10 //
children.translated_text: An iron mortar of nine <s>aṅgulas</s>, with a depth of six <s>aṅgulas</s>, // Rcūm 5.10 //
and a pestle of eight <s>aṅgulas</s> — this is called the heated mortar (<s>taptakhalva</s>);
having made a furnace in the shape of a mortar, it should be filled with charcoal. // Rcūm 5.11 //

children.text: tasyāṃ niveśitaṃ khalvaṃ pārśve bhastrikayā dhamet /
children.translated_text: The mortar placed in it, one should blow with bellows at the sides;
the <s>piṣṭī</s> (paste) ground therein, combined with alkalis and acids, // Rcūm 5.12 //
melts with great speed due to the steaming — there is no doubt about this;
if made of magnetic iron (<s>kānta</s>), it would be ten million times more effective. // Rcūm 5.13 //
{<s>Valabhīyantra</s> (gallery apparatus)}
In a metal vessel having two rings on its sides,
a similar but smaller vessel with a compartment attached to the ring, // Rcūm 5.14 //
placing it upon the larger vessel, in the smaller vessel one should deposit
the solidified mercury, filling the large vessel with sour gruel; // Rcūm 5.15 //
one should steam for two <s>yāmas</s> (six hours) thus, for the purpose of raising the mercury's quality;
this is the <s>valabhīyantra</s> (gallery apparatus), the cause of mercury's excellence. // Rcūm 5.16 //
In a fine vessel of magnetic iron, mercury becomes of superior quality.
{<s>Ūrdhvapātanayantra</s> (upward distillation apparatus)}

children.text: aṣṭāṅgulamitā samyak vartulā cipaṭī tale // Rcūm_5.17 //
children.translated_text: Properly measured at eight <s>aṅgulas</s>, round, with a flat bottom, // Rcūm 5.17 //
four <s>aṅgulas</s> below the neck, fitted with a trough
four <s>aṅgulas</s> wide and deep, firmly attached. // Rcūm 5.18 //
Its cover-pot at the base is sixteen <s>aṅgulas</s> in width,
fitted with a neck nine <s>aṅgulas</s> in extent. // Rcūm 5.19 //

children.text: pūrvaghaṭyāṃ rasaṃ kṣiptvā nyubjāṃ dadyāt parāṃ ghaṭīm /
children.translated_text: Having placed mercury in the first pot, one should invert the second pot over it,

children.text: sordhvaṃ nimnaṃ ca parito dṛḍhapālikayānvitām // Rcūm_5.20 //
children.translated_text: facing upward with a depression around it, fitted with a firm rim. // Rcūm 5.20 //
One should pour water into the rim-trough and kindle fire below;
this upward distillation apparatus is proclaimed by <s>Nandin</s>. // Rcūm 5.21 //
{<s>Adhaḥpātanayantra</s> (downward distillation apparatus)}
Upon the upper pan one should place another pan face-down,
a pan with a flat bottom, its interior smeared with mercury. // Rcūm 5.22 //

children.text: kṣiptvā tāṃ paṅkile garte jvālayenmūrdhni pāvakam /
children.translated_text: Having placed it in a muddy pit, one should kindle fire on top;
that is described as the downward distillation apparatus. // Rcūm 5.23 //
{<s>Tiryakpātanayantra</s> (lateral distillation apparatus)}
One should place mercury in a pot equipped with a long downward-slanting tube,
and insert that tube into the interior of another pot. // Rcūm 5.24 //
Having sealed the mouths of both pots properly with clay,
one should kindle a fierce fire below the mercury pot. // Rcūm 5.25 //

children.text: itarasmin ghaṭe toyaṃ prakṣipet svādu śītalam /
children.translated_text: In the other pot, one should pour sweet, cool water;
this is called the lateral distillation apparatus by the practitioners. // Rcūm 5.26 //
{Distillation apparatuses: their use}
Three types of distillation have been described — truly three apparatuses;

children.text: pātanaiśca vinā sūto na tarāṃ doṣamujhati // Rcūm_5.27 //
children.translated_text: without distillation, mercury does not readily shed its defects. // Rcūm 5.27 //
Why is it not freed from defects by upward distillation alone, repeated three times?

children.text: vibhāgena vipāke tu dravyeṇānyena yogataḥ // Rcūm_5.28 //
children.translated_text: Because by division in processing, with different substances in combination, // Rcūm 5.28 //
and by transfer to different vessels, diverse qualities are indeed produced;
just as rice is freed from impurities by means of fragments, mortar, and water. // Rcūm 5.29 //
By distillation alone, great purification is proclaimed by <s>Nandin</s>.
{<s>Kacchapayantra</s> (tortoise apparatus)}
In a wide-mouthed vessel filled with water, one should place // Rcūm 5.30 //

children.text: kharparaṃ pṛthukaṃ samyak prasare tasya madhyame /
children.translated_text: a broad shallow dish properly in the middle of the surface;

children.text: ālavālaṃ viḍaiḥ kṛtvā tanmadhye pāradaṃ kṣipet // Rcūm_5.31 //
children.translated_text: making a basin with auxiliary substances (<s>viḍa</s>), one should place mercury in its center. // Rcūm 5.31 //
Having placed auxiliary substance above and below, sealing carefully with a lid,
a <s>puṭa</s> (heating) of appropriate type should be given — that is prescribed. // Rcūm 5.32 //
This is indeed the apparatus called <s>kacchapa</s> (tortoise); it is used in the assimilation (<s>jāraṇa</s>) of mercury.
{<s>Antarālikayantra</s> (intermediate apparatus)}
Having made a metal crucible in the shape of an eggplant (<s>vṛntāka</s>), // Rcūm 5.33 //
measured at one <s>vitasti</s> (span), constructed of magnetic iron,
or made of wrought iron — two <s>aṅgulas</s> below the neck, below that, // Rcūm 5.34 //
one should provide a ring of two <s>aṅgulas</s>, from the neck at the middle portion,
a bracelet broad as a tamarind leaf to hold the cover. // Rcūm 5.35 //
A cover fitted inside with a knob, with tight joints,

children.text: tale pravihitacchidraṃ bhāṇḍaṃ kṛtvā hy adhomukham // Rcūm_5.36 //
children.translated_text: a vessel with a hole made at the bottom, placed inverted — // Rcūm 5.36 //

children.text: tatraināṃ lambayenmūrdhni nirudhya ca viśoṣya ca /
children.translated_text: one should suspend it therein at the top, seal and dry it,
then give the neck of the pan a fire-producing <s>puṭa</s> (heating). // Rcūm 5.37 //
Such is the form of the apparatus called <s>antarālika</s> (intermediate);
with this one should perform the melting of sulphur and internal melting. // Rcūm 5.38 //
{<s>Tāpikāyantra</s> (heating apparatus)}

children.text: tāpīṃ mūṣāṃ mṛdā kṛtvā dṛḍhāṃ cāratnimātrikām /
children.translated_text: Having made a firm clay crucible (<s>tāpī mūṣā</s>) measuring one cubit,
very firm and fitted with a two-<s>aṅgula</s> hole in the middle, // Rcūm 5.39 //
one should place a magnetic iron pan above the sulphur,
and fill the heating apparatus all around with clean sand. // Rcūm 5.40 //

children.text: tāṃ ca cullyāṃ samāropya kṣepaṃ kṣepaṃ viḍadravam /
children.translated_text: Having placed it on the furnace, adding auxiliary liquid portion by portion,
one should kindle the fire with a flame the size of a big toe. // Rcūm 5.41 //
One should assimilate all metals, mica, and the like into mercury;
this is called the <s>tāpikāyantra</s> (heating apparatus), easy to use in mercury assimilation. // Rcūm 5.42 //
{<s>Pratigarbhayantra</s> (counter-womb apparatus)}

children.text: sthālyāṃ vinikṣipya rasādi vastu svarṇādi khāryā prapidhāya bhūyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having placed mercury and other substances in a pan, covering with a metal dish containing gold and the like,

children.text: amlena cordhve lavaṇādi vastu cullyāṃ pacettat pratigarbhayantram // Rcūm_5.43 //
children.translated_text: and acid above with salt and other substances, one should cook it on a furnace — that is the <s>pratigarbhayantra</s>. // Rcūm 5.43 //
{<s>Garbhayantra</s> (womb apparatus)}
One should carefully seal a metal dish inside a lid-vessel;

children.text: sthālyāṃ mṛdo'thavā khāryāṃ kṣiptvā vastu nirudhya ca // Rcūm_5.44 //
children.translated_text: having placed the substance in a pan or metal dish and sealed it, // Rcūm 5.44 //
having added acid and the like and sealed — the cooking takes place in the <s>garbhayantra</s> (womb apparatus).
{<s>Pālikāyantra</s> (pan apparatus)}
A round iron cup with an upward rod at its bent top — // Rcūm 5.45 //
this is the <s>pālikāyantra</s> (pan apparatus), for the purpose of assimilating offerings.
{<s>Ghaṭayantra</s> (pot apparatus)}
Holding four <s>prasthas</s> of water, with a mouth of four <s>aṅgulas</s> — // Rcūm 5.46 //
that is described as the <s>ghaṭayantra</s> (pot apparatus); it is regarded as useful for the saturation process.
{<s>Iṣṭikāyantra</s> (brick apparatus)}

children.text: vidhāya vartulaṃ gartaṃ mallamatra nidhāya ca // Rcūm_5.47 //
children.translated_text: Having made a round pit and placing a lid-vessel in it, // Rcūm 5.47 //
one should place a brick therein, a fine one with a cavity in the middle,
and make a rim one <s>aṅgula</s> high around the pit. // Rcūm 5.48 //

children.text: garte sūtaṃ vinikṣipya gartāsye vasanaṃ kṣipet /
children.translated_text: Having placed mercury in the cavity and cloth over the cavity's mouth,

children.text: nikṣipya gandhakaṃ tatra mallenāsyaṃ nirudhya ca // Rcūm_5.49 //
children.translated_text: having placed sulphur thereon and sealed the mouth with a lid, // Rcūm 5.49 //
having properly sealed between lid and rim with clay,

children.text: vanopalaiḥ puṭaṃ deyaṃ kapotākhyaṃ na cādhikam // Rcūm_5.50 //
children.translated_text: a mild <s>puṭa</s> called <s>kapota</s> (dove) should be given, and no more. // Rcūm 5.50 //
This is indeed the brick apparatus; with it one should assimilate sulphur.
{<s>Vidyādharayantra</s> (knowledge-holder apparatus)}

children.text: sthālikopari vinyasya sthālīṃ samyaṅnirudhya ca // Rcūm_5.51 //
children.translated_text: Having placed a pan upon a pan and properly sealing, // Rcūm 5.51 //
having poured water into the upper pan, one should kindle fire below;
this is the <s>vidyādhara</s> apparatus, for the purpose of extracting cinnabar (<s>hiṅgula</s>). // Rcūm 5.52 //
{<s>Ḍamaruyantra</s> (drum apparatus)}

children.text: yatra sthālyupari sthālīṃ nyubjāṃ dattvā nirudhya ca /
children.translated_text: Where a pan is placed inverted upon another pan and sealed —
that apparatus called <s>ḍamaruka</s> (drum) is useful for making mercury ash (<s>rasabhasma</s>). // Rcūm 5.53 //
{<s>Nābhiyantra</s> (navel apparatus)}
In the middle of the <s>malla</s> (cup-crucible), one should make a pit; therein [place] mercury with sulphur.

children.text: gartasya paritaḥ kuḍyaṃ prakuryād dvyaṅgulocchrayam // Rcūm_5.54 //
children.translated_text: Around the pit, one should make a wall two fingers high. // Rcūm 5.54 //
Then one should cover it properly with a cow-teat-shaped crucible (<s>gostanākāramūṣā</s>),
sealing well with water-clay, with the height equal to the pit. // Rcūm 5.55 //
Then, pouring in water, one should kindle fire below —
this is called the navel-apparatus (<s>nābhiyantra</s>), declared by <s>Nandin</s>, the all-knowing. // Rcūm 5.56 //
By this [apparatus], mercury is digested; smokeless, pure sulphur [is obtained].
{Water-clay (<s>toyamṛttikā</s>)}
Kneaded like a paste with <s>barbūra</s> (Clerodendrum) decoction, // Rcūm 5.57 //
the fine powder of consumed slag, combined with jaggery powder —

children.text: iyaṃ hi jalamṛtproktā durbhedyā salilaiḥ khalu // Rcūm_5.58 //
children.translated_text: this is called water-clay (<s>jalamṛt</s>), indeed impervious to liquids. // Rcūm 5.58 //
{Fire-clay (<s>vahnimṛtsnā</s>)}
With chalk (<s>khaṭikā</s>), alum (<s>paṭu</s>), and slag (<s>kiṭṭa</s>), kneaded with buffalo milk —
fire-clay is produced, truly able to withstand fierce heat of fire. // Rcūm 5.59 //

children.text: etayā mṛtsnayā ruddho na gantuṃ kṣamate rasaḥ /
children.translated_text: Mercury sealed with this clay is unable to escape,
like a man bound by the mature love of a sophisticated woman. // Rcūm 5.60 //
<s>Nandin</s>, <s>Nāgārjuna</s>, and <s>Brahmajyoti</s> the lord of sages —
and the revered <s>Somadeva</s> know [this]; no other [knows it] on the surface of the earth. // Rcūm 5.61 //
{Swallowing-apparatus (<s>grastayantra</s>)}
A crucible placed inside another crucible, uniformly round from end to end,

children.text: cipiṭāṃ ca tale proktaṃ grastayantraṃ manīṣibhiḥ // Rcūm_5.62 //
children.translated_text: and flat at the bottom — this is called the swallowing-apparatus (<s>grastayantra</s>) by the wise. // Rcūm 5.62 //
It is prescribed by the knowers of mercury for the purpose of binding mercury (<s>sūtendrabandha</s>).
{Balance-apparatus (<s>tulāyantra</s>)}

children.text: vṛntākākāramūṣe dve tayoḥ kaṇṭhādadhaḥ khalu // Rcūm_5.63 //
children.translated_text: Two brinjal-shaped crucibles; below the neck of each, // Rcūm 5.63 //
a tube one span in length, with joints well-sealed with clay —

children.text: tatraikasyāṃ kṣipet sūtam anyasyāṃ gandhacūrṇakam // Rcūm_5.64 //
children.translated_text: in one [crucible] one should place mercury, in the other, sulphur powder. // Rcūm 5.64 //
Sealing the mouths of both crucibles and placing them in a sand-bath apparatus,
one should kindle fire below — this is called the balance-apparatus (<s>tulāyantra</s>). // Rcūm 5.65 //
It is proclaimed for the digestion (<s>jāraṇā</s>) of realgar (<s>śilā</s>), orpiment (<s>tālaka</s>), and sulphur (<s>gandhāśma</s>).
{Pot-apparatus (<s>sthālīyantra</s>)}

children.text: sthālyāṃ tāmrādi nikṣipya mallenāsyaṃ nirudhya ca // Rcūm_5.66 //
children.translated_text: Having placed copper etc. in a pot and sealed the mouth with a cup-crucible (<s>malla</s>), // Rcūm 5.66 //
what is cooked while placed in the pot — that is called the pot-apparatus (<s>sthālīyantra</s>).
{Chamber-apparatus (<s>koṣṭhikāyantra</s>)}
Inside a large vessel, one should place fine sand // Rcūm 5.67 //
to a height of one <s>vitasti</s> (span); then therein one should set
an unfired earthen chamber (<s>koṣṭhī</s>), twelve fingers in height, // Rcūm 5.68 //
six fingers in width, made very smooth in the middle,
with a lid five fingers [wide], having a sharp-pointed crown shape. // Rcūm 5.69 //

children.text: na nyūnā nādhikā koṣṭhī kaṇṭhato masṛṇā bahiḥ /
children.translated_text: The chamber should be neither too small nor too large, smooth outside from the neck;

children.text: koṣṭhyāṃ ca nikṣipedgandhaṃ ṣaṭpalaṃ ślakṣṇacūrṇitam // Rcūm_5.70 //
children.translated_text: in the chamber, one should place six <s>palas</s> of sulphur, finely powdered. // Rcūm 5.70 //
Then, placing an iron tripod and making it steady,

children.text: tasyāṃ ca vinyaset khārīṃ lauhīṃ vā kāntalohajām // Rcūm_5.71 //
children.translated_text: upon it one should set an iron pan (<s>khārī</s>) or one made of lodestone (<s>kāntalohajā</s>). // Rcūm 5.71 //
Therein one should place twenty <s>palas</s> of purified mercury,
and the mercury with digested sulphur should be treated with garlic juices. // Rcūm 5.72 //
Covering with the aforementioned lid, inverted,
one should seal the joint with lime-clay-jaggery mixture. // Rcūm 5.73 //
When the joint-seal has dried, one should place sand on top;
sealing the vessel's mouth, one should then kindle fire below. // Rcūm 5.74 //
Intensely, for three <s>yāmas</s> (nine hours); then the sulphur-born [vapour],
the smoke adhering to the lid, melting, falls down onto the mercury. // Rcūm 5.75 //

children.text: evaṃ hi ṣaḍguṇaṃ gandhaṃ bhuktvā sūto guṇī bhavet /
children.translated_text: Thus, having consumed six times [its weight of] sulphur, the mercury becomes endowed with qualities,
producing all the superior qualities prescribed by the treatise. // Rcūm 5.76 //
This chamber-apparatus (<s>koṣṭhikāyantra</s>) was proclaimed by <s>Nandin</s>.
{Sand-bath apparatus (<s>vālukāyantra</s>)}
Having carefully placed [the material] in a vessel filled to five-eighths with sand, // Rcūm 5.77 //
what is cooked — mercury pills etc. — that is called the sand-bath apparatus (<s>vālukāyantra</s>).
{Salt-apparatus (<s>lavaṇayantra</s>)}
Similarly, by filling with salt, the salt-apparatus (<s>lavaṇayantrakam</s>) is declared. // Rcūm 5.78 //
{Fumigation-apparatus (<s>dhūpayantra</s>)}
One should make an iron vessel eight fingers [in diameter] and eight fingers in height;

children.text: kaṇṭhādho dvyaṅgule deśe jalādhāraṃ hi tatra ca // Rcūm_5.79 //
children.translated_text: two fingers below the neck, there should be a water-reservoir. // Rcūm 5.79 //
Thin iron rods should be placed horizontally across it;
thin gold leaves should be placed upon them. // Rcūm 5.80 //
Below the vessel, one should place the fumigant to be described here;
that vessel should be covered with another inverted vessel. // Rcūm 5.81 //

children.text: mṛdā vilipya saṃdhiṃ ca vahniṃ prajvālayedadhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Sealing the joint with clay, one should kindle fire below;
by this, gold leaves are blackened, processed by the prescribed method. // Rcūm 5.82 //
Mercury moves with force — both the flux (<s>druti</s>) and the inner flux (<s>garbhadruti</s>);

children.text: gandhālakaśilānāṃ hi kajjalyā vā mṛtāhinā // Rcūm_5.83 //
children.translated_text: of sulphur, orpiment, realgar — using black collyrium (<s>kajjalī</s>) or killed tin — // Rcūm 5.83 //
the fumigation of gold leaves is proclaimed as supreme.
For silver purposes, silver leaves should be fumigated with killed tin. // Rcūm 5.84 //
One should also fumigate with appropriate mercurial and semi-metallic preparations;
this is called the fumigation-apparatus (<s>dhūpayantra</s>), used for conveying digestive substances. // Rcūm 5.85 //
{Ball-apparatus (<s>kuṇḍakayantra</s> = <s>kandukayantra</s>)}

children.text: sthūlasthālyāṃ dravaṃ kṣiptvā vāso baddhvā mukhe dṛḍham /
children.translated_text: Having placed liquid in a large pot and tying cloth firmly over the mouth,

children.text: tatra svedyaṃ vinikṣipya pidhānyā prapidhāya ca // Rcūm_5.86 //
children.translated_text: placing the substance to be steamed therein and covering with another lid, // Rcūm 5.86 //
one should kindle fire below — that is the ball-apparatus (<s>kuṇḍakayantrakam</s>);
other wise men call this the steaming apparatus (<s>svedanayantra</s>). // Rcūm 5.87 //
{Pot-apparatus, second type (<s>kuṇḍayantra</s> (2))}

children.text: yadvā sthālyāṃ jalaṃ kṣiptvā tṛṇaṃ dattvā mukhopari /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, having placed water in a pot and placing straw over the mouth,

children.text: svedyadravyaṃ vinikṣipya pidhānyā prapidhāya ca // Rcūm_5.88 //
children.translated_text: placing the substance to be steamed and covering with another lid, // Rcūm 5.88 //
one should kindle fire below — this too is a pot-apparatus (<s>kuṇḍayantrakam</s>).
{Distillation-apparatus (<s>ḍekīyantra</s>)}
In an opening below the neck of the vessel, one should insert a bamboo tube; // Rcūm 5.89 //
placing a pair of bronze vessels in a sealed pair containing water,

children.text: nālāsyaṃ tatra saṃyojya dṛḍhaṃ taccāpi kārayet // Rcūm_5.90 //
children.translated_text: joining the tube's opening thereto, one should make it firm. // Rcūm 5.90 //
Mercury previously placed in the pot with the prescribed substances,

children.text: agninā tāpito nālāt toye tasmin patatyadhaḥ // Rcūm_5.91 //
children.translated_text: heated by fire, falls through the tube into the water below. // Rcūm 5.91 //
When the entire contents of the vessel become hot,

children.text: jāyate rasasaṃdhānaṃ ḍhekīyantram idaṃ bhavet // Rcūm_5.92 //
children.translated_text: a consolidation of mercury occurs — this is the distillation-apparatus (<s>ḍhekīyantra</s>). // Rcūm 5.92 //
{Fire-and-water apparatus (<s>somānalayantra</s>)}

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ vahnir adhaścāpo madhye tu rasasaṃgrahaḥ /
children.translated_text: Fire above, water below, and collection of mercury in the middle —

children.text: somānalam idaṃ proktaṃ jārayed gaganādikam // Rcūm_5.93 //
children.translated_text: this is called the fire-and-water [apparatus] (<s>somānala</s>); it digests mica (<s>gagana</s>) and other [substances]. // Rcūm 5.93 //
{Tube-apparatus (<s>nālikāyantra</s>)}
Mercury placed in an iron tube, in a vessel filled with salt,
sealed and cooked by the wise — that is called the tube-apparatus (<s>nālikāyantra</s>). // Rcūm 5.94 //
{Crucible (<s>mūṣā</s>)}
Now the clay called crucible (<s>mūṣā</s>) — its form is of various shapes;
its proper application is described by <s>Somadeva</s>. // Rcūm 5.95 //
{Crucible: synonyms}

children.text: mūṣā hi koṣṭhikā proktā kumudī karahārikā /
children.translated_text: The crucible (<s>mūṣā</s>) is also called <s>koṣṭhikā</s>, <s>kumudī</s>, <s>karahārikā</s>,

children.text: pātanī vahnimitrā ca rasavādibhir īryate // Rcūm_5.96 //
children.translated_text: <s>pātanī</s>, and <s>vahnimitrā</s> — so declared by the practitioners of alchemy (<s>rasavādin</s>). // Rcūm 5.96 //
{Crucible: etymology (<s>nirukti</s>)}
That which steals (<s>muṣṇāti</s>) defects — that is called <s>mūṣā</s> (crucible);

children.text: upādānaṃ bhavettasyā mṛttikā lohameva ca // Rcūm_5.97 //
children.translated_text: its material is either clay or metal. // Rcūm 5.97 //
Better is even a single <s>kākiṇī</s> (small coin) extracted from the crucible's mouth
than a hundred thousand [obtained by] bowing to vile people — fie upon the proud! // Rcūm 5.98 //
{Joint-sealing (<s>saṃdhilepa</s>)}
The binding of crucible and lid, the sealing — that is the joint-sealing (<s>saṃdhilepanam</s>);

children.text: andhraṇaṃ randhraṇaṃ caiva saṃśliṣṭaṃ saṃdhibandhanam // Rcūm_5.99 //
children.translated_text: <s>andhraṇa</s>, <s>randhraṇa</s>, <s>saṃśliṣṭa</s>, and <s>saṃdhibandhanam</s> [are its synonyms]. // Rcūm 5.99 //
{Clay: <s>śarkarā</s> (gritty clay)}
White, coarse clay — <s>śarkarā</s> (gritty clay) is reddish-white;
it withstands prolonged blowing [of bellows] and is highly recommended for crucible-making.

children.text: tadabhāve ca vālmīkī kaulālī samudīryate // Rcūm_5.100 //
children.translated_text: In its absence, anthill clay (<s>vālmīkī</s>) or potter's clay (<s>kaulālī</s>) is prescribed. // Rcūm 5.100 //

children.text: yā mṛttikā dagdhatuṣaiḥ śaṇena śikhitrakairvā hayaladdinā ca /
children.translated_text: Clay mixed with burnt husks, hemp (<s>śaṇa</s>), peacock feathers (<s>śikhitraka</s>), or horse-dung (<s>hayaladdinā</s>),

children.text: lauhena daṇḍena ca kuṭṭitā sā sādhāraṇā syātkhalu mūṣikārthe // Rcūm_5.101 //
children.translated_text: and pounded with an iron rod — that is the ordinary [clay] for crucible-making. // Rcūm 5.101 //
White stone, burnt husks, peacock feathers, hemp rags,

children.text: laddiḥ kiṭṭaṃ yathāyogyaṃ saṃyojyā mūṣikāmṛdi // Rcūm_5.102 //
children.translated_text: dung, and slag — combined as appropriate in the crucible clay. // Rcūm 5.102 //
{Diamond-crucible (<s>vajramūṣā</s>)}
Three parts clay, one part each of hemp and dung, and one part of burnt husks and stone,

children.text: kiṭṭārdhabhāgaṃ parikhaṇḍya vajramūṣāṃ vidadhyātkhalu sattvapāte // Rcūm_5.103 //
children.translated_text: and half a part of slag — cutting [and mixing thus], one should make a diamond-crucible for metal extraction. // Rcūm 5.103 //
{Combination-crucible (<s>yogamūṣā</s>)}
Clay from an anthill, mixed with burnt charcoal-husks,
combined with the appropriate <s>viḍa</s> (alkali flux) and smeared with the appropriate <s>viḍa</s> — // Rcūm 5.104 //

children.text: tayā yā vihitā mūṣā yogamūṣeti kathyate /
children.translated_text: a crucible made from that is called the combination-crucible (<s>yogamūṣā</s>);

children.text: anayā sādhitaḥ sūto jāyate guṇavattaraḥ // Rcūm_5.105 //
children.translated_text: mercury processed in it becomes of superior quality. // Rcūm 5.105 //
{Diamond-melting crucible (<s>vajradrāvaṇamūṣā</s>)}
With equal [parts of] calcined calcium (<s>gāra</s>), earth, lead (<s>nāga</s>), and gold (<s>dhauta</s>), hemp, and burnt husks,

children.text: samaiḥ samā ca mūṣā mṛnmahiṣīdugdhamarditā // Rcūm_5.106 //
children.translated_text: the clay [is made], equal [in parts], kneaded with buffalo milk. // Rcūm 5.106 //
Fermented for a fortnight and turned over many times —
a crucible made from that is called the diamond-melting [crucible] (<s>vajradrāvaṇī</s>). // Rcūm 5.107 //
{Calcium-crucible (<s>gāramūṣā</s>)}
Enriched with six times [its weight of] burnt calcium (<s>gāra</s>), with slag, charcoal, and hemp,
a crucible made from black clay is called the calcium-crucible (<s>gāramūṣā</s>). // Rcūm 5.108 //
Even with blowing for two <s>yāmas</s> (six hours), it does not melt by fire.
{Best-crucible (<s>varamūṣā</s>)}
Cloth, charcoal, and husks in equal [parts], and four times that [amount of] clay, // Rcūm 5.109 //
and calcium equal to the clay — all kneaded together,

children.text: varamūṣeti nirdiṣṭā yāmaṃ vahniṃ saheta ca // Rcūm_5.110 //
children.translated_text: that is designated as the best-crucible (<s>varamūṣā</s>); it withstands fire for one <s>yāma</s> (three hours). // Rcūm 5.110 //
{Color-crucible (<s>varṇamūṣā</s>)}
Combined with the powder of the red group [of substances], treated with the liquid of the red group,

children.text: mṛt tayā lepitā mūṣā kṣitikhecaralepitā // Rcūm_5.111 //
children.translated_text: clay smeared therewith, [and] the crucible coated with land-and-sky [substances] — // Rcūm 5.111 //
that is called the color-crucible (<s>varṇamūṣā</s>); it is employed for enhancing color.
{Silver-crucible (<s>rūpyamūṣā</s>)}

children.text: evaṃ hi śvetavargeṇa rūpyamūṣā prakīrtitā // Rcūm_5.112 //
children.translated_text: Similarly, with the white group [of substances], the silver-crucible (<s>rūpyamūṣā</s>) is proclaimed. // Rcūm 5.112 //
{Alkali-crucible (<s>viḍamūṣā</s>)}
Made from clay mixed with the appropriate <s>viḍa</s> (alkali flux), smeared with the appropriate <s>viḍa</s> —
for the purpose of body-metal processing (<s>dehalohārtha</s>), it is called the alkali-crucible (<s>viḍamūṣā</s>). // Rcūm 5.113 //
{Diamond-melting crucible, second type (<s>vajradrāvaṇamūṣā</s> (II))}
With calcined calcium, earth, lead, and gold, husks, ashes, and hemp,

children.text: samaiḥ samā ca mūṣā mṛnmahiṣīdugdhamarditā // Rcūm_5.114 //
children.translated_text: the clay [is made], equal [in parts], kneaded with buffalo milk. // Rcūm 5.114 //
Fermented for a fortnight and turned over many times —

children.text: tayā viracitā mūṣā liptā matkuṇaśoṇitaiḥ // Rcūm_5.115 //
children.translated_text: a crucible made from that, smeared with bedbug blood, // Rcūm 5.115 //
with roots of <s>balā</s>, <s>abda</s> (Cyperus), and <s>dhāvanī</s> — [this is] the diamond-melting beak-crucible (<s>vajradrāvaṇakrauñcikā</s>);

children.text: sahate'gniṃ caturyāmaṃ drāvaṇe vyayitā satī // Rcūm_5.116 //
children.translated_text: it withstands fire for four <s>yāmas</s> (twelve hours), being consumed in the melting process. // Rcūm 5.116 //
{Crucible-reviving (<s>mūṣāpyāyana</s>)}
When the crucible approaches a molten state due to sustained blowing,
the momentary lifting [of the crucible from the fire] — that is called crucible-reviving (<s>mūṣāpyāyana</s>). // Rcūm 5.117 //
{Brinjal-crucible (<s>vṛntākamūṣā</s>)}
In a brinjal-shaped crucible, having attached a tube ten fingers [long],
pointing upward like a <s>dhattūra</s> flower, firmly and tightly sealed — // Rcūm 5.118 //
eight fingers [in height] with an opening — that is the brinjal-crucible (<s>vṛntākamūṣikā</s>);
with this, one should extract the essence (<s>sattva</s>) of mica (<s>kharpara</s>) and other soft [minerals]. // Rcūm 5.119 //
{Cow-teat crucible (<s>gostanīmūṣā</s>)}
A crucible shaped like a cow's teat, with a lid having a tip —

children.text: sattvānāṃ drāvaṇe śuddhau sā mūṣā gostanī bhavet // Rcūm_5.120 //
children.translated_text: for melting and purification of metallic essences, that crucible is the cow-teat [type] (<s>gostanī</s>). // Rcūm 5.120 //
{Cup-crucible (<s>mallamūṣā</s>)}
The prescribed cup-crucible (<s>mallamūṣā</s>), formed of a pair of cup-halves joined together,
is proclaimed for the steaming of <s>parpaṭī</s> (laminated preparations), mercury preparations, etc. // Rcūm 5.121 //
{Fired-crucible (<s>pakvamūṣā</s>)}
That which has the form of a potter's vessel, firm and well-fired —
that is called the fired-crucible (<s>pakvamūṣā</s>), used for heating bolus-preparations (<s>poṭalī</s>) etc. // Rcūm 5.122 //
{Sphere-crucible (<s>golamūṣā</s>)}
Mouthless, shaped like a ball, containing the substances [to be processed] inside —

children.text: golamūṣeti sā proktā satvaraṃ dravyarodhinī // Rcūm_5.123 //
children.translated_text: that is called the sphere-crucible (<s>golamūṣā</s>), quickly containing the substances. // Rcūm 5.123 //
{Great-crucible (<s>mahāmūṣā</s>)}

children.text: tale yā kūrparākārā kramād upari vistṛtā /
children.translated_text: Turtle-shaped at the base, gradually expanding upward —
A large crucible resembling a large <s>vṛntāka</s> (eggplant) — that is known as the <s>mahāmūṣā</s> (great crucible);

children.text: sā cāyo'bhrakasattvādeḥ puṭāya drāvaṇāya ca // Rcūm_5.124 //
children.translated_text: it is used for the heating (<s>puṭa</s>) and melting (<s>drāvaṇa</s>) of iron (<s>ayas</s>), mica-essence (<s>abhrakasattva</s>), and the like. // Rcūm 5.124 //
{<s>Mañjūṣamūṣā</s> (box-crucible)}
A crucible which is in the shape of a box (<s>mañjūṣā</s>), deep but not wide,
measuring six <s>aṅgulas</s> (finger-breadths) — that crucible is designated <s>mañjūṣā</s>;

children.text: bhūmau nikhanya tāṃ mūṣāṃ dadyātpuṭamathopari // Rcūm_5.125 //
children.translated_text: one should bury that crucible in the ground and apply a <s>puṭa</s> (sealed heating) over it from above. // Rcūm 5.125 //
{<s>Mūśalamūṣā</s> (pestle-crucible)}
A crucible that is flat at the base, cylindrical, and eight <s>aṅgulas</s> in height —

children.text: mūṣā sā muśalākhyā syāccakrībaddharase hitā // Rcūm_5.126 //
children.translated_text: that crucible is called <s>muśala</s> (pestle-shaped); it is suitable for mercury bound by the <s>cakrī</s> method. // Rcūm 5.126 //
{<s>Koṣṭhī</s> (furnace — introduction)}
For the extraction of essences (<s>sattva</s>) from [minerals], and for the purification of those already extracted,
furnaces (<s>koṣṭhikā</s>) of various shapes [are described]; their characteristics are now stated. // Rcūm 5.127 //
{<s>Aṅgārakoṣṭhikā</s> (charcoal furnace)}
Having a height equal to a royal <s>hasta</s> (cubit), and half that in length and width,

children.text: caturasrā ca kuḍyena veṣṭitā mṛnmayena hi // Rcūm_5.128 //
children.translated_text: square in shape, and enclosed by a wall made of clay — // Rcūm 5.128 //
on one wall a hole should be made, measuring a <s>vitasti</s> (span) in circumference;

children.text: dvāraṃ sārdhavitastyā ca saṃmitaṃ sudṛḍhaṃ śubham // Rcūm_5.129 //
children.translated_text: the door should measure one and a half <s>vitastis</s>, well-built and sturdy. // Rcūm 5.129 //
Below the threshold, an opening suitable for blowing should be made;
the wall above the lintel should be a <s>prādeśa</s> (hand-span) in height. // Rcūm 5.130 //
An opening should also be made above, measuring one <s>prādeśa</s>;

children.text: tataśceṣṭikayā ruddhvā dvārasaṃdhiṃ vilipya ca // Rcūm_5.131 //
children.translated_text: then, blocking it with a brick and sealing the door-joint — // Rcūm 5.131 //
filling it with charcoal, one should blow with a pair of bellows;
the charcoal and the material to be smelted should be inserted through the upper opening. // Rcūm 5.132 //
The <s>sattva</s>-extraction pellets should be [added] five at a time, again and again;
this is the charcoal furnace (<s>aṅgārakoṣṭhī</s>), which extracts the essence (<s>sattva</s>) of hard [minerals]. // Rcūm 5.133 //
{<s>Pātālakoṣṭhikā</s> (underground furnace)}
In firm ground, one should dig a pit measuring one <s>vitasti</s>, well-shaped;

children.text: vartulaṃ cātha tanmadhye gartamanyaṃ prakalpayet // Rcūm_5.134 //
children.translated_text: round; and then in its center, another pit should be fashioned — // Rcūm 5.134 //
four <s>aṅgulas</s> wide and of corresponding depth,
with a horizontal tube extending from the pit to the surface of the earth. // Rcūm 5.135 //
Slightly raised on the outside, sloping inward toward the pit —
a clay disc with five holes should be placed over the inner pit. // Rcūm 5.136 //
Filling the furnace with charcoal (<s>kokila</s>), one should blow with a single bellows;

children.text: pātālakoṣṭhikā hy eṣā dhātūnāṃ sattvapātinī // Rcūm_5.137 //
children.translated_text: this is the underground furnace (<s>pātālakoṣṭhikā</s>), which extracts the essence (<s>sattva</s>) of metals (<s>dhātu</s>), // Rcūm 5.137 //
proclaimed by <s>Nandin</s> for substances that require smelting.
{<s>Gārakoṣṭhī</s> (lime furnace)}
That which is twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> deep and one <s>prādeśa</s> in measure, // Rcūm 5.138 //
four <s>aṅgulas</s> above which is fitted with a ring —
a perforated disc should be placed upon the ring. // Rcūm 5.139 //
Placing charcoal therein, one should blow through a curved tube (<s>vaṅkanāla</s>);
this is the lime furnace (<s>gārakoṣṭhī</s>), said to destroy refined metals. // Rcūm 5.140 //
{<s>Vaṅkanāla</s> (curved tube)}
It should be made of crucible-clay, measuring one <s>aratni</s> (forearm-length), sturdy,

children.text: adhomukhaṃ ca tadvaktre nālaṃ pañcāṅgulaṃ tathā // Rcūm_5.141 //
children.translated_text: with its mouth facing downward and a tube of five <s>aṅgulas</s> at its opening. // Rcūm 5.141 //
This is called the <s>vaṅkanāla</s> (curved tube), prescribed for vigorous blowing.
{<s>Tiryakpradhamanakoṣṭhī</s> (lateral-blowing furnace)}
A furnace of similar type is prescribed for the processing of mercury and other substances. // Rcūm 5.142 //
It has a height of twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> and is four <s>aṅgulas</s> at the base;
called the lateral-blowing (<s>tiryakpradhamana</s>) furnace, it purifies soft substances. // Rcūm 5.143 //
{<s>Puṭa</s> (sealed heating — definition)}
The <s>puṭa</s> is the indicator of proper calcination (<s>māraṇa</s>) for mercury and similar substances;

children.text: neṣṭo nyūnādhikaḥ pākaḥ supākaṃ hitamauṣadham // Rcūm_5.144 //
children.translated_text: neither insufficient nor excessive heating is desirable — well-heated medicine is beneficial. // Rcūm 5.144 //
From <s>puṭa</s> [comes] the irreversibility (<s>apunarbhāva</s>) of metals and the increase of their qualities, hence superiority;
non-sinking in water (<s>apsu-amajjana</s>) and the filling of finger-lines (<s>rekhāpūrṇatā</s>) result from the <s>puṭa</s>. // Rcūm 5.145 //
From the <s>puṭa</s> [come] coloring power, lightness, rapid pervasion, and the power of kindling;
even from mercury that has undergone <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion), metals gain superior qualities. // Rcūm 5.146 //
Just as fire penetrates a stone from outside through the application of <s>puṭa</s>,
so too the attainment of qualities such as pulverization is certain in metals. // Rcūm 5.147 //
{<s>Mahāpuṭa</s> (great heating)}
In a low, wide pit, two <s>hastas</s> square,
filled with a thousand cow-dung cakes — the medicine to be heated // Rcūm 5.148 //
sealed carefully in a <s>krauñcī</s> (crane-shaped vessel) should be placed upon the cakes;
half of a thousand cow-dung cakes should be arranged above the <s>krauñcī</s>. // Rcūm 5.149 //
Fire should be ignited there — this is known as <s>mahāpuṭa</s> (great heating).
{<s>Gajapuṭa</s> (elephant heating)}
A square pit measuring one royal <s>hasta</s>, and of corresponding depth — // Rcūm 5.150 //
filled with thousands of cow-dung cakes up to the brim, one should then place
a <s>kumudī</s> vessel there, filled with the substance to be heated. // Rcūm 5.151 //
Half the previous quantity of cow-dung cakes and dried dung (<s>giriṇḍa</s>) should be placed above;
this is called <s>gajapuṭa</s> (elephant heating), which produces great qualities. // Rcūm 5.152 //

children.text: itthaṃ cāratnike kuṇḍe puṭaṃ vārāhamucyate // Rcūm_5.153 //
