children.translated_text: Similarly, in a pit of one <s>aratni</s> (forearm-length), the heating is called <s>vārāha</s> (boar). // Rcūm 5.153 //

body.translated_text: {<s>Vārāhapuṭa</s> (boar heating)}

children.translated_text: {<s>Kukkuṭapuṭa</s> (hen heating)}
A <s>puṭa</s> given on the surface of the ground, two <s>vitastis</s> in height
and equally wide at the base — that is the <s>kukkuṭaka</s> (hen) <s>puṭa</s>. // Rcūm 5.154 //
{<s>Kapotapuṭa</s> (pigeon heating)}
A <s>puṭa</s> given on the ground with eight cow-dung cakes —
that, used for [preparing] ash of young mercury, is called <s>kapotapuṭa</s> (pigeon heating). // Rcūm 5.155 //
{<s>Govara</s> (definition; a kind of dried cow-dung)}
Dried cow-dung, trampled by cow-hooves inside a cowshed, and powdered —
that is designated as <s>govara</s>, the best agent in alchemical processing. // Rcūm 5.156 //
{<s>Govarapuṭa</s> (<s>govara</s> heating)}
A <s>puṭa</s> given with <s>govara</s> (dried cow-dung powder) or with rice husks —
that is called <s>govarapuṭa</s>, for the perfection of mercury-ash. // Rcūm 5.157 //
{<s>Bhāṇḍapuṭa</s> (vessel heating)}
In a large vessel filled with rice husks, with a crucible placed in the middle,
when heating is done by fire — that is called <s>bhāṇḍapuṭa</s> (vessel heating). // Rcūm 5.158 //
{<s>Vālukāpuṭa</s> (sand heating)}
When the <s>krauñcikā</s> (vessel) is covered from below and above
with heated sand — that is <s>vālukāpuṭa</s> (sand heating). // Rcūm 5.159 //
{<s>Bhūdharapuṭa</s> (mountain heating)}
One should properly bury the fire-vessel in the earth, two <s>aṅgulas</s> below;
when the <s>puṭa</s> is [applied] from above — that is called <s>bhūdhara</s> (mountain) <s>puṭa</s>. // Rcūm 5.160 //
{<s>Lāvakapuṭa</s> (reaper heating)}
A <s>puṭa</s> with only sixteen rice husks or <s>govaras</s> placed above —
that is called <s>lāvaka</s> (reaper), for processing very soft substances. // Rcūm 5.161 //
{<s>Anuktapuṭa</s> (unspecified heating)}
When the measure of <s>puṭa</s> is unspecified, then according to the strength or weakness of the substance to be processed,
the <s>puṭa</s> should be determined and given by those skilled in reasoning and deliberation. // Rcūm 5.162 //
{Synonyms for dried cow-dung}
<s>Piṣṭaka</s>, <s>chagaṇa</s>, <s>chāṇa</s>, <s>upala</s>, and also <s>utpala</s>,
<s>giriṇḍa</s>, <s>upalasāṭhī</s>, and <s>navārī</s> — these are names for dried cow-dung (<s>chagaṇa</s>). // Rcūm 5.163 //
{Conclusion}

children.text: yaḥ somadevairvihitaṃ prakīrṇamadhyāyam enaṃ prakaroti pāṭhe /
children.translated_text: Whoever studies this miscellaneous chapter (<s>prakīrṇādhyāya</s>) composed by <s>Somadeva</s>,

children.text: nāsau samīheta gurūpadeśaṃ rasendravaidye'pi ca dhātuvāde // Rcūm_5.164 //
children.translated_text: he shall not need a teacher's instruction even in the science of the lord of mercury (<s>rasendravaidya</s>) and metallurgy (<s>dhātuvāda</s>). // Rcūm 5.164 //
<s>Rasendracūḍāmaṇi</s>, Chapter 7
Now <s>Somadeva</s> describes the plants that aid mercury (<s>darśina rasāḥ</s>),
as prescribed in the <s>Śrīkaṇṭhāgama</s>, distinguished in alchemical processing. // Rcūm 7.1 //
{Sixty-eight types of <s>rasauṣadhi</s> (mercurial medicines)}
<s>Jalotpala</s> (water lily), <s>samaṅgā</s>, <s>rasā</s>, <s>jalapippalī</s> (water long-pepper),
<s>sthalaprasāriṇī</s>, <s>ciñcī</s> (tamarind), <s>jālinī</s>, <s>jalamūlakā</s> (water radish) — // Rcūm 7.2 //
<s>Candrodakā</s>, <s>ardhacandā</s>, <s>jalāpāmārga</s>, <s>tiktakā</s>,

children.text: tuṣāmbu kākamācī ca jalakumbhī tathā śaṭī // Rcūm_7.3 //
children.translated_text: <s>tuṣāmbu</s>, <s>kākamācī</s> (black nightshade), <s>jalakumbhī</s>, and also <s>śaṭī</s> (zedoary) — // Rcūm 7.3 //
<s>Uttamā</s>, <s>hemapuṣpī</s> (golden-flowered), <s>durgandhā</s> (foul-smelling), <s>sitagandhinī</s>,

children.text: māṇḍūkī mohinī māṃsī pāṣāṇī cātha śīśikā // Rcūm_7.4 //
children.translated_text: <s>māṇḍūkī</s> (frog plant), <s>mohinī</s>, <s>māṃsī</s> (spikenard), <s>pāṣāṇī</s>, and <s>śīśikā</s> — // Rcūm 7.4 //
<s>Sārivā</s> (Indian sarsaparilla), <s>lambuṣā</s>, <s>meghanādī</s>, and <s>śukanāsikā</s> (parrot-beak),
<s>potakī</s>, <s>hīriṇī</s>, <s>vajrakandikā</s>, and <s>aparājitā</s> (unconquerable) — // Rcūm 7.5 //
<s>Vanamālā</s>, <s>vidārī</s> (Pueraria tuberosa), <s>kukkuṭā</s>, <s>halinīśvarī</s>,

children.text: vārāhī bṛhatī mūrvā sarpākṣī sadacitrikā // Rcūm_7.6 //
children.translated_text: <s>vārāhī</s> (Dioscorea), <s>bṛhatī</s> (Solanum indicum), <s>mūrvā</s>, <s>sarpākṣī</s>, <s>sadacitrikā</s> — // Rcūm 7.6 //
<s>Mālārjuna</s>, <s>gojihvā</s> (oxtongue), <s>garuḍī</s>, <s>haṃsapādikā</s> (goosefoot),

children.text: nandinī śikhipādī ca kāśmarī tulasī tathā // Rcūm_7.7 //
children.translated_text: <s>nandinī</s>, <s>śikhipādī</s> (peacock-foot), <s>kāśmarī</s> (Gmelina arborea), and also <s>tulasī</s> (holy basil) — // Rcūm 7.7 //
<s>Vanakūṣmāṇḍavallī</s> (wild ash-gourd creeper), <s>vṛścikālī</s> (scorpion plant), and <s>veṇukā</s>,

children.text: muśalī citrapādī ca karmasphoṭī tathā viṣā // Rcūm_7.8 //
children.translated_text: <s>muśalī</s> (Curculigo), <s>citrapādī</s>, <s>karmasphoṭī</s>, and also <s>viṣā</s> (aconite) — // Rcūm 7.8 //
<s>Ajamārī</s>, <s>pāṭalā</s> (Stereospermum), <s>paṭolī</s> (pointed gourd), <s>dhanvayāsaka</s>,

children.text: bhārṅgī viṣaghnī guḍūcī vāsā bhṛṅgī ca pāgavaḥ // Rcūm_7.9 //
children.translated_text: <s>bhārṅgī</s> (Clerodendrum), <s>viṣaghnī</s> (poison-destroyer), <s>guḍūcī</s> (Tinospora), <s>vāsā</s> (Adhatoda), <s>bhṛṅgī</s>, and <s>pāgava</s>. // Rcūm 7.9 //
Thus sixty-eight powerful <s>rasauṣadhīs</s> (mercurial herbs) have been declared,
[useful] in binding (<s>bandhana</s>), killing (<s>māraṇa</s>), likewise digestion (<s>jāraṇa</s>), and restraining (<s>niyāmana</s>),
in the absorption (<s>bandhādāna</s>) of mercury, and in the removal of all its defects. // Rcūm 7.10 //

children.text: vindhyādrau himaparvate ca malaye gomantake śrīgirau sahyādrāvatha pāriyātrakagirau kiṣkindhanāmālaye /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Vindhya</s> mountains, the <s>Himālaya</s>, the <s>Malaya</s>, <s>Gomanta</s>, <s>Śrīgiri</s>, the <s>Sahyādri</s>, the <s>Pāriyātraka</s> mountain, in [the range] named <s>Kiṣkindha</s>,

children.text: māhendre'pyatha mālyavatkṣitidhare tadrūpanāmādhikaṃ gopābhīrakasiddhavaidyamukhato vaidyaiḥ samāvedyatām // Rcūm_7.11 //
children.translated_text: in the <s>Māhendra</s> and also the <s>Mālyavat</s> mountain — their forms and names in detail should be learned by physicians from cowherds, <s>Ābhīra</s> tribesmen, <s>Siddhas</s>, and experienced healers. // Rcūm 7.11 //
{<s>Sarpākṣyādigaṇa</s> (the <s>sarpākṣī</s> group)}
<s>Sarpākṣī</s> (snake-eye), <s>vandhyakarkoṭī</s> (barren bitter gourd), <s>jalabimbī</s> (water <s>bimba</s>), and <s>jambukī</s>,

children.text: punarnavā ca matsyākṣī bhṛṅgarājaḥ śatāvarī // Rcūm_8.1 //
children.translated_text: <s>punarnavā</s> (Boerhavia), <s>matsyākṣī</s> (fish-eye), <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> (Eclipta), <s>śatāvarī</s> (Asparagus) — // Rcūm 8.1 //

body.translated_text: <s>Rasendracūḍāmaṇi</s>, Chapter 8

children.translated_text: <s>Śarapuṅkhā</s> (Tephrosia), <s>maṇḍūkaparṇikā</s> (Centella), <s>brahmadaṇḍikā</s>,

children.text: anantā kukkuṭī jaṅghā kākamācī śikhaṇḍinī // Rcūm_8.2 //
children.translated_text: <s>anantā</s> (endless), <s>kukkuṭī</s>, <s>jaṅghā</s>, <s>kākamācī</s> (black nightshade), <s>śikhaṇḍinī</s> (peacock-crested) — // Rcūm 8.2 //
<s>Sahadevī</s>, <s>kapotī</s> (pigeon plant), <s>viṣṇukrāntā</s> (Evolvulus), <s>kuraṇṭaka</s>,

children.text: mahābalā nāgabalā mūrvā rāsnā kuriṅginī // Rcūm_8.3 //
children.translated_text: <s>mahābalā</s> (great-strength), <s>nāgabalā</s> (Grewia), <s>mūrvā</s>, <s>rāsnā</s>, <s>kuriṅginī</s> — // Rcūm 8.3 //
<s>Phaṇi</s> (hooded one), <s>nīlī</s> (indigo), <s>prapunnāṭa</s> (Cassia), <s>samaṅgā</s>, and also <s>āmalakī</s> (Indian gooseberry),
<s>jvālinī</s> (flaming), <s>meghanāda</s> (thunder), <s>gojihvā</s> (oxtongue), <s>padmacāriṇī</s> (lotus-walker) — // Rcūm 8.4 //
<s>Pāṭhā</s> (Cissampelos), <s>kokilākṣa</s> (cuckoo-eye), <s>tripattrā</s> (three-leaved), <s>ākhukarṇikā</s> (mouse-ear),

children.text: ekaparṇī dviparṇī ca triparṇī kṣīriṇī tathā // Rcūm_8.5 //
children.translated_text: <s>ekaparṇī</s> (one-leaved), <s>dviparṇī</s> (two-leaved), <s>triparṇī</s> (three-leaved), and also <s>kṣīriṇī</s> (milky) — // Rcūm 8.5 //
<s>Tittiḍī</s>, <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s> (ram's horn), <s>tulasī</s> (holy basil), <s>śyāmaparṇikā</s> (dark-leaved),
<s>śvetādriparṇikā</s> (white mountain-leaf) — thus is considered the <s>sarpākṣyādigaṇa</s> (the <s>sarpākṣī</s> group). // Rcūm 8.6 //
Forty-six in number, it serves as the restrainer (<s>niyāmaka</s>) of mercury;
the five parts (<s>pañcāṅgī</s>) of these plants should be collected according to proper method. // Rcūm 8.7 //
For sweating (<s>svedana</s>) of mercury and such, for crucible-preparation, and for purification,

children.text: aṣṭopari yathālābhaṃ grāhyā prokteṣu karmasu // Rcūm_8.8 //
children.translated_text: more than eight [plants] should be taken as available for the prescribed operations. // Rcūm 8.8 //
An excess beyond eight certainly increases the [efficacy of] qualities.
{<s>Vyāghrikādigaṇa</s> (the <s>vyāghrikā</s> group)}
<s>Vyāghrikā</s> (tiger plant), <s>rākṣasī</s> (demoness plant), <s>vahni</s> (fire plant), <s>cāṇḍālī</s>, <s>gajakarṇikā</s> (elephant-ear) — // Rcūm 8.9 //
<s>Ṣaṭkārī</s>, <s>śaṅkhapuṣpī</s> (conch-flower), <s>bṛhatī</s> (Solanum), <s>hilamocaka</s>,
<s>śṛgālajihvikā</s> (jackal-tongue), <s>vahni</s> (fire plant), <s>madanī</s>, and also <s>lāṅgalī</s> (plough plant) — // Rcūm 8.10 //
<s>Cakrikā</s>, <s>vajriṇī</s>, <s>vyāghrī</s> (tigress), <s>kaṅkatī</s>, <s>putrajīvikā</s> (child-life plant),

children.text: kañcukī caiva karkoṭī kumārī padmacāriṇī // Rcūm_8.11 //
children.translated_text: <s>kañcukī</s> (armored), <s>karkoṭī</s> (bitter gourd), <s>kumārī</s> (aloe), <s>padmacāriṇī</s> (lotus-walker) — // Rcūm 8.11 //

children.text: ekavīrā rudantī ca lakṣmī narakasā tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Ekavīrā</s> (sole hero), <s>rudantī</s> (weeping plant), <s>lakṣmī</s>, and also <s>narakasā</s>,

children.text: uccaṭā raktacitrā ca nāginī nāgavallikā // Rcūm_8.12 //
children.translated_text: <s>uccaṭā</s> (eradicator), <s>raktacitrā</s> (red-spotted), <s>nāginī</s> (serpent plant), <s>nāgavallikā</s> (betel) — // Rcūm 8.12 //
<s>Saktukā</s>, <s>saktuśṛṅgī</s>, <s>raktasnuk</s> (red spurge), <s>yajñavallikā</s> (sacrificial creeper),

children.text: śākhoṭo meṣaśṛṅgī ca hemalī vyāghrapādikā // Rcūm_8.13 //
children.translated_text: <s>śākhoṭa</s>, <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s> (ram's horn), <s>hemalī</s>, <s>vyāghrapādikā</s> (tiger-foot) — // Rcūm 8.13 //
<s>Śamī</s> (Prosopis), <s>vyāghranakhī</s> (tiger-claw), <s>somavallarī</s> (moon creeper), <s>arkapuṣpikā</s> (Calotropis flower),
<s>keśinī</s> (hairy), <s>kāsamārī</s>, <s>vṛkṣarāja</s> (king of trees), <s>ajamārikā</s> (goat-killer) — // Rcūm 8.14 //
<s>Koṭarākṣī</s> (hollow-eyed), <s>hanūmantī</s> (<s>Hanūmat</s>'s plant), <s>narajīvā</s>, <s>aṅganāyakī</s>,

children.text: mālikā kākatuṇḍī ca meghapuṣpī ca kaṅguṇī // Rcūm_8.15 //
children.translated_text: <s>mālikā</s> (garland plant), <s>kākatuṇḍī</s> (crow-beak), <s>meghapuṣpī</s> (cloud-flower), <s>kaṅguṇī</s> — // Rcūm 8.15 //
Also <s>tuvaravallī</s>, <s>jagatī</s>, <s>haṃsapādikā</s> (goosefoot),

children.text: kumbhinī vahnimārī ca sūryabhaktā ca vākucī // Rcūm_8.16 //
children.translated_text: <s>kumbhinī</s> (pot plant), <s>vahnimārī</s> (fire-killer), <s>sūryabhaktā</s> (sun-devoted), and <s>vākucī</s> (Psoralea) — // Rcūm 8.16 //
<s>Rasanirjīvakārī</s> (mercury-killer), <s>bhūśuṇḍī</s>, <s>kaṭutumbikā</s> (bitter gourd),

children.text: devadālī viśālā ca kārpāsī brahmarañjakam // Rcūm_8.17 //
children.translated_text: <s>devadālī</s> (Luffa), <s>viśālā</s> (broad-leaved), <s>kārpāsī</s> (cotton), <s>brahmarañjaka</s> (Brahma's dye) — // Rcūm 8.17 //
<s>Kṛṣṇākṣī</s> (black-eyed) likewise, <s>kṛṣṇadhattūra</s> (black thorn-apple), <s>vanapīluka</s> (wild <s>pīlu</s>),

children.text: śvetārko yavaciñcā ca kāravellī ca dantikā // Rcūm_8.18 //
children.translated_text: <s>śvetārka</s> (white Calotropis), <s>yavaciñcā</s>, <s>kāravellī</s> (bitter melon), and <s>dantikā</s> (Baliospermum) — // Rcūm 8.18 //

children.text: gojihvā kākajaṅghā ca śvetaguñjā ca śambarā /
children.translated_text: <s>Gojihvā</s> (oxtongue), <s>kākajaṅghā</s> (crow-shank), <s>śvetaguñjā</s> (white rosary pea), and <s>śambarā</s>,
<s>mahākālī</s> (great dark one), <s>sitāṅkola</s> (white <s>aṅkola</s>), <s>māyūra</s> (peacock plant), and <s>paṭolikā</s> — // Rcūm 8.19 //
This is the <s>vyāghrikādigaṇa</s> (the <s>vyāghrikā</s> group), supreme in producing mercury-ash (<s>rasabhasma</s>).
In the aforementioned medicinal seeds, mercury is digested separately. // Rcūm 8.20 //
{The group of <s>raktasnuhī</s> and others}
<s>Raktasnuhī</s> (red milk-hedge), <s>rudantī</s>, <s>raktāgni</s>, <s>somavallikā</s>,
<s>vṛddhadāru</s>, <s>śākhoṭī</s>, <s>mohinī</s>, <s>aṅgāravallikā</s>, // Rcūm 8.21 //
<s>barhikā</s>, <s>kṣīramārjārī</s>, <s>triśūlā</s>, <s>kṣīrakukkuṭī</s>,

children.text: jīmūtaḥ kākamācī ca nīlikā śaṅkhapuṣpikā // Rcūm_8.22 //
children.translated_text: <s>jīmūta</s>, <s>kākamācī</s> (black nightshade), <s>nīlikā</s>, <s>śaṅkhapuṣpikā</s>, // Rcūm 8.22 //
<s>nāgakarṇī</s> — a small <s>kandinī</s> (bulbous plant) having leaves shaped like <s>nāgavallī</s> (betel) leaves,

children.text: śrīśailotthā ca vajraghnī nāgakarṇīti sā smṛtā // Rcūm_8.23 //
children.translated_text: originating from <s>Śrīśaila</s>, and also called <s>vajraghnī</s> — she is known as <s>nāgakarṇī</s>. // Rcūm 8.23 //
<s>Jyotiṣmatī</s> (intellect tree), <s>drumajyoti</s>, <s>tṛṇajyoti</s>, and <s>uccaṭā</s>,
<s>udumbarī</s> (cluster fig), <s>tridaṇḍī</s>, and another called <s>nīlajyoti</s>. // Rcūm 8.24 //
<s>Hemavallarikā</s>, <s>tāmravallarī</s>, and <s>cukra</s> (sorrel),

children.text: tridaṇḍī brahmadaṇḍī ca krauñcikā sthalapadminī // Rcūm_8.25 //
children.translated_text: <s>tridaṇḍī</s>, <s>brahmadaṇḍī</s>, <s>krauñcikā</s>, <s>sthalapadminī</s>, // Rcūm 8.25 //

children.text: varā vartulaparṇā ca nāgakaṇṭhī ca lāṅgalī /
children.translated_text: <s>varā</s>, <s>vartulaparṇā</s> (round-leaved), <s>nāgakaṇṭhī</s>, and <s>lāṅgalī</s>,
<s>nāgajihvā</s>, <s>arkapatrī</s>, and likewise <s>kāṣṭhodumbarikā</s>. // Rcūm 8.26 //
<s>Kāladaṇḍī</s>, <s>triparṇī</s> — this is the group of <s>raktasnuhī</s> and others,

children.text: rasabandhe vadhe śuddhau vihitaḥ śambhunā svayam // Rcūm_8.27 //
children.translated_text: prescribed by <s>Śambhu</s> (Śiva) himself for the binding, killing, and purification of mercury. // Rcūm 8.27 //
With these vegetable substances endowed with contact, fragrance, and flavor,

children.text: śodhito marditaḥ sūto mriyate badhyate sukham // Rcūm_8.28 //
children.translated_text: mercury, when purified and triturated, is killed and bound with ease. // Rcūm 8.28 //
{The group of <s>kadalī</s> and others}
<s>Kadalī</s> (plantain), <s>sūryabhakta</s> (sunflower), and <s>kaṭukoṣātakī</s> (bitter gourd),

children.text: drāviṇī kākamācī ca śigrukā kṣīrakañcukī // Rcūm_8.29 //
children.translated_text: <s>drāviṇī</s>, <s>kākamācī</s> (black nightshade), <s>śigrukā</s> (drumstick tree), <s>kṣīrakañcukī</s>, // Rcūm 8.29 //
and <s>nīrapippalikā</s> — this is the group of <s>kadalī</s> and others;

children.text: drāvaṇaḥ sarvalohānāṃ rasādīnāṃ ca niścitam // Rcūm_8.30 //
children.translated_text: it is certain to be a flux (<s>drāvaṇa</s>) for all metals, mercury, and the like. // Rcūm 8.30 //
{The group of <s>kākamācī</s> and others}
<s>Kākamācī</s>, <s>arkapatrī</s>, <s>kāsamarda</s>, <s>kṛtāñjali</s>,

children.text: lakṣmaṇā haṃsapādī ca nāginī kṣīranālikā // Rcūm_8.31 //
children.translated_text: <s>lakṣmaṇā</s>, <s>haṃsapādī</s>, <s>nāginī</s>, <s>kṣīranālikā</s>, // Rcūm 8.31 //
<s>tāmbūlī</s> (betel), <s>vyālikā</s>, <s>brāhmī</s>, <s>kāravallī</s>, <s>arjunī</s>, <s>carā</s>,
<s>vārāhakarṇikā</s>, <s>meghadhvani</s>, and <s>sahadevikā</s>; // Rcūm 8.32 //
also <s>kuruvaka</s> — this is the group of <s>kākamācī</s> and others,

children.text: krāmaṇāya vinirdiṣṭā dehe lohe rasasya hi // Rcūm_8.33 //
children.translated_text: prescribed for the permeation (<s>krāmaṇa</s>) of mercury through the body and through metals. // Rcūm 8.33 //
<s>Ekavīrā</s>, <s>mahāvīrā</s>, <s>prayoga</s>, and <s>hemadaṇḍikā</s> —
these four varieties are proclaimed as definitive for the binding of mercury. // Rcūm 8.34 //
All of them transform body and metals, and draw away great diseases;
they are auspicious, grant offspring, and are aphrodisiac — through seeing, touching, and the like. // Rcūm 8.35 //
{<s>Ekavīrā</s>}
A creeper with leaves like those of a corpse (<s>śavapatra</s>), bearing a single fruit when cut,

children.text: ekavīreti sā proktā rasabandhakarī param // Rcūm_8.36 //
children.translated_text: she is called <s>ekavīrā</s> — supreme in effecting the binding of mercury. // Rcūm 8.36 //
{<s>Mahāvīrā</s>}

children.text: ekamekaṃ phalaṃ yasyāḥ pare patre prajāyate /
children.translated_text: She whose single fruit is produced on the terminal leaf,
whose color resembles coral — she is regarded as <s>mahāvīrā</s>. // Rcūm 8.37 //
{<s>Prayoga</s> tuber}
Having three tubers, three crests, and a pair of fruits attached to its stalk,
with leaves resembling bamboo leaves — it grows on <s>Gajavindhyācala</s> (the elephant-Vindhya mountain). // Rcūm 8.38 //

children.text: tasya madhyamakando hi prayogo nāma rākṣasaḥ /
children.translated_text: Its middle tuber is the one called <s>prayoga</s>, which is <s>rākṣasa</s> (demonically potent);

children.text: tena saṃmarditaḥ sūto mriyate badhyate sukham // Rcūm_8.39 //
children.translated_text: mercury triturated with it is killed and bound with ease. // Rcūm 8.39 //
{<s>Hemavallī</s> (golden creeper)}
Having leaves like betel leaves, yielding golden-colored sap,

children.text: phalapuṣpādihīnā ca hemavallīti sā matā // Rcūm_8.40 //
children.translated_text: devoid of fruit and flower — she is regarded as <s>hemavallī</s>. // Rcūm 8.40 //
One who has employed her through union, [and] has bound mercury with her secretions (<s>mūtra</s>),

children.text: saṃvatsaradhṛto vaktre pradhatte khecarāṃ gatim // Rcūm_8.41 //
children.translated_text: and held it in the mouth for a year — attains the power of sky-roaming (<s>khecarī gati</s>). // Rcūm 8.41 //
{The class of <s>vajradaṇḍa</s> and others}
<s>Vajralaśunadaṇḍa</s> (diamond-garlic staff), <s>lohadaṇḍa</s> (iron staff) — these three
are of the nature of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Śiva</s>, protectors of the three worlds. // Rcūm 8.42 //

children.text: pathyā śuṇṭhī śilā muṇḍī nirguṇḍī ca viḍaṅgakam /
children.translated_text: <s>Pathyā</s> (chebulic myrobalan), <s>śuṇṭhī</s> (dry ginger), <s>śilā</s> (bitumen), <s>muṇḍī</s>, <s>nirguṇḍī</s> (five-leaved chaste tree), and <s>viḍaṅga</s> (embelia),
<s>citraka</s> (leadwort), <s>trikaṭu</s> (the three pungents), gold, <s>mākṣika</s> (iron pyrites), and <s>vimala</s>. // Rcūm 8.43 //
This class of <s>vajradaṇḍa</s> and others is most excellent in <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation),
supreme in removing all diseases, and destroyer of old age and death. // Rcūm 8.44 //
{The class of <s>bhūpāṭalī</s> and others}
<s>Bhūpāṭalī</s>, <s>paṭolī</s> (pointed gourd), <s>yogārī</s>, <s>siṃhavallikā</s>,

children.text: śūkarī hemavallī ca nāgadhārī ca mārkavaḥ // Rcūm_8.45 //
children.translated_text: <s>śūkarī</s>, <s>hemavallī</s>, <s>nāgadhārī</s>, and <s>mārkava</s>. // Rcūm 8.45 //
This class of <s>bhūpāṭalī</s> and others effects the binding of mercury.
{The group of five gems (<s>pañcaratnaka</s>)}
<s>Pāṭalendīvarī</s>, <s>mantrasiṃhāsanī</s>, // Rcūm 8.46 //
<s>niśācarī</s>, and <s>kaṅkālakhecarī</s> — [these constitute] the five gems (<s>pañcaratnaka</s>),
which transform body and metals, and effect the killing and binding of mercury,
which destroy wrinkles and grey hair, and are supreme in removing all diseases. // Rcūm 8.47 //
{The sweet triad (<s>madhuratraya</s>)}

children.text: ghṛtaṃ khaṇḍo mākṣikaṃ ca vijñeyaṃ madhuratrayam /
children.translated_text: Ghee, sugar (<s>khaṇḍa</s>), and honey (<s>mākṣika</s>) — these are known as the sweet triad (<s>madhuratraya</s>).
{The urine group (<s>mūtravarga</s>)}
The urines of elephant, young elephant, buffalo, donkey, and horse, // Rcūm 9.1 //

body.translated_text: Rcūm, Chapter 9

children.text: go'jāvīnāṃ striyaḥ puṃsāṃ puṣpaṃ bījaṃ ca yojayet /
children.translated_text: of cow, goat, and sheep — the menstrual fluid and semen of women and men should be employed.
{The five earths (<s>pañcamṛttikā</s>)}

children.text: iṣṭikā gairikaṃ loṇaṃ bhasma valmīkamṛttikā // Rcūm_9.2 //
children.translated_text: Brick-powder, ochre (<s>gairika</s>), salt (<s>loṇa</s>), ash, and anthill-earth — // Rcūm 9.2 //
these are declared as the five earths by those skilled in mercury operations.
{The three alkalis (<s>kṣāratraya</s>)}
<s>Ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), barley-alkali (<s>yavakṣāra</s>), and <s>sarjikṣāra</s> (sodium carbonate) as the third. // Rcūm 9.3 //
{The alkali group (<s>kṣāravarga</s>)}
<s>Palāśa</s> (flame-of-the-forest), <s>kadalī</s> (plantain), <s>śigru</s> (drumstick), sesame (<s>tila</s>), <s>apāmārga</s> (prickly chaff flower), <s>mokṣaka</s>,
<s>mūlaka</s> (radish), tamarind (<s>tintiḍī</s>), <s>bodhi</s> (fig tree), and <s>raktarājagiri</s>. // Rcūm 9.4 //
<s>Kambala</s> and <s>aparakuḍya</s> — the alkalis of these are of various kinds;

children.text: kṣāravarga iti proktaḥ dīpanaśca mahābalaḥ // Rcūm_9.5 //
children.translated_text: this is called the alkali group, which is digestive and of great potency. // Rcūm 9.5 //
It is also a digestor (<s>jāraṇa</s>) of gems and the like, and a digestor of all metals.
{The acid group (<s>amlavarga</s>)}
<s>Amlavetasa</s> (sorrel), <s>jambīra</s> (citron), <s>nimbuka</s> (lime), <s>rājanimbuka</s> (large lime), // Rcūm 9.6 //

children.text: badaraṃ bījapūraṃ ca tintiḍī cukrikā tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>badara</s> (jujube), <s>bījapūra</s> (citron), tamarind (<s>tintiḍī</s>), and <s>cukrikā</s> (sorrel),
<s>caṇāmla</s> (chickpea acid), <s>kāñjika</s> (sour gruel), likewise <s>amlikā</s>, and sour pomegranate (<s>amladāḍima</s>), // Rcūm 9.7 //
<s>karamarda</s> and <s>kolāmla</s> (sour jujube) — this is called the acid group;

children.text: rasādīnāṃ viśuddhyarthaṃ drāvaṇe jāraṇe hitaḥ // Rcūm_9.8 //
children.translated_text: it is beneficial for the purification, fluxing, and digestion of mercury and the like. // Rcūm 9.8 //
{The salt group (<s>lavaṇavarga</s>)}
Sea salt (<s>sāmudra</s>), <s>Sindhu</s>-born (rock salt), <s>kāca</s>-derived (glass salt), that called <s>viḍa</s> (fetid salt),

children.text: sauvarcalamatho raumaṃ cullikaṃ ca gaḍādi ca // Rcūm_9.9 //
children.translated_text: <s>sauvarcala</s> (sochal salt), <s>rauma</s>, <s>cullika</s>, and <s>gaḍa</s> salt and others. // Rcūm 9.9 //
This group of salts is appetizing, digestive, and stimulant,
a flux and purifier of all metals, and of ashes as well. // Rcūm 9.10 //
{The poison group (<s>viṣavarga</s>)}

children.text: śṛṅgikaṃ kālakūṭaṃ ca vatsanābhaṃ ca saktukam /
children.translated_text: <s>Śṛṅgika</s>, <s>kālakūṭa</s>, <s>vatsanābha</s> (aconite), <s>saktuka</s>,

children.text: pītaṃ ca viṣavargo'yaṃ sa varaḥ parikīrtitaḥ // Rcūm_9.11 //
children.translated_text: and <s>pīta</s> (yellow arsenic) — this poison group is declared to be excellent. // Rcūm 9.11 //
{Poison group: medicinal properties}
This group is recommended in mercury operations and in the binding and killing thereof;
but used improperly, it certainly kills. // Rcūm 9.12 //
{The sub-poison group (<s>upaviṣavarga</s>)}

children.text: lāṅgalī viṣamuṣṭiśca karavīraś ca jayā tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Lāṅgalī</s>, <s>viṣamuṣṭi</s>, <s>karavīra</s> (oleander), and <s>jayā</s>,
<s>nīlaka</s>, <s>kanaka</s> (thorn-apple), and <s>arka</s> (calotropis) — this is the group of sub-poisons. // Rcūm 9.13 //
{Sub-poisons: medicinal properties}

children.text: dīpanaḥ pācano bhedī rase kvāpi ca yujyate /
children.translated_text: Digestive, cooking, and purgative — it is sometimes employed in mercury [operations];

children.text: viṣeṣu jaṅgamādyeṣu viṣaṃ sarpasya nāparam // Rcūm_9.14 //
children.translated_text: among animal poisons such as those of moving creatures, the poison of the serpent is unsurpassed. // Rcūm 9.14 //
{The oil group (<s>tailavarga</s>)}
Of sesame (<s>tila</s>), linseed (<s>atasī</s>), safflower (<s>kusumbha</s>), neem (<s>nimba</s>), and <s>karaja</s>,
of mustard (<s>rājyā</s>), white mustard (<s>siddhārthaka</s>), and of <s>guñjā</s> (rosary pea) and <s>kaṅguṇi</s> seeds, // Rcūm 9.15 //

children.text: madhūkasya ca tailaiśca tailavargo rase hitaḥ /
children.translated_text: and of <s>madhūka</s> (mahua) — the oils [of these constitute] the oil group, beneficial in mercury [operations].
{The milk group (<s>dugdhavarga</s>)}
Elephant, horse, woman, cow, she-donkey, she-goat, and ewe; // Rcūm 9.16 //
she-camel, <s>udumbara</s> (cluster fig), <s>aśvattha</s> (sacred fig), <s>bhānu</s> (sun-plant), <s>nyagrodha</s> (banyan), <s>tilvaka</s>,
<s>dugdhikā</s> (milk-plant), the <s>snuk</s> group (euphorbias), and likewise <s>uttamakarṇikā</s>; // Rcūm 9.17 //
the milk of these constitutes the milk group prescribed for mercury and the like.
{The bile group (<s>pittavarga</s>)}
Of buffalo, boar, and fish, of goat and peacock, // Rcūm 9.18 //
of black serpent, <s>rohita</s> (red fish), and of cat — with [their] bile,
the bile group is proclaimed for the killing, binding, and processing of mercury. // Rcūm 9.19 //
{The fat group (<s>vasāvarga</s>)}
With the fat derived from frog, tortoise, boar, serpent, and human flesh,

children.text: vasayā ca vasāvargo rasakarmaṇi śasyate // Rcūm_9.20 //
children.translated_text: the fat group is recommended in mercury operations. // Rcūm 9.20 //
{The excrement group (<s>viḍgaṇa</s>)}
Of pigeon, <s>cāṣa</s> (blue jay), dove, peacock,

children.text: gṛdhrasya kukkuṭasyāpi vinirdiṣṭo hi viḍgaṇaḥ // Rcūm_9.21 //
children.translated_text: vulture, and rooster — this is the prescribed excrement group. // Rcūm 9.21 //
It is a purifier of all metals through calcination and coating applications.
{The red group (<s>raktavarga</s>)}
Safflower (<s>kusumbha</s>), <s>khadira</s> (catechu), lac (<s>lākṣā</s>), <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s> (madder), red sandalwood (<s>raktacandana</s>), // Rcūm 9.22 //

children.text: adrī ca bandhujīvaṃ ca tathā karpūragandhinī /
children.translated_text: <s>adri</s> (mountain mineral), <s>bandhujīva</s> (noon flower), and <s>karpūragandhinī</s>,
and <s>mākṣika</s> (iron pyrites) — this should be known as the red group, a supreme coloring agent. // Rcūm 9.23 //
{The yellow group (<s>pītavarga</s>)}
<s>Kiṃśuka</s> (flame-of-the-forest), <s>karṇikāra</s> (golden shower tree), and the pair of turmeric (<s>haridrā</s>),
this yellow group is prescribed for operations with the king of mercury. // Rcūm 9.24 //
{The white group (<s>śvetavarga</s>)}

children.text: tagaraḥ kuṭajaṃ kundo guñjā jīvantikā tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Tagara</s>, <s>kuṭaja</s> (kurchi), <s>kunda</s> (jasmine), <s>guñjā</s> (rosary pea), and <s>jīvantikā</s>,
white lotus rhizome — this is stated as the white group. // Rcūm 9.25 //
{The black group (<s>kṛṣṇavarga</s>)}

children.text: kadalī krūravallī ca triphalā nīlikā nalaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Kadalī</s> (plantain), <s>krūravallī</s>, <s>triphalā</s> (three myrobalans), <s>nīlikā</s> (indigo), and <s>nala</s> (reed),
mud (<s>paṅka</s>), <s>kāsīsa</s> (green vitriol), and <s>bālāmra</s> (young mango) — this is stated as the black group. // Rcūm 9.26 //
With the red group and other groups, the substance that is of the nature of digestion (<s>jāraṇa</s>)
should be carefully imbued (<s>bhāvanīya</s>) for the attainment of such coloring indeed. // Rcūm 9.27 //
{The purifying group (<s>śodhanīyagaṇa</s>)}
Glass (<s>kāca</s>), borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), and <s>śiprā</s> — these constitute the purifying group,
which destroys the impurities of essences (<s>sattva</s>), bound mercury, and metals;
it is said by alchemists (<s>rasavādins</s>) to be the destroyer of the <s>kāpālikā</s> class [of impurities]. // Rcūm 9.28 //
{The softening group (<s>mṛdukaravarga</s>)}
Buffalo and ram horns, combined with seeds from <s>Kaliṅga</s>,
and hare bones — this combination is a destroyer of hardness in metals. // Rcūm 9.29 //
{The fluxing group (<s>drāvakavarga</s>)}
With jaggery (<s>guḍa</s>), <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium), <s>guñjā</s>, ghee (<s>ājya</s>), <s>sāra</s>, <s>ghai</s>, and borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>) —
this group is regarded as [the agent] for fluxing all hard-to-melt metals and the like. // Rcūm 9.30 //
All alkalis destroy impurities; acids [serve for] purification and digestion;

children.text: māndyaṃ viṣāṇi nighnanti snaigdhyaṃ snehāḥ prakurvate // Rcūm_9.31 //
children.translated_text: poisons counteract debility, and unctuous substances produce unctuousness. // Rcūm 9.31 //
{The great minerals (<s>mahārasas</s>)}
The great minerals are: <s>ghana</s> (mica), <s>rājāvarta</s> (lapis lazuli), <s>vaikrānta</s>, and <s>sasya</s> (zinc ore), with <s>vimala</s> and <s>adrija</s> (bitumen),

children.text: tutthaṃ ca tāpyaṃ ca rasāyanāste sattvāni teṣām amṛtopamāni // Rcūm_10.1 //
children.translated_text: <s>tuttha</s> (blue vitriol) and <s>tāpya</s> (pyrites) — these are <s>rasāyanas</s> (rejuvenative agents); their essences are like nectar. // Rcūm 10.1 //

body.translated_text: Rcūm, Chapter 10

children.translated_text: {Mica (<s>abhraka</s>): medicinal properties}

children.text: gaurītejaḥ paramam amṛtaṃ vātapittakṣayaghnaṃ prajñodbodhi praśamitarujaṃ vṛṣyam āyuṣyam agryam /
children.translated_text: The supreme radiance of <s>Gaurī</s> (Pārvatī), it is ambrosia, destroyer of <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and wasting diseases; it awakens wisdom, pacifies ailments, is aphrodisiac, life-prolonging, and supreme,

children.text: balyaṃ snigdhaṃ rucidam akaphaṃ dīpanaṃ śītavīryaṃ tattadyogaiḥ sakalagadahṛd vyoma sūtendrabandhi // Rcūm_10.2 //
children.translated_text: strengthening, unctuous, appetizing, non-phlegmatic, digestive-stimulant, and cooling in potency — through various preparations, mica destroys all diseases and binds the lord of mercury. // Rcūm 10.2 //
That mica which is brought from below the king's hand from a mine —
it yields the stated results; [but if] devoid of essence, it is utterly fruitless. // Rcūm 10.3 //
{Varieties of mica (<s>abhraka</s>)}
<s>Pināka</s>, <s>nāga</s>, <s>maṇḍūka</s>, and <s>vajra</s> — thus mica is classified;
each is fourfold according to color distinctions of white and so on. // Rcūm 10.4 //
{Mica: <s>pināka</s> type}
<s>Pināka</s> mica, when heated in fire, releases a mass of flakes;

children.text: tatsevitaṃ malaṃ baddhvā mārayatyeva mānavam // Rcūm_10.5 //
children.translated_text: if consumed, it binds impurities and certainly kills a person. // Rcūm 10.5 //
{Mica: <s>nāga</s> type}
<s>Nāga</s> mica, when placed in fire, produces a sound like a serpent;

children.text: tadbhuktaṃ kurute kuṣṭhaṃ maṇḍalākhyaṃ na saṃśayaḥ // Rcūm_10.6 //
children.translated_text: if consumed, it causes the skin disease called <s>maṇḍala</s> (ringworm) — there is no doubt. // Rcūm 10.6 //
{Mica: <s>maṇḍūka</s> type}
<s>Maṇḍūka</s> (frog) mica, when heated, falls down by jumping repeatedly;
it causes urinary stone disease (<s>aśmarī</s>), incurable except by surgery. // Rcūm 10.7 //
{Mica: <s>vajra</s> type}
<s>Vajra</s> (diamond) mica, when heated in fire, is freed from all defects;
it transforms body and metals, and is supreme in removing all diseases. // Rcūm 10.8 //
{Mica subtypes: by color}

children.text: śvetaṃ raktaṃ ca pītaṃ ca kṛṣṇamevaṃ caturvidham /
children.translated_text: White, red, yellow, and black — thus it is fourfold;
white is prescribed for white-making operations, red and others for yellow-making operations. // Rcūm 10.9 //
Although mica is stated to be of four excellent varieties in <s>rasāyana</s>,
nevertheless, the black-colored one is superior by tens of millions of times. // Rcūm 10.10 //
{Mica: physical properties}
That which is unctuous, with broad flakes, resistant to fire, and heavier than average,

children.text: sukhanirmocyapatraṃ ca tadabhraṃ śastam īritam // Rcūm_10.11 //
children.translated_text: and whose leaves are easily separated — that mica (<s>abhra</s>) is declared excellent. [Rcūm 10.11]
{<s>Abhra</s> (mica): inferior types}
Mica that is sparkling, resembling glass or slag (<s>kiṭṭa</s>), should not consume mercury.

children.text: grāsitaścenna yojyo'sau lohe caiva rasāyane // Rcūm_10.12 //
children.translated_text: If it does consume, that [mercury] should not be used in metallurgy or in <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation therapy). [Rcūm 10.12]

children.text: niścandrikaṃ mṛtaṃ vyoma sevyaṃ sarvagadeṣu ca /
children.translated_text: Mica calcined to be free of sparkle (<s>niścandrika</s>) is fit for use in all diseases.

children.text: sevitaṃ candrikāyuktaṃ mehaṃ mandānalaṃ caret // Rcūm_10.13 //
children.translated_text: If taken with sparkle still present, it causes diabetes (<s>meha</s>) and weakened digestive fire. [Rcūm 10.13]
Those devoid of proper method who have prescribed leaf-mica as a rejuvenative —
they have prescribed what is called <s>Kālakūṭa</s> (deadly poison) as a life-giving substance. [Rcūm 10.14]
One should employ only purified mica, whether for essence-extraction or for therapeutic use.

children.text: anyathā tvaguṇaṃ kṛtvā vikarotyeva niścitam // Rcūm_10.15 //
children.translated_text: Otherwise, it certainly produces harm by rendering [the medicine] without virtue. [Rcūm 10.15]
{<s>Abhra</s> (mica): purification (<s>śodhana</s>)}
Mica heated and cast seven times into sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>)

children.text: nirdoṣaṃ jāyate nūnaṃ nikṣiptaṃ vāpi gojale // Rcūm_10.16 //
children.translated_text: certainly becomes free of defects; or it may be cast into cow's urine. [Rcūm 10.16]
Or [it may be quenched] in a decoction of <s>triphalā</s> (three fruits), or especially in cow's milk.
{<s>Abhra</s> (mica): calcination (<s>māraṇa</s>)}

children.text: tato dhānyābhrakaṃ kṛtvā piṣṭvā matsyākṣikārasaiḥ // Rcūm_10.17 //
children.translated_text: Then, having made grain-mica (<s>dhānyābhra</s>) and ground it with the juices of <s>matsyākṣikā</s> (litharge), [Rcūm 10.17]
having made discs and dried them, one should fire them with a half-elephant-dung-cake fire (<s>ardhebhaka puṭa</s>).

children.text: puṭedevaṃ hi ṣaḍvāraṃ paunarnavarasaiḥ saha // Rcūm_10.18 //
children.translated_text: One should fire thus six times with the juices of <s>punarnavā</s> (Boerhavia diffusa). [Rcūm 10.18]
Grinding the mica portion with borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>) and making into discs,
one should fire similarly seven times with half-elephant-dung-cake fires. [Rcūm 10.19]
Similarly, with the juice of <s>vāsā</s> (Adhatoda vasica) and the juice of <s>taṇḍulīya</s> (Amaranthus),
one should fire seven times according to the previously stated method. [Rcūm 10.20]
The mica thus perfected should be employed in all formulations.
{<s>Abhra</s> (mica): calcination (<s>māraṇa</s>)}
Combined with a quarter portion of borax, ground with <s>matsyākṣī</s> (litharge) juice, [Rcūm 10.21]

children.text: rundhyāt koṣṭhyāṃ dṛḍhaṃ dhmātaṃ sattvarūpaṃ bhaved ghanam /
children.translated_text: confined in a furnace and firmly smelted, the mica becomes an essence-form solid.
Having then made it into cloth-powder (fine powder) and soaked it with cow's ghee, [Rcūm 10.22]
one should roast it seven times in a potsherd placed on a stove,

children.text: agnivarṇaṃ bhavedyāvad vāraṃ vāraṃ ca cūrṇayet // Rcūm_10.23 //
children.translated_text: until it becomes fire-colored, powdering it at each turn. [Rcūm 10.23]
One should roast until a straw thrown [on it] burns.
Then, grinding it with sulphur using a decoction of banyan root, [Rcūm 10.24]
one should fire it twenty times with the <s>vārāha puṭa</s> (boar-dung-cake fire).
Again, twenty times with a decoction made from <s>triphalā</s>. [Rcūm 10.25]
Processed with <s>triphalā</s>, <s>muṇḍikā</s>, <s>bhṛṅga</s> (Eclipta), <s>pathyā</s> (Terminalia chebula), <s>nīlī</s> (indigo), and <s>sumūlaka</s>,
it should be administered in proper dosage in all diseases. [Rcūm 10.26]
Slightly inferior to essence-mica, yet free from side effects and superior in qualities —
if thus processed with a hundred firings, [Rcūm 10.27]
it becomes exceedingly virtuous, supremely digestive and appetite-stimulating.
By consuming half a <s>guñjā</s> (dose), it produces extreme hunger,
and with formulations specific to each disease, it cuts through all diseases. [Rcūm 10.28]
{<s>Abhra</s> (mica): calcination (<s>māraṇa</s>)}
Grain-mica ground with the juice of <s>kāsamarda</s> (Cassia occidentalis)
and fired a hundred times is killed (calcined) — there is no doubt in this. [Rcūm 10.29]
{<s>Abhra</s> (mica): calcination (<s>māraṇa</s>)}
Similarly, with <s>mustā</s> (nutgrass) juice and <s>taṇḍulīya</s> (Amaranthus) juice,
mica ground with <s>śivā</s> (Terminalia chebula), <s>āmalaka</s> (Indian gooseberry), and <s>saubhāgya</s> (ginger), formed into discs, [Rcūm 10.30]
fired sixty times, becomes vermilion-colored.
It destroys consumption (<s>kṣaya</s>) and innumerable other diseases, depending on the formulation and vehicle. [Rcūm 10.31]
{<s>Abhra</s> (mica): calcination (<s>māraṇa</s>)}
In a decoction of banyan root-bark, with the essence of betel leaf,
or with <s>vāsā</s> and <s>matsyākṣikī</s>, or with <s>matsyākṣī</s> and <s>kaṭhilla</s>, [Rcūm 10.32]
the mica ground with banyan tree milk and fired
becomes vermilion-like in twenty firings. [Rcūm 10.33]
{<s>Abhrakabhasma</s> (mica ash), method 6}

children.text: saṭaṅkaṇaṃ gavāṃ dugdhaiḥ piṣṭaṃ prapuṭitaṃ ghanam /
children.translated_text: Mica ground with borax and cow's milk, properly fired,
becomes free of sparkle and of superior quality in thirty firings. [Rcūm 10.34]

children.text: evaṃ siddhāni cābhrāṇi tālena puṭitāni cet /
children.translated_text: Micas thus processed, if further fired with orpiment (<s>tāla</s>),
become exceedingly potent and even superior to mercury. [Rcūm 10.35]
{<s>Abhra</s> (mica) ash: physical properties}
Dryness, fineness, floating on water, emergence of a reddish color,
and a lustre of various qualities — these arise through many firings. [Rcūm 10.36]
{<s>Abhra</s> (mica) essence: extraction (<s>sattva-pātana</s>)}
With the juices of <s>kāsamarda</s>, <s>ghana</s> (Cyperus rotundus), <s>dhvanivāsā</s>, and <s>punarbhū</s> (Boerhavia),

children.text: matsyākṣyāḥ kāravellyāśca haṃsapādyā rasaiḥ pṛthak // Rcūm_10.37 //
children.translated_text: of <s>matsyākṣī</s>, <s>kāravellī</s> (bitter gourd), and <s>haṃsapādī</s>, each separately, [Rcūm 10.37]
grinding and grinding carefully, one should dry it by exposure to heat.

children.text: khaliṃ godhūmacūrṇaṃ ca kṣudramatsyāṃśca ṭaṅkaṇam // Rcūm_10.38 //
children.translated_text: Oil-cake, wheat flour, small fish, and borax — [Rcūm 10.38]
each in a portion equal to the mica, one should add and grind.
At each grinding, one should properly dry it in sunlight. [Rcūm 10.39]
The five products of goat, the five products of cow (<s>pañcagavya</s>), and the five products of buffalo —

children.text: kṣiptvā golān prakurvīta kiṃcit tindukasaṃmitān // Rcūm_10.40 //
children.translated_text: adding these, one should make balls roughly the size of a <s>tinduka</s> (Diospyros) fruit. [Rcūm 10.40]
{<s>Pañcāṅga</s> (five constituents)}

children.text: payo dadhi ghṛtaṃ mūtraṃ viṭ ca pañcāṅgam ucyate /
children.translated_text: Milk, curd, ghee, urine, and dung — these are called the five constituents (<s>pañcāṅga</s>).

children.text: adhaḥpātanakoṣṭhyāṃ hi dhmātvā sattvaṃ nipātayet // Rcūm_10.41 //
children.translated_text: In a downward-extraction furnace, one should smelt and cause the essence to drop down. [Rcūm 10.41]

children.text: {abhra:: sattva:: pātana:: separating kiṭṭa and sattva}
children.translated_text: {<s>Abhra</s> essence extraction: separating slag and essence}

children.text: koṣṭhyāḥ kiṭṭaṃ samāhṛtya vicūrṇya ravakān haret /
children.translated_text: Having collected the slag (<s>kiṭṭa</s>) from the furnace, crushing it, one should extract the globules.
That slag should be ground with a little borax and cow dung. [Rcūm 10.42]
Having made balls and dried them, one should smelt again as before.

children.text: bhūyaḥ kiṭṭaṃ samāhṛtya mṛditvā sattvamāharet // Rcūm_10.43 //
children.translated_text: Again collecting the slag, softening it, one should extract the essence. [Rcūm 10.43]

children.text: evameva punaḥ kiṭṭaṃ dhmātvā sattvaṃ samāharet /
children.translated_text: In this same way, one should again smelt the slag and collect the essence.
{Purification of mica essence (<s>abhrakasattvaśodhana</s>)}
Then those essence-granules, having been boiled with acidic sour gruel, [Rcūm 10.44]
combined with the group of purifying [herbs], confined in a crucible,

children.text: samyag drutaṃ samāhṛtya dvivāraṃ pradhamet punaḥ // Rcūm_10.45 //
children.translated_text: properly melted and collected, one should smelt again twice. [Rcūm 10.45]
Thus perfected, the essence is fit for use in mercurial rejuvenation therapy.
{Softening of mica essence (<s>abhrakasattvamṛdukaraṇa</s>)}
Melted and quenched in honey, oil, animal fat, and ghee, [Rcūm 10.46]
the essence and hard metals become soft in ten turns.
{<s>Abhra</s> essence: formulation}
A heated ball of the essence [placed] in sour gruel mixed with tin, [Rcūm 10.47]
quenched instantly, one should break it with an iron hammer.

children.text: sampratāpya ghanasthūlān kaṇānkṣiptvā ca kāñjike // Rcūm_10.48 //
children.translated_text: Having reheated the large thick granules and cast them into sour gruel, [Rcūm 10.48]
collecting them instantly, breaking them, one should make a powder.

children.text: goghṛtena ca taccūrṇaṃ bharjayet pūrvavattridhā // Rcūm_10.49 //
children.translated_text: That powder should be roasted with cow's ghee three times as before. [Rcūm 10.49]
Similarly with the juice of <s>dhātrī</s> (amla) fruits, or with the juice of <s>dhātrī</s> leaves.

children.text: bharjane bharjane kāryaṃ śilāpaṭṭena peṣaṇam // Rcūm_10.50 //
children.translated_text: At each roasting, grinding on a stone slab should be performed. [Rcūm 10.50]
Then, with juices of <s>punarnavā</s> and <s>vāsā</s> mixed with sour gruel,
one should fire ten times, and ten times with sulphur. [Rcūm 10.51]
Mica essence thus perfected is of the highest quality in all respects,

children.text: yatheṣṭaṃ viniyoktavyaṃ jāraṇe ca rasāyane // Rcūm_10.52 //
children.translated_text: and should be employed as desired in digestion [of mercury] and in rejuvenation therapy. [Rcūm 10.52]

children.text: vellavyoṣasamanvitaṃ ghṛtayutaṃ vallonmitaṃ sevitaṃ divyābhraṃ kṣayapāṇḍuruggrahaṇikāḥ śūlāmakoṣṭhāmayam /
children.translated_text: Mica taken in a dose of one <s>valla</s>, combined with <s>vella</s> (Embelia ribes) and <s>vyoṣa</s> (three pungents), mixed with ghee, conquers consumption, pallor, severe <s>grahaṇī</s> (malabsorption), colic, intestinal disease,

children.text: jūrtiṃ śvāsagadaṃ pramehamaruciṃ kāsāmayaṃ durdharaṃ mandāgniṃ jaṭharavyathāṃ vijayate yogairaśeṣāmayān // Rcūm_10.53 //
children.translated_text: fever, asthma, diabetes, loss of appetite, intractable cough, weak digestive fire, abdominal pain — and by [specific] formulations, all diseases whatsoever. [Rcūm 10.53]
{<s>Abhrakadruti</s> (mica liquefaction)}

children.text: drutayo naiva nirdiṣṭāḥ śāstre dṛṣṭā api dhruvam /
children.translated_text: The liquefactions [of mica] have not been described in the treatises, though they have certainly been observed.

children.text: vinā śambhoḥ prasādena na sidhyanti kathañcana // Rcūm_10.54 //
children.translated_text: Without the grace of <s>Śambhu</s> (Śiva), they never succeed. [Rcūm 10.54]
{<s>Rājāvarta</s> (lapis lazuli): examination}
<s>Rājāvarta</s> (lapis lazuli) is slightly red, with a mixed reddish-blue lustre,

children.text: guruśca masṛṇaḥ śreṣṭhastadanyo madhyamaḥ smṛtaḥ // Rcūm_10.55 //
children.translated_text: heavy and smooth — that is the best; any other is considered middling. [Rcūm 10.55]
{<s>Rājāvarta</s>: medicinal properties}
It removes diabetes (<s>prameha</s>), consumption (<s>kṣaya</s>), hemorrhoids (<s>durnāma</s>), anemia (<s>pāṇḍu</s>), phlegm, and wind disorders.

children.text: dīpanaḥ pācano vṛṣyo rājāvartto rasāyanaḥ // Rcūm_10.56 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rājāvarta</s> is a digestive stimulant, digestive, aphrodisiac, and rejuvenative. [Rcūm 10.56]
{<s>Rājāvarta</s>: purification (<s>śodhana</s>)}
Sweated with lemon juice along with cow's urine and alkalis,
<s>rājāvarta</s> and similar minerals are purified in two or three turns. [Rcūm 10.57]
{<s>Rājāvarta</s>: calcination (<s>māraṇa</s>)}
<s>Rājāvarta</s> powdered and combined with <s>bhṛṅga</s> (Eclipta) water and sulphur,
by firing for seven nights, <s>rājāvarta</s> becomes killed (calcined). [Rcūm 10.58]
<s>Sūryāvarta</s>, <s>vajrakanda</s>, plantain, <s>koṣātakī</s> (snake gourd), drumstick (<s>śigru</s>),

children.text: vandhyā nīrakaṇā ghanā nṛpaśamī dhvāṃkṣī kumārī varā /
children.translated_text: <s>vandhyā</s>, rain-cloud water, <s>nṛpaśamī</s> (Prosopis), crow-plant (<s>dhvāṃkṣī</s>), <s>kumārī</s> (aloe), and <s>varā</s> (Terminalia chebula) —
by firing with the juice of any one of these along with acid, minerals and the like are purified.

children.text: svedakledavadhānvrajanti ca punardhmātāśca sattvāni te // Rcūm_10.59 //
children.translated_text: By sweating, moistening, and calcination they yield [their impurities], and when smelted, they [release] their essences. [Rcūm 10.59]

body.translated_text: {Minerals (<s>dhātu</s>) in general: purification (<s>śodhana</s>)}

children.translated_text: {<s>Rājāvarta</s> (?): essence extraction (<s>sattvapātana</s>)}
With alkalis, salts, household soot, <s>guñjā</s> (rosary pea), and <s>niśā</s> (turmeric) fruits,
stones and rocks combined with these release their essence completely. [Rcūm 10.60]

body.translated_text: This formulation indeed purifies all impurities from minerals.

children.translated_text: {<s>Vaikrānta</s> (tourmaline): physical properties}
Octahedral, with eight faces, six-cornered, smooth, heavy,
and endowed with pure or mixed colors — that is called <s>vaikrānta</s> (tourmaline). [Rcūm 10.61]
{<s>Vaikrānta</s>: subtypes by color}
White, red, yellow, blue, pigeon-colored,

children.text: śyāmalaḥ kṛṣṇavarṇaśca karburaścāṣṭadhā hi saḥ // Rcūm_10.62 //
children.translated_text: dark brown, black, and variegated — it is of eight kinds. [Rcūm 10.62]
{<s>Vaikrānta</s>: medicinal properties}
It grants longevity, produces strength and complexion, is highly aphrodisiac, bestows wisdom, removes all humoral disorders and diseases,

children.text: dīptāgnikṛt pavisamānaguṇas tarasvī vaikrāntakaḥ khalu vapurbalalohakārī // Rcūm_10.63 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vaikrānta</s> kindles the digestive fire, has qualities equal to a thunderbolt, is energetic, and produces strength and robustness of body. [Rcūm 10.63]
Among all rejuvenatives, it is to be counted foremost, being powerful.
<s>Vaikrānta</s>, destroyer of all diseases, should be used in place of diamond. [Rcūm 10.64]
{<s>Vaikrānta</s>: purification (<s>śodhana</s>)}
<s>Vaikrānta</s> is purified by sweating in a decoction of horse gram (<s>kulattha</s>).
{<s>Vaikrānta</s>: calcination (<s>māraṇa</s>)}
It is killed (calcined) in eight firings when combined with sulphur and lemon juice. [Rcūm 10.65]
{<s>Vaikrānta</s>: essence extraction (<s>sattvapātana</s>)}
Ground and made into pills by the essence-extraction method,
placed in a crucible and smelted for one <s>ghaṭikā</s> (24 minutes), <s>vaikrānta</s> releases its essence. [Rcūm 10.66]
{<s>Vaikrānta</s>: formulation}

children.text: bhasmatvaṃ samupāgato vikṛtako hemnā mṛtenānvitaḥ pādāṃśena kaṇājyavellasahito vallonmitaḥ sevitaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Vaikrānta</s> reduced to ash, combined with calcined gold in a quarter portion, with ghee and <s>vella</s> (Embelia), taken in a dose of one <s>valla</s>,

children.text: yakṣmāṇaṃ kṣaraṇaṃ ca pāṇḍugudajaṃ śvāsaṃ ca kāsāmayaṃ duṣṭāṃ ca grahaṇīm uraḥkṣatamukhān rogāñjayeddehakṛt // Rcūm_10.67 //
children.translated_text: conquers consumption, wasting, pallor, hemorrhoids, asthma, cough, corrupt <s>grahaṇī</s> (malabsorption), chest wounds, and such diseases — it builds the body. [Rcūm 10.67]
{<s>Vaikrānta</s>: formulation}
Blue <s>vaikrānta</s> ash combined with half [its weight of] mercury ash,
and calcined mica-essence, the two weighed equally and ground together, [Rcūm 10.68]
mixed with honey and ghee, taken in the morning in a dose of one <s>guñjā</s>,
by the method of rejuvenation therapy, one lives as long as the moon, sun, and stars. [Rcūm 10.69]
Taken in a barley-grain dose with the appropriate vehicle for each disease,
it destroys all diseases that are intractable by other medicines. [Rcūm 10.70]
Within thrice-seven (twenty-one) days, [it removes] men's sins like the waters of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>.
{<s>Sasyaka</s> (blue vitriol): mythological origin}
Having drunk the <s>Hālāhala</s> (cosmic poison) and vomited it, <s>Garutmat</s> (Garuḍa) who had drunk <s>amṛta</s> (nectar), [Rcūm 10.71]
on the mountain called <s>Maruta</s>, by the vomit mixed with nectar and poison,

children.text: tadvāntaṃ hi ghanībhūtaṃ saṃjātaṃ sasyakaṃ khalu // Rcūm_10.72 //
children.translated_text: that vomit having solidified — thus <s>sasyaka</s> (blue vitriol) was indeed born. [Rcūm 10.72]
{<s>Sasyaka</s>: examination: good quality}
That which has the beautiful hue of a peacock's neck and is heavy is greatly praised.
Just as poison combined with a substance acquires the superior qualities of that substance,
so <s>hālāhala</s> (deadly poison) combined with nectar acquires the superior qualities of nectar. // Rcūm 10.73 //
{<s>Sasyaka</s> (blue vitriol): medicinal properties}
Destroying all <s>doṣas</s> and poisons, curing abdominal colic, pain, corrupt acid bile, and constipation, beneficial,

children.text: rāsāyanaṃ vamanarekakaraṃ garaghnaṃ śvitrāpahaṃ gaditamatra mayūratuttham // Rcūm_10.74 //
children.translated_text: a rejuvenative, causing emesis and purgation, antidote to poison, and removing leucoderma — thus is described <s>mayūratuttha</s> (peacock vitriol). // Rcūm 10.74 //
<s>Sasyaka</s> well-steamed in the <s>dolāyantra</s> (swing apparatus) for three <s>praharas</s> (nine hours),
with the urines of humans, buffalo, goat, and cow — thus is <s>sasyaka</s> purified. // Rcūm 10.75 //

body.translated_text: {<s>Sasyaka/Tuttha</s>: purification}

children.translated_text: {<s>Sasyaka</s>: calcination}
Combined with <s>lakuca</s> juice, sulphur, mineralite (<s>aśma</s>), and borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>),

children.text: nirudhya mūṣikāmadhye mriyate kaukkuṭaiḥ puṭaiḥ // Rcūm_10.76 //
children.translated_text: sealed inside a mouse-shaped crucible, it dies (is calcined) with cock-type heatings (<s>kaukkuṭa puṭa</s>). // Rcūm 10.76 //
{<s>Sasyaka</s>: essence extraction}
With lemon juice and a small amount of borax, sealed inside a crucible,

children.text: tāmrarūpaṃ paridhmātaṃ sattvaṃ muñcati sasyakam // Rcūm_10.77 //
children.translated_text: <s>sasyaka</s> when fully heated releases its essence (<s>sattva</s>) in the form of copper. // Rcūm 10.77 //
{<s>Sasyaka</s>: essence extraction (alternative)}
Purified <s>sasya</s>, passed through fire, combined with the aforesaid medicines,
by the tube-blowing method, it certainly releases its essence. // Rcūm 10.78 //
{<s>Sasyaka</s>: essence ring}
Taking this essence and combining it with the essences of <s>varabhu</s> and lead (<s>nāga</s>),
a ring made therefrom, upon touch, instantly becomes a destroyer of colic. // Rcūm 10.79 //

children.text: carācaraṃ viṣaṃ bhūtaṃ ḍākinīṃ dṛggataṃ jayet /
children.translated_text: It conquers mobile and immobile poisons, evil spirits, <s>ḍākinīs</s>, and afflictions of the eye;
like <s>Rāma</s>, the commander <s>Somasena</s> — the ring, with its mantra syllable, // Rcūm 10.80 //
this ring should be made, producing visible results.
On the northern slope of the <s>Himālaya</s> there is a great tree called <s>aśvakarṇa</s>; // Rcūm 10.81 //

children.text: tatra śūlaṃ samutpannaṃ tatraiva nidhanaṃ gataḥ /
children.translated_text: there the colic arose and there itself it met its end.
Water charged with this ring, consecrated seven times with the mantra, when drunk, // Rcūm 10.82 //
is said to instantly cure colic — thus speaks <s>Bhāluki</s>.

children.text: anayā mudrayā taptaṃ tailamagnau suniścitam // Rcūm_10.83 //
children.translated_text: Oil heated with this ring over fire, applied with certainty, // Rcūm 10.83 //

children.text: lepitaṃ hanti vegena śūlaṃ yatra kvacidbhavam /
children.translated_text: when smeared, swiftly destroys colic arising from any source whatsoever;

children.text: sadyaḥ sūtikaraṃ nāryāḥ sadyo netrarujāpaham // Rcūm_10.84 //
children.translated_text: it immediately induces childbirth for women and immediately removes eye pain. // Rcūm 10.84 //
{<s>Vimala</s>: subtypes}
<s>Vimala</s> is said to be of three kinds: the first is gold-<s>vimala</s>, the second silver-<s>vimala</s>,
and the third is bronze-<s>vimala</s> — each is identified by its respective luster. // Rcūm 10.85 //
{<s>Vimala</s>: physical properties}
Round, angular, unctuous, and flaky.
{<s>Vimala</s>: medicinal properties}
<s>Vimala</s> alleviates <s>vāta</s> (wind) and <s>pitta</s> (bile), is an aphrodisiac, and an excellent rejuvenative. // Rcūm 10.86 //
{<s>Vimala</s>: subtypes and uses}
The first is prescribed for gold-making operations, the second is regarded as producing silver,

children.text: tṛtīyo bheṣaje teṣu pūrvaḥ pūrvaguṇottaraḥ // Rcūm_10.87 //
children.translated_text: and the third for medicine — among them, each earlier one has superior qualities. // Rcūm 10.87 //
{<s>Vimala</s>: purification}
<s>Vimala</s> steamed with <s>āṭarūṣa</s> (Adhatoda) juice becomes pure.
{<s>Vimala</s>: calcination}

children.text: gandhāśmalakucābhyāṃ sa mriyate daśabhiḥ puṭaiḥ // Rcūm_10.88 //
children.translated_text: With sulphur, mineralite, and <s>lakuca</s> [juice], it dies (is calcined) in ten heatings. // Rcūm 10.88 //
{<s>Vimala</s>: essence extraction}
With borax and <s>lakuca</s> juices and the ash of ram's horn,

children.text: piṣṭo mūṣodare liptaḥ saṃśoṣya ca nirudhya ca // Rcūm_10.89 //
children.translated_text: ground, smeared inside a crucible, dried, and sealed, // Rcūm 10.89 //
<s>vimala</s> when blown with six <s>prasthas</s> of charcoal releases

children.text: sattvaṃ muñcati tadyukto rasaḥ syāttu rasāyanaḥ // Rcūm_10.90 //
children.translated_text: an essence resembling lead; mercury combined with it becomes a rejuvenative. // Rcūm 10.90 //
{<s>Vimala</s>: essence medicinal use}
This essence, combined with mercury, made into a <s>piṣṭī</s> (paste) and well ground,

children.text: vilīne gandhake kṣiptvā jārayet triguṇālakam // Rcūm_10.91 //
children.translated_text: thrown into molten sulphur, one should assimilate three times the weight of realgar (<s>alaka</s>); // Rcūm 10.91 //
and also five times the weight of orpiment (<s>śilā</s>) in the tube-apparatus;
silver ash at one-tenth the amount, and an equal amount of calcined <s>vaikrānta</s> — // Rcūm 10.92 //
all powdered together and filtered through cloth,
placed inside a bottle and carefully filled up. // Rcūm 10.93 //

children.text: līḍho vyoṣavarānvito vimalako yukto ghṛtaiḥ sevito hanyād durbhagakṛjjvarān śvayathukaṃ pāṇḍupramehārucim /
children.translated_text: Licked with <s>vyoṣa</s> (the three pungents) and <s>triphala</s>, combined with <s>vimala</s> and taken with ghee, it destroys fevers causing misfortune, swelling, jaundice, urinary diseases, and loss of appetite,

children.text: mūlārtiṃ grahaṇīṃ ca śūlamatulaṃ yakṣmāmayān kāmalāṃ sarvānpittamarudgadān kimaparaṃ yogairaśeṣān gadān // Rcūm_10.94 //
children.translated_text: hemorrhoids, chronic bowel disease (<s>grahaṇī</s>), unparalleled colic, consumptive diseases, and jaundice; all diseases of <s>pitta</s> and <s>vāta</s> — what more — all diseases whatsoever by these formulations. // Rcūm 10.94 //
{<s>Śilājatu</s> (mineral pitch/bitumen): subtypes}
<s>Śilādhātu</s> (mineral pitch) is said to be of two kinds: the first, beginning with cow's urine [type], is a rejuvenative,
and the other begins with camphor; furthermore, the first is again of two kinds: // Rcūm 10.95 //
with essence and without essence — of those, the former is of superior quality.
{<s>Śilājatu</s>: origin from heated rocks}
In summer, from the feet of the <s>Himālaya</s> mountains intensely heated by the fierce sun, // Rcūm 10.96 //
from those bearing gold, silver, and copper within — <s>śilādhātu</s> (mineral pitch) oozes forth.
{<s>Śilājatu</s>: from gold-bearing rock}
That born from gold-bearing mountains is heavy, resembling the <s>japā</s> (hibiscus) flower; // Rcūm 10.97 //
it is slightly bitter, very pleasant in taste — that is the supreme rejuvenative.
{<s>Śilājatu</s>: from silver-bearing rock}
That born from silver-bearing mountains is sweet, whitish, and heavy; // Rcūm 10.98 //
<s>śilāja</s> that destroys diseases of <s>pitta</s> (bile), especially curing jaundice.
{<s>Śilājatu</s>: from copper-bearing rock}
That born from copper-bearing mountains is blue-colored, dense, and heavy; // Rcūm 10.99 //
{<s>Śilājatu</s>: testing for purity}
That which, when cast into fire, assumes a <s>liṅga</s> (phallic) shape without smoke,

children.text: salile'tha vilīnaṃ ca tacchuddhaṃ hi śilājatu // Rcūm_10.100 //
children.translated_text: and dissolves in water — that is pure <s>śilājatu</s>. // Rcūm 10.100 //

body.translated_text: <s>śilāja</s> that destroys <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) and <s>vāta</s> (wind), bitter and heating, curing consumptive diseases.

children.translated_text: {<s>Śilājatu</s>: medicinal properties}

children.text: nūnaṃ sajvarapāṇḍuśophaśamanaṃ mehāgnimāndyāpahaṃ medaśchedakaraṃ ca yakṣmaśamanaṃ mūtrāmayonmūlanam /
children.translated_text: Surely it pacifies fever, jaundice, swelling, destroys urinary diseases and digestive weakness, reduces fat, cures consumption, eradicates urinary tract diseases,

children.text: gulmaplīhavināśanaṃ jaṭharahṛcchūlaghnam āmāpahaṃ sarvatvaggadanāśanaṃ kimaparaṃ dehe ca lohe hitam // Rcūm_10.101 //
children.translated_text: destroys tumors and splenic enlargement, cures abdominal disorders, destroys colic, removes undigested toxins, destroys all skin diseases — what more — it is beneficial for both body and metals. // Rcūm 10.101 //
{<s>Śilājatu</s>: possesses properties of all other substances}
Whatever qualities exist in <s>rasa</s> (mercury), <s>uparasa</s> (secondary minerals), the lord of mercury, gems, and metals —
they all reside in <s>śilādhātu</s>, with the power to conquer old age and death. // Rcūm 10.102 //
{<s>Śilājatu</s>: purification}
With alkalis, acids, and <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium), placed in the sweating apparatus,
steamed for one <s>ghaṭikā</s> (24 minutes) — <s>śilādhātu</s> becomes purified. // Rcūm 10.103 //
{<s>Śilājatu</s>: calcination}
With orpiment (<s>śilā</s>), sulphur, yellow orpiment (<s>tāla</s>), and citron (<s>mātuluṅga</s>) juice,
<s>śilādhātu</s> when heated dies (is calcined) in eight <s>giriṇḍaka</s> heatings. // Rcūm 10.104 //
{<s>Śilājatu</s>: calcined form, medicinal use}

children.text: bhasmībhūtaśilodbhavaṃ samatulaṃ kāntaṃ ca vaikrāntakaṃ yuktaśca triphalākaṭutrayaghṛtairvallena tulyaṃ bhajet /
children.translated_text: The ash of <s>śilādhātu</s>, with equal [parts of] <s>kānta</s> (magnetic iron) and <s>vaikrāntaka</s>, combined with <s>triphala</s>, the three pungents, and ghee, should be consumed in doses equal to a <s>valla</s> (seed),

children.text: pāṇḍau yakṣmagude tathāgnisadane maheṣu mūtrāmaye gulmaplīhamahodare bahuvidhe śūle ca yonyāmaye // Rcūm_10.105 //
children.translated_text: for jaundice, consumption, hemorrhoids, digestive weakness, diabetes, urinary diseases, tumors, splenic enlargement, abdominal distension, and various types of colic and uterine disorders. // Rcūm 10.105 //
If one takes it for six months following the rejuvenative regimen,
freed from wrinkles and grey hair, one lives a hundred years in happiness. // Rcūm 10.106 //
{<s>Śilājatu</s>: essence extraction}
The mountain-born [mineral pitch], ground with the group of dissolving agents and acid,

children.text: liptvā mūṣodare ruddhvā gāḍhairdhmātaṃ hi kokilaiḥ // Rcūm_10.107 //
children.translated_text: smeared inside a crucible and sealed, blown firmly with charcoal — // Rcūm 10.107 //
<s>śilādhātu</s> releases its essence, resembling the metal of its own mine.
{<s>Karpūra-śilājatu</s> (camphor-type mineral pitch): physical properties}
The camphor-type <s>śilājatu</s> is whitish and sand-like in appearance. // Rcūm 10.108 //
{<s>Karpūra-śilājatu</s>: medicinal properties}
It destroys painful urination, urinary stones, diabetes, jaundice, and anemia.
{<s>Karpūra-śilājatu</s>: purification}

children.text: elātoyena saṃsvinnaṃ śuṣkaṃ śuddhimupaiti tat // Rcūm_10.109 //
children.translated_text: Steamed with cardamom (<s>elā</s>) water and dried, it attains purity. // Rcūm 10.109 //
Neither calcination nor essence extraction is prescribed for it by the wise.
{<s>Rasaka</s> (calamine): subtypes}

children.text: rasako dvividhaḥ prokto darduraḥ kāravellakaḥ // Rcūm_10.110 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rasaka</s> (calamine) is said to be of two kinds: <s>dardura</s> and <s>kāravellaka</s>. // Rcūm 10.110 //
The one with layers is called <s>dardura</s>, the one without layers is <s>kāravellaka</s>;
the former is better for essence extraction, and the latter for medicines and such. // Rcūm 10.111 //
{<s>Rasaka</s>: medicinal properties}
<s>Rasaka</s> destroys all urinary diseases, eliminates <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>,
cures eye diseases and consumption, and tinges metals and mercury. // Rcūm 10.112 //
{<s>Rasaka</s>: high quality}
<s>Nāgārjuna</s> declared that both mercury and <s>rasaka</s>,

children.text: śreṣṭhau siddharasau syātāṃ dehalohakarau parau // Rcūm_10.113 //
children.translated_text: when perfected, become the supreme agents for body and metal. // Rcūm 10.113 //
He by whom both mercury and <s>rasaka</s> have been made fire-resistant —

children.text: dehalohamayī siddhirdāsī tasya na saṃśayaḥ // Rcūm_10.114 //
children.translated_text: the perfection of body and metals becomes his servant, without doubt. // Rcūm 10.114 //
{<s>Rasaka</s>: purification}
<s>Kharpara</s> (calamine ore), heated and immersed seven times
in the juice of citron (<s>bījapūra</s>) — it attains spotless purity. // Rcūm 10.115 //
{<s>Rasaka</s>: purification (alternative)}

children.text: nṛmūtre meṣamūtre vā takre vā kāñjike tathā /
children.translated_text: In human urine, ram's urine, buttermilk, or sour gruel,

children.text: pratāpya majjitaṃ samyak kharparaṃ pariśudhyati // Rcūm_10.116 //
children.translated_text: heated and properly immersed — <s>kharpara</s> is purified. // Rcūm 10.116 //
{<s>Rasaka</s>: tinging with calamine}

children.text: naramūtre sthito māsaṃ rasako rañjayed dhruvam /
children.translated_text: <s>Rasaka</s> kept in human urine for a month certainly tinges

children.text: śuddhaṃ tāmraṃ rasaṃ tāraṃ śuddhaṃ svarṇaprabhaṃ tathā // Rcūm_10.117 //
children.translated_text: purified copper, mercury, and silver — making [them] shine with the luster of gold. // Rcūm 10.117 //
{<s>Rasaka</s> essence extraction (method 1)}
With turmeric, <s>triphala</s>, <s>rāla</s> (resin), sea-foam (<s>sindhudhūma</s>), borax,

children.text: sāruṣkaraiśca pādāṃśaiḥ sāmlaiḥ saṃmardya kharparam // Rcūm_10.118 //
children.translated_text: and <s>aruṣkara</s> (marking-nut) in quarter parts, with acid, grinding <s>kharpara</s>, // Rcūm 10.118 //
smeared inside an eggplant-crucible, dried and sealed,
placing <s>kharpara</s> over the crucible's mouth, one should then blow. // Rcūm 10.119 //
When the <s>kharpara</s> is removed, if the flame appears blue-white,

children.text: tadā sandaṃśato mūṣāṃ dhṛtvā kṛtvā hyadhomukhīm // Rcūm_10.120 //
children.translated_text: then holding the crucible with tongs, turning it face-down, // Rcūm 10.120 //

children.text: śanairāsphālayed bhūmau yathā nālaṃ na bhajyate /
children.translated_text: one should gently tap it on the ground so that the tube does not break;

children.text: vaṅgābhaṃ patitaṃ sattvaṃ tadādāya niyojayet // Rcūm_10.121 //
children.translated_text: the essence that falls out, resembling tin — one should take and employ it. // Rcūm 10.121 //

children.text: evaṃ hi tricaturvāraiḥ sarvaṃ sattvaṃ viniḥsaret /
children.translated_text: In this way, after three or four times, all the essence will come out.
{<s>Rasaka</s> essence extraction (method 2)}

children.text: yadvā jalayutāṃ sthālīṃ nikhanet koṣṭhikodare // Rcūm_10.122 //
children.translated_text: Alternatively, one should bury a water-filled pan inside a furnace chamber; // Rcūm 10.122 //
a perforated lid-vessel at its mouth, and at that mouth one should place the crucible face-down,

children.text: mūṣopari śikhitrāṃśca prakṣipya pradhamed dṛḍham // Rcūm_10.123 //
children.translated_text: placing charcoal atop the crucible and blowing firmly. // Rcūm 10.123 //
The essence that falls into the water of the pan should be taken and employed.
{<s>Rasaka</s>: essence calcination}

children.text: tatsattvaṃ tālakopetaṃ nikṣipya khalu kharpare // Rcūm_10.124 //
children.translated_text: That essence, combined with yellow orpiment (<s>tālaka</s>), placed on a <s>kharpara</s> dish, // Rcūm 10.124 //
roasted with an iron rod — it certainly becomes ash.
{<s>Rasaka</s>: calcined essence, medicinal use}

children.text: tadbhasma mṛtakāntena samena saha yojitam // Rcūm_10.125 //
children.translated_text: That ash, combined with an equal amount of calcined magnetic iron (<s>kānta</s>), // Rcūm 10.125 //
powder measured at eight <s>guñjā</s> seeds, combined with <s>triphala</s> decoction,
kept overnight in an iron vessel, with sesame oil as an adjunct, // Rcūm 10.126 //
when taken, it swiftly destroys even diabetes (<s>madhumeha</s>) certainly,

children.text: paittaṃ kṣayaṃ ca pāṇḍuṃ ca śvayathuṃ gulmameva ca // Rcūm_10.127 //
children.translated_text: as well as bilious diseases, consumption, anemia, swelling, and tumors, // Rcūm 10.127 //
blood-tumors in women, uterine discharge, and <s>Soma</s>-diseases,
all uterine diseases whatsoever, and intermittent fevers too,

children.text: rajaḥśūlaṃ ca nārīṇāṃ kāsaṃ śvāsaṃ ca hidhmikām // Rcūm_10.128 //
children.translated_text: menstrual pain in women, cough, asthma, and hiccups. // Rcūm 10.128 //
{<s>Mākṣika</s> (pyrites)}
<s>Mākṣika</s> is of two kinds: gold-<s>mākṣika</s> and silver-<s>mākṣika</s>.
{Gold-<s>mākṣika</s>: origin}
Of those, the first, <s>mākṣika</s> originating from <s>Kānyakubja</s>, resembles gold. // Rcūm 10.129 //
{Silver-<s>mākṣika</s>: origin}
Born on the banks of the <s>Tapatī</s> river, of five colors like fine gold;
that which is predominantly stony is called <s>tāpya</s> (pyrites) and has fewer qualities. // Rcūm 10.130 //
{<s>Mākṣika</s>: medicinal properties}

children.text: mākṣīkadhātuḥ sakalāmayaghnaḥ prāṇo rasendrasya paraṃ hi vṛṣyaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s> mineral destroys all diseases, is the life-force of the lord of mercury, supremely aphrodisiac,
it fuses the two inferior metals (<s>durmelaloha</s>), and is the foremost of all rejuvenatives with superior qualities. // Rcūm 10.131 //
{<s>Mākṣika</s> (pyrites): purification}
<s>Mākṣika</s> is purified when treated in castor oil and citron water.
{<s>Mākṣika</s>: purification}

children.text: siddhaṃ ca kadalīkandatoye ca ghaṭikādvayam // Rcūm_10.132 //
children.translated_text: Also, [it is purified when] boiled in plantain-stem juice for two <s>ghaṭikās</s> (48 minutes). // Rcūm 10.132 //
{<s>Mākṣika</s>: purification}
Heated and cast into a decoction of <s>varā</s> (<s>triphalā</s>), <s>mākṣika</s> attains purity.
{<s>Mākṣika</s>: killing (calcination)}
Ground with citron water and sulphur, placed inside a crucible, // Rcūm 10.133 //
<s>mākṣika</s> is truly killed when burnt with five <s>kroḍapuṭas</s> (heap-firings).
{<s>Mākṣika</s>: killing (calcination)}
With castor oil, cow's ghee, and citron juice, // Rcūm 10.134 //
placed on a mica plate and firmly cooked, it becomes metal-like.

children.text: evaṃ mṛtaṃ rase yojyaṃ rasāyanavidhāvapi // Rcūm_10.135 //
children.translated_text: Thus killed, it should be employed with mercury and also in <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation) procedures. // Rcūm 10.135 //
{<s>Mākṣika</s>: essence extraction (<s>sattvapātana</s>)}
Combined with one-thirtieth [its weight of] lead, rolled with alkalis and acids,

children.text: dhmātaṃ prakaṭamūṣāyāṃ sattvaṃ muñcati mākṣikam // Rcūm_10.136 //
children.translated_text: and blown in an open crucible, <s>mākṣika</s> releases its essence (<s>sattva</s>). // Rcūm 10.136 //
{<s>Mākṣika</s>: essence purification}
Melted seven times and cast into <s>nirguṇḍī</s> (Vitex negundo) juice,
the lead mixed with the <s>mākṣika</s> essence is certainly destroyed. // Rcūm 10.137 //
Having the color of <s>guñjā</s> seeds, with a fluid flow like lead —

children.text: tāpyasattvaṃ viśuddhaṃ tu dehalohakaraṃ param // Rcūm_10.138 //
children.translated_text: the purified <s>tāpya</s> (pyrites) essence is supreme for body and metal [transmutation]. // Rcūm 10.138 //
{<s>Mākṣika</s> rejuvenation formula (1)}

children.text: mākṣīkasattvena rasasya piṣṭīṃ kṛtvā vilīne ca baliṃ nidhāya /
children.translated_text: Making a cake of mercury with <s>mākṣika</s> essence, placing an offering in the melted [mixture],

children.text: saṃmiśrya saṃmardya ca khalvamadhye nikṣipya sattvaṃ drutamabhrakasya ca // Rcūm_10.139 //
children.translated_text: mixing and grinding in a mortar, and adding the melted essence of mica — // Rcūm 10.139 //

children.text: vidhāya golaṃ lavaṇākhyayantre paceddinārdhaṃ mṛduvahninā ca /
children.translated_text: making a ball and cooking it in the salt-apparatus for half a day with gentle fire,

children.text: svataḥ suśītaṃ paricūrṇya samyag vallonmitaṃ khaṇḍaviḍaṅgayuktam // Rcūm_10.140 //
children.translated_text: when self-cooled, powdering it properly, measured by a <s>valla</s> (small measure), with <s>khaṇḍa</s> (sugar) and <s>viḍaṅga</s> (Embelia ribes) — // Rcūm 10.140 //

children.text: saṃsevitaṃ kṣaudrayutaṃ nihanti jarāṃ sarogām apamṛtyumeva /
children.translated_text: consumed with honey, it destroys old age along with disease and even untimely death;
in seven doses, it [cures] even incurable diseases — not even nectar equals it. // Rcūm 10.141 //
{<s>Mākṣika</s> rejuvenation formula (2)}
Killed <s>mākṣika</s> mineral, half that [amount of] killed mica,

children.text: tadardhaṃ kāntalohaṃ ca tadardhaṃ tāmrabhasmakam // Rcūm_10.142 //
children.translated_text: half of that [amount of] lodestone, and half of that [amount of] copper ash — // Rcūm 10.142 //
combining all together, one should mix with an equal [amount of] sulphur;
grinding with lemon juice, one should fire it ten times. // Rcūm 10.143 //
With a hundred forest-lotuses, one should triturate the powder
twenty-one times with the juice of <s>vyoṣa</s> (three pungents) and <s>bāhlīka</s> (saffron). // Rcūm 10.144 //
This becomes killed <s>mākṣika</s>, the destroyer of all diseases —

children.text: kṣayaṃ pāṇḍuṃ ca kuṣṭhāni grahaṇīṃ gudajāṃ rujaḥ // Rcūm_10.145 //
children.translated_text: consumption, jaundice, leprosy (<s>kuṣṭha</s>), intestinal diseases (<s>grahaṇī</s>), rectal ailments, // Rcūm 10.145 //
weak digestion, jaundice (<s>kāmalā</s>), wasting (<s>śoṣa</s>), hoarseness, loss of appetite,

children.text: nānārūpān jvarān ugrān āmadoṣaṃ visūcikām // Rcūm_10.146 //
children.translated_text: various fierce fevers, undigested toxins (<s>āmadoṣa</s>), cholera (<s>visūcikā</s>), // Rcūm 10.146 //
and all those diseases arising from <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s> without remainder,
when administered with appropriate vehicles (<s>anupāna</s>) suitable for each condition.

children.text: mahāraseṣu sarveṣu tāpyameva varaṃ matam // Rcūm_10.147 //
children.translated_text: Among all the great minerals (<s>mahārasa</s>), <s>tāpya</s> (pyrites) alone is considered the best. // Rcūm 10.147 //
{Semi-minerals (<s>uparasāḥ</s>)}

Sulphur (<s>gandhāśma</s>), orpiment (<s>tāla</s>), realgar (<s>tuvarī</s>), <s>kunaṭī</s>, antimony (<s>sauvīra</s>), alum (<s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>), mica (<s>khecara</s>), and ochre (<s>gairika</s>) — by these names

children.text: uktā budhairuparasāśca rasāyanāste tairbaddhapāradavaro na rasāyanaḥ syāt // Rcūm_11.1 //
children.translated_text: the semi-minerals (<s>uparasa</s>) are declared by the wise; they are [used for] rejuvenation; mercury bound by them would not be [a proper] rejuvenation [agent]. // Rcūm 11.1 //

body.translated_text: Rcūm, 11

children.translated_text: {Sulphur: subtypes}

children.text: caturdhā gandhako jñeyo varṇaiḥ śvetādibhiḥ khalu /
children.translated_text: Sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>) should be known as fourfold, by colors — white and so forth.
{Sulphur: white}

children.text: śveto'tra khaṭikā prokto lepane lohamāraṇe // Rcūm_11.2 //
children.translated_text: The white [variety] is called chalk-like (<s>khaṭikā</s>), [used] for coating and killing metals. // Rcūm 11.2 //
{Sulphur: yellow}
Likewise, that which is yellow in color is called <s>amalasāra</s> (pure essence);

children.text: śukapicchaḥ sa eva syācchreṣṭho rasarasāyane // Rcūm_11.3 //
children.translated_text: it is also known as parrot-feather (<s>śukapiccha</s>) — the best for mercury and rejuvenation. // Rcūm 11.3 //
{Sulphur: red}
The red [variety], called parrot-beak (<s>śukatuṇḍa</s>), is the best in alchemical (<s>dhātuvāda</s>) procedures.
{Sulphur: black}
The black variety is rare and it is the destroyer of old age and death. // Rcūm 11.4 //
{Sulphur: medicinal properties}

children.text: gandhāśmātirasāyanaḥ samadhuraḥ pāke kaṭūṣṇānvitaḥ kaṇḍūkuṣṭhavisarpadadrudamano dīptānalaḥ pācanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Sulphur (<s>gandhāśma</s>) is a supreme rejuvenative, sweet [in post-digestive taste], pungent and hot in potency; it subdues itching, leprosy (<s>kuṣṭha</s>), erysipelas (<s>visarpa</s>), and ringworm (<s>dadru</s>); it kindles the digestive fire and is digestive;

children.text: āmonmocanaśoṣaṇo viṣaharaḥ sūtendravīryaprado gaurīpuṣpabhavastathā krimiharaḥ sattvātmakaḥ sūtajit // Rcūm_11.5 //
children.translated_text: it releases undigested matter (<s>āma</s>), is desiccant, removes poison, bestows the potency of mercury (<s>sūtendra</s>); born from the flower of <s>Gaurī</s> (Pārvatī), it also destroys worms, is of essential (<s>sattva</s>) nature, and conquers mercury. // Rcūm 11.5 //
{Sulphur: mythological origin}
Formerly consumed by [the demon] <s>Bali</s> for the sake of abundant strength —
as he churned <s>Vāsuki</s> [the serpent], by the flames from his [Vāsuki's] mouth, melted, // Rcūm 11.6 //
the fat rich with the smell of sulphur oozed out from his body on all sides;

children.text: gandhakatvaṃ ca sā prāptā gandho'bhūtsaviṣastataḥ // Rcūm_11.7 //
children.translated_text: that [fat] attained the state of sulphur — hence sulphur became poisonous. // Rcūm 11.7 //
Therefore sulphur is called 'the fat of <s>Bali</s>' (<s>balivasa</s>) — most enchanting.
{Sulphur: purification}

children.text: payaḥsvinno ghaṭīmātraṃ vāridhauto hi gandhakaḥ // Rcūm_11.8 //
children.translated_text: Sulphur steamed in milk for one <s>ghaṭikā</s> (24 minutes) and then washed with water, // Rcūm 11.8 //
melted in cow's ghee and filtered through cloth, attains purity.

children.text: evaṃ saṃśodhitaḥ so'yaṃ pāṣāṇānambare tyajet // Rcūm_11.9 //
children.translated_text: Thus purified, it abandons the poison of minerals in the air. // Rcūm 11.9 //

children.text: ghṛte viṣaṃ tuṣākāraṃ svayaṃ piṇḍatvameti ca /
children.translated_text: The poison in the ghee, husk-like, spontaneously forms into a lump.

children.text: iti śuddho hi gandhāśmā nāgajāṃ vikṛtiṃ tyajet // Rcūm_11.10 //
children.translated_text: Thus purified, the sulphur abandons its lead-born impurity. // Rcūm 11.10 //
If [taken] improperly otherwise, it would kill like swallowed <s>hālāhala</s> poison.
{Sulphur: purification}

children.text: gandhako drāvito bhṛṅgarase kṣipto viśudhyati // Rcūm_11.11 //
children.translated_text: Sulphur melted and cast into <s>bhṛṅga</s> (Eclipta) juice is purified. // Rcūm 11.11 //
Sulphur steamed seven times with those juices becomes fully purified.
{Sulphur purification (3)}

children.text: sthālyāṃ dugdhaṃ vinikṣipya mukhe vastraṃ nibadhya ca // Rcūm_11.12 //
children.translated_text: Having placed milk in a pot and tying cloth over the mouth, // Rcūm 11.12 //
placing powdered sulphur therein, ground to a sandy consistency,
one should cover the sulphur with a broad, long mica plate. // Rcūm 11.13 //
One should kindle fire above the mica plate with dried cow-dung cakes and stones;

children.text: dugdhe nipatito gandho galitvā pariśudhyati // Rcūm_11.14 //
children.translated_text: the sulphur, melting, falls into the milk and is purified. // Rcūm 11.14 //

children.text: itthaṃ viśuddhas triphalājyabhṛṅgamadhvanvitaḥ śāṇamito hi līḍhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus purified, combined with <s>triphalā</s>, ghee, <s>bhṛṅga</s> (Eclipta), and honey, licked in a <s>śāṇa</s> (small) measure,
it makes the pair of eyes equal to a vulture's [in sharpness] and produces long life free from disease. // Rcūm 11.15 //
{Sulphur: flux (<s>druti</s>)}
Sulphur combined with one-sixteenth [its weight of] <s>vyoṣa</s> (three pungents), finely powdered,

children.text: aratnimātre vastre tadviprakīrya viveṣṭya tat // Rcūm_11.16 //
children.translated_text: scattered on a cloth one cubit [in length], rolled up, // Rcūm 11.16 //
wrapped with thread, and then immersed in oil for one <s>yāma</s> (three hours) —

children.text: dhṛtvā saṃdaṃśato vartiṃ sarvāṃ prajvālayettataḥ // Rcūm_11.17 //
children.translated_text: holding the wick with tongs, one should ignite it entirely. // Rcūm 11.17 //
The melted sulphur falls drop by drop into a glass vessel;
that flux (<s>druti</s>), three drops, should be placed on a betel leaf (<s>nāgavallī</s>). // Rcūm 11.18 //

children.text: vallena pramitaṃ śuddhaṃ rasendraṃ ca pramardayet /
children.translated_text: Measured by a <s>valla</s>, purified mercury should be ground [with it],

children.text: aṅgulyātha sapatrāṃ tāṃ drutiṃ sūtaṃ ca bhakṣayet // Rcūm_11.19 //
children.translated_text: and then the flux with mercury on the leaf should be consumed with the finger. // Rcūm 11.19 //

children.text: karoti dīpanaṃ tīvraṃ kṣayaṃ pāṇḍuṃ ca nāśayet /
children.translated_text: It produces intense stimulation of digestion, destroys consumption and jaundice,

children.text: kāsaṃ śvāsaṃ ca śūlārtiṃ grahaṇīmatidustarām // Rcūm_11.20 //
children.translated_text: cough, asthma, colic pain, and the most intractable intestinal disease (<s>grahaṇī</s>). // Rcūm 11.20 //
It quickly destroys undigested toxins (<s>āma</s>) and produces lightness [of body].
{Sulphur: purified: medicinal use}

children.text: ghṛtākte lohapātre tu vidrutaṃ śuddhagandhakam // Rcūm_11.21 //
children.translated_text: In a ghee-smeared iron vessel, melted purified sulphur, // Rcūm 11.21 //
dropped with a ghee-smeared ladle, measured as two <s>niṣkas</s>, should be consumed;
it destroys diseases beginning with consumption, especially leprosy (<s>kuṣṭha</s>). // Rcūm 11.22 //
Alkalis, acids, oil, antimony (<s>sauvīra</s>), burning substances, and split pulses —
