during the regimen of purified sulphur, one should avoid these for the sake of curing disease. // Rcūm 11.23 //
{Sulphur: medicinal use (leprosy)}
Sulphur with an equal [amount of] black pepper, six times [that of] <s>triphalā</s>,
ground with <s>śampāka</s> (Cassia fistula) root and drunk — it destroys all leprosy (<s>kuṣṭha</s>). // Rcūm 11.24 //
That root ground in water should be applied daily to the body;
this is a formula of proven efficacy, unmatched everywhere. // Rcūm 11.25 //
This has been properly proclaimed by the revered <s>Somadeva</s>.
{Sulphur: medicinal use (skin diseases)}

children.text: dviniṣkapramitaṃ gandhaṃ pītvā tailena saṃyutam // Rcūm_11.26 //
children.translated_text: Having drunk sulphur measured as two <s>niṣkas</s>, combined with oil, // Rcūm 11.26 //
then with <s>apāmārga</s> (Achyranthes aspera) water and oil mixed with pepper,

children.text: vilipya sakalaṃ dehaṃ tiṣṭhed gharme tataḥ param // Rcūm_11.27 //
children.translated_text: one should smear the entire body and then stand in the hot sun. // Rcūm 11.27 //

children.text: takrabhaktaṃ ca bhuñjīta tṛtīye prahare khalu /
children.translated_text: One should eat food with buttermilk in the third <s>prahara</s> (watch of the day),

children.text: bhajedrātrau tathā vahniṃ samutthāya tataḥ prage // Rcūm_11.28 //
children.translated_text: and at night should sit near a fire; rising early the next morning, // Rcūm 11.28 //
smearing [the body] with buffalo-dung, one should bathe in cold water;
then anointing the body with ghee, one should bathe with suitably warm water. // Rcūm 11.29 //
By this sequential method, there are destroyed with great speed

children.text: durjayā bahukālīnā pāmā kaṇḍūḥ suniścitam // Rcūm_11.30 //
children.translated_text: the most stubborn, long-standing scabies (<s>pāmā</s>) and itching — this is certain. // Rcūm 11.30 //
The thousands of applications of sulphur have not been proclaimed [here]
by king <s>Somadeva</s>, out of fear of the text's expansion. // Rcūm 11.31 //
{Orpiment (<s>haritāla</s>): subtypes}
Orpiment (<s>haritāla</s>) is said to be twofold: leaf-type (<s>patrākhya</s>) and lump-type (<s>piṇḍasaṃjñita</s>).
{Leaf-orpiment: physical properties}

children.text: svarṇavarṇaṃ guru snigdhaṃ tanupatraṃ ca bhāsuram // Rcūm_11.32 //
children.translated_text: Golden in color, heavy, unctuous, thin-leafed, and lustrous — // Rcūm 11.32 //
{Lump-orpiment: physical properties}
Without leaves, lump-like, of little essence, and heavy,
that which destroys women's [menstrual] flow — that is the less potent lump-orpiment (<s>piṇḍatālaka</s>). // Rcūm 11.33 //

body.translated_text: that is called leaf-orpiment (<s>patratālaka</s>), multi-layered, [and used as] a rejuvenative.

children.translated_text: {Orpiment: medicinal properties}
It removes <s>kapha</s>, <s>vāta</s>, poison, blood [disorders], and evil spirits; alone it destroys the menses of women;

children.text: snigdham uṣṇakaṭukaṃ ca dīpanaṃ kuṣṭhahāri haritālamucyate // Rcūm_11.34 //
children.translated_text: unctuous, hot, pungent, it kindles digestion and destroys leprosy (<s>kuṣṭha</s>) — thus is orpiment (<s>haritāla</s>) described. // Rcūm 11.34 //
{Orpiment: purification}
Steamed in ash-gourd (<s>kūṣmāṇḍa</s>) juice, or in sesame-lye water,

children.text: toye vā cūrṇasaṃyukte dolāyantreṇa śudhyati // Rcūm_11.35 //
children.translated_text: or in water mixed with [herbal] powder, in a <s>dolāyantra</s> (swing-apparatus), it becomes purified. // Rcūm 11.35 //
{Orpiment: essence extraction}
Immersed in horse-gram decoction, <s>saubhāgya</s> (alum), buffalo ghee, and curd,

children.text: sthālyāṃ kṣiptvā pidadhyācca mallena chidrayoginā // Rcūm_11.36 //
children.translated_text: placed in a pot and covered with a cup-crucible (<s>malla</s>) having an opening, // Rcūm 11.36 //
sealing properly, one should kindle fire gradually increasing;
for one <s>prahara</s> (three hours) only, covering the opening with cow-dung. // Rcūm 11.37 //

children.text: yāmānte chidramudghāṭya dṛṣṭe dhūme ca pāṇḍure /
children.translated_text: At the end of one <s>yāma</s>, opening the hole, when white smoke is seen,

children.text: śītāṃ sthālīṃ samuttārya sattvamutkṛṣya cāharet // Rcūm_11.38 //
children.translated_text: lifting the cooled pot, one should extract and collect the essence (<s>sattva</s>). // Rcūm 11.38 //
The methods for essences of all minerals exist in the millions;

children.text: granthavistārabhītyā te likhitā na mayā khalu // Rcūm_11.39 //
children.translated_text: out of fear of the text's expansion, they have not been written by me. // Rcūm 11.39 //
What is easy to do everywhere, readily available, and productive of results
regarding mercury, semi-minerals, and metals — only that is stated here. // Rcūm 11.40 //
{Leaf-orpiment: essence extraction}
One should grind leaf-orpiment with <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) milk for one day,

children.text: kṣiptvā ṣoḍaśikāṃ taile miśrayitvā tataḥ pacet // Rcūm_11.41 //
children.translated_text: place it in a sixteenth [measure] of oil, mix, and then cook — // Rcūm 11.41 //
in an uncovered place, for seven <s>yāmas</s> (twenty-one hours), certainly;

children.text: svāṅgaśītamadhaḥsthaṃ ca sattvaṃ śvetaṃ samāharet // Rcūm_11.42 //
children.translated_text: when self-cooled, one should collect the white essence settled below. // Rcūm 11.42 //
{Orpiment: essence extraction}
Combined with the dung of a young goat,
grinding the orpiment for two days with effort, // Rcūm 11.43 //
mixed with the melting-group [of substances], one should place it in a glass flask;

children.text: tridhā tāṃ ca mṛdā liptvā pariśoṣya kharātape // Rcūm_11.44 //
children.translated_text: coating the flask thrice with clay and drying in fierce sunlight, // Rcūm 11.44 //
then inserting half of the flask into a hole in a mica plate,
one should kindle fire for up to twelve <s>praharas</s> (thirty-six hours). // Rcūm 11.45 //

children.text: kūpīkaṇṭhe sthitaṃ sattvaṃ śubhraṃ śīte samāharet /
children.translated_text: The bright essence settled in the neck of the flask should be collected when cool. // Rcūm 11.46a //
{Orpiment: essence extraction}

children.text: palārdhapramitaṃ tālaṃ baddhvā vastre site dṛḍhe // Rcūm_11.46 //
children.translated_text: Measuring half a <s>pala</s> of orpiment, tying it firmly in a white cloth, // Rcūm 11.46 //
carefully smearing with <s>balinā</s> (a paste) and drying three times,
when three <s>palas</s> of copper are melted, one should cast the orpiment bolus [into it]. // Rcūm 11.47 //
One should quickly cover it with ash, wrapped in copper, white,
and collect the soft essence — as stated in the treatise on mercury and rasāyana. // Rcūm 11.48 //
{<s>Tuvarī</s>: origin}
The mineral clay born from the mines of <s>Saurāṣṭra</s> is regarded as <s>tuvarī</s>;
it is applied to fabrics and binds the color of <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s> (madder). // Rcūm 11.49 //
{<s>Tuvarī</s>: subtypes}
<s>Phaṭikā</s> and <s>phullikā</s> — thus two varieties are proclaimed.
{<s>Phaṭikā</s>: physical and medicinal properties}
Slightly yellow, heavy, unctuous — <s>pīṭikā</s> is a destroyer of poison. // Rcūm 11.50 //
{<s>Phullikā</s>: physical and medicinal properties}

children.text: nirbhārā śubhravarṇā ca snigdhā sāmlā parā matā /
children.translated_text: Lightweight, white in color, unctuous, and slightly sour — the superior one is regarded;

children.text: sā phullatuvarī proktā lepācchīghraṃ caredayaḥ // Rcūm_11.51 //
children.translated_text: she is called <s>phullatuvarī</s> — through its application, iron quickly becomes malleable. // Rcūm 11.51 //

body.translated_text: It removes wounds and leprosy, and is especially a destroyer of all skin diseases.

children.translated_text: {<s>Tuvarī</s>: medicinal properties}

children.text: kāṅkṣī kaṣāyā kaṭukāmlakaṇṭhyā keśyā vraṇaghnī viṣanāśinī ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Kāṅkṣī</s> (alum), astringent, pungent, sour, beneficial for the throat, good for hair, wound-healing, and poison-destroying,

children.text: śvitrāpahā netrahitā tridoṣaśāntipradā pāradajāriṇī ca // Rcūm_11.52 //
children.translated_text: it removes <s>śvitra</s> (leucoderma), is beneficial for the eyes, pacifies the three <s>doṣas</s>, and is an enemy of mercury's impurities. // Rcūm 11.52 //
{Purification of <s>tuvarī</s>}
<s>Tuvarī</s> immersed in <s>kāñjika</s> (sour gruel) attains purity in three days.
{<s>Tuvarī</s>: extraction of essence (<s>sattva</s>)}

children.text: kṣārāmlairmarditā dhmātā sattvaṃ muñcati niścitam // Rcūm_11.53 //
children.translated_text: Triturated with alkalis and acids and then heated, it certainly releases its essence. // Rcūm 11.53 //
{<s>Manaḥśilā</s> (realgar): subtypes}
<s>Manaḥśilā</s> (realgar) is declared to be of three kinds: <s>śyāmāṅgī</s>, <s>kaṇavīrikā</s>,

children.text: khaṇḍākhyā ceti tadrūpaṃ vivicya parikathyate // Rcūm_11.54 //
children.translated_text: and <s>khaṇḍā</s> — their respective forms are now described in detail. // Rcūm 11.54 //
{<s>Śyāmāṅgī</s>: physical properties}

children.text: śyāmā raktā sagaurā ca bhārāḍhyā śyāmikā matā /
children.translated_text: Dark, reddish, with some whiteness, and heavy — this is regarded as <s>śyāmikā</s>.
{<s>Kaṇavīrikā</s>: physical properties}

children.text: tejasvinī ca nirgaurā tāmrābhā kaṇavīrikā // Rcūm_11.55 //
children.translated_text: Lustrous, without whiteness, copper-hued — this is <s>kaṇavīrikā</s>. // Rcūm 11.55 //
{<s>Khaṇḍa</s>: physical properties}
Powdery, very red-bodied, heavy — this is <s>khaṇḍā</s>;
each succeeding variety is superior, and is proclaimed to be rich in essence. // Rcūm 11.56 //
{<s>Manaḥśilā</s>: medicinal properties}
<s>Manaḥśilā</s> is foremost among all <s>rasāyanas</s>; it is bitter, pungent, hot, and destroys <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>;
it is of the nature of essence (<s>sattva</s>) and removes evil spirits, poison, digestive weakness, itching, skin eruptions (<s>koṭha</s>), and wasting diseases. // Rcūm 11.57 //
{<s>Manaḥśilā</s>: purification}
Steeped seven times in the juice of <s>agastya</s> (sesbania) leaves,
or in the juice of ginger (<s>śṛṅgavera</s>) — <s>manaḥśilā</s> becomes purified. // Rcūm 11.58 //
{<s>Manaḥśilā</s>: extraction of essence}
With one-eighth part of iron slag (<s>kiṭṭa</s>), jaggery, <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium), and ghee,

children.text: koṣṭhyāṃ ruddhvā dṛḍhaṃ dhmātā sattvaṃ muñcenmanaḥśilā // Rcūm_11.59 //
children.translated_text: sealed firmly in a crucible and heated strongly — <s>manaḥśilā</s> releases its essence. // Rcūm 11.59 //
{<s>Manaḥśilā</s>: extraction of essence [alternate method]}
With <s>bhūnāga</s>, <s>dhauta</s>, <s>saubhāgya</s>, and <s>madana</s>, triturated,
a crucible is made with the juice of <s>kāravellī</s> (bitter gourd) leaves, and [the substance] is placed in it. // Rcūm 11.60 //
The <s>śilā</s> (realgar), ground with alkalis and acids, should then be heated;

children.text: ghaṭikādvayamātraṃ hi dhmātā sattvaṃ tyajatyasau // Rcūm_11.61 //
children.translated_text: when heated for a period of two <s>ghaṭikās</s> (48 minutes), it releases its essence. // Rcūm 11.61 //
{<s>Añjana</s> (collyrium): subtypes}
<s>Sauvīra</s> is the [first] collyrium declared; after that, <s>rasāñjana</s>,
<s>sroto'ñjana</s>, and another — <s>puṣpāñjana</s>,

children.text: nīlāñjanaṃ hi teṣāṃ ca svarūpamiha varṇyate // Rcūm_11.62 //
children.translated_text: and <s>nīlāñjana</s> (blue antimony) — the nature of these is now described. // Rcūm 11.62 //
{<s>Sauvīra</s>: physical properties}
<s>Sauvīra</s> collyrium is smoky-grey, cooling, and removes <s>raktapitta</s> (blood-bile disorder);
it destroys vomiting, hiccups, and eye diseases, and purifies and heals wounds. // Rcūm 11.63 //
{<s>Rasāñjana</s>: physical and medicinal properties}
<s>Rasāñjana</s> is yellowish in appearance, and removes poison, blood disorders, and diseases;
it removes asthma and hiccups, improves complexion, and destroys <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and blood [disorders]. // Rcūm 11.64 //
{<s>Sroto'ñjana</s>: medicinal properties}

children.text: sroto'ñjanaṃ himaṃ snigdhaṃ kaṣāyaṃ svādu lekhanam /
children.translated_text: <s>Sroto'ñjana</s> is cooling, unctuous, astringent, sweet, and scraping;
beneficial for the eyes, it destroys hiccups, poison, vomiting, <s>kapha</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and blood disorders. // Rcūm 11.65 //
{<s>Puṣpāñjana</s>: medicinal properties}
<s>Puṣpāñjana</s> is white, unctuous, cooling, and removes all eye diseases;
it destroys extremely stubborn hiccups, and removes poison, fever, and diseases. // Rcūm 11.66 //
{<s>Nīlāñjana</s>: medicinal properties}
<s>Nīlāñjana</s> is heavy, unctuous, beneficial for the eyes, and removes the three <s>doṣas</s>;
it is a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative), a destroyer of gold [impurities], and softens metals. // Rcūm 11.67 //
{<s>Añjana</s>: purification}
Collyriums are purified with the juice of <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> (eclipta) leaves.
{<s>Añjana</s>: extraction of essence}
The essence of collyriums should be collected in the same manner as that of <s>manaḥśilā</s>. // Rcūm 11.68 //
{<s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s>: place of discovery}
<s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s> is produced on the foothills of the <s>Himavat</s> (Himālaya).
{<s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s>: subtypes}

children.text: tatraikaṃ nalikākhyaṃ hi tadanyadreṇukaṃ matam // Rcūm_11.69 //
children.translated_text: One variety is called <s>nalikā</s>, and the other is regarded as <s>reṇuka</s>. // Rcūm 11.69 //
{<s>Nalikā</s>: physical properties}
Yellow-hued, heavy, unctuous — the first <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> is the best.
{<s>Reṇuka</s>: physical properties}

children.text: śyāmaṃ pītaṃ laghu tyaktasattvaṃ neṣṭaṃ hi reṇukam // Rcūm_11.70 //
children.translated_text: Dark, yellowish, light, and devoid of essence — <s>reṇuka</s> is undesirable. // Rcūm 11.70 //
{<s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s>: origin from feces}
Some say that <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> is the feces of a newly-born elephant;

children.text: varcaḥ sa śyāmapītābhaṃ recanaṃ parikathyate // Rcūm_11.71 //
children.translated_text: that is dark-yellowish and is described as a purgative. // Rcūm 11.71 //
Others say that the tube (<s>nāla</s>) of certain fire-carriers (fireflies) is called <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>;
they say it is white-yellowish and exceedingly purgative. // Rcūm 11.72 //
{<s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s>: medicinal properties}
Excellent in mercury and <s>rasāyana</s> [operations], [but when] devoid of essence, it causes many disorders;
<s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> is bitter and pungent, hot in potency, and strongly purgative. // Rcūm 11.73 //
It removes wounds, <s>udāvarta</s> (upward displacement), colic pain, tumors (<s>gulma</s>), splenic diseases, and rectal pain.
{<s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s>: purification}
<s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s> attains purity by being steeped thrice in the best water (<s>triphalā</s> decoction). // Rcūm 11.74 //
{<s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s>: extraction of essence}

children.text: sattvākarṣo'sya na prokto yasmātsattvamayaṃ hi tat /
children.translated_text: Extraction of its essence is not prescribed, since it is itself entirely of the nature of essence.
{<s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s>: medicinal use}
For the purpose of purgation, one should administer it in a barley-grain dose with binding substances. // Rcūm 11.75 //
It destroys indigestion and congestion, purging within a moment;
consumed together with betel (<s>tāmbūla</s>), it purges and swiftly destroys [the ailment]. // Rcūm 11.76 //
A decoction of <s>barbūrī</s> root, cumin (<s>jīra</s>), and <s>saubhāgya</s> in equal parts —
a person should drink it again and again to counteract the toxic effects of <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>. // Rcūm 11.77 //
{<s>Vālukā-kāsīsa</s>: medicinal properties}
Alkaline, sour, heavy, smoky in color, hot in potency, and poison-destroying —
the sand-type <s>kāsīsa</s> destroys <s>śvitra</s> (leucoderma) and dyes the hair. // Rcūm 11.78 //

body.translated_text:
{<s>Kāsīsa</s> (green vitriol): subtypes}
<s>Kāsīsa</s> is of two kinds: one beginning with <s>vālukā</s> (sand-like), and the other preceded by <s>puṣpa</s> (flower-like).

children.translated_text: {<s>Puṣpa-kāsīsa</s>: medicinal properties}
The flower-type <s>kāsīsa</s> is very well-known; it is hot, astringent, sour, and exceedingly beneficial for the eyes;
it destroys poison, <s>vāta</s>, <s>kapha</s> diseases, wounds, <s>śvitra</s> (leucoderma), and wasting — and it dyes the hair. // Rcūm 11.79 //
{<s>Kāsīsa</s>: purification}

children.text: sakṛd bhṛṅgāmbunā klinnaṃ kāsīsaṃ nirmalaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: Once moistened with <s>bhṛṅga</s> (eclipta) water, <s>kāsīsa</s> becomes pure.
{<s>Kāsīsa</s>: extraction of essence}
Its essence should be collected in the same manner as that of <s>tuvarī</s>. // Rcūm 11.80 //
{Administration of <s>kāsīsa</s>}
<s>Kāsīsa</s> killed by <s>balin</s> (strong substances), and <s>kānta</s> (magnetic iron) killed by <s>kāsīsa</s> —
both in equal parts, combined with <s>triphalā</s> and cardamom (<s>vella</s>), // Rcūm 11.81 //
immersed in unequal parts of ghee and honey, in a <s>śāṇa</s>-measure dose, taken in the morning —
when consumed, it swiftly destroys <s>śvitra</s> (leucoderma), <s>pāṇḍu</s> (anemia), and wasting diseases. // Rcūm 11.82 //
It [also destroys] tumors (<s>gulma</s>), splenic disease, colic, and urinary diseases completely,
when administered by the <s>rasāyana</s> method for up to a year. // Rcūm 11.83 //
It is excellent for drying up undigested matter (<s>āma</s>), stimulates sluggish digestion,

children.text: palitaṃ valibhiḥ sārdhaṃ vināśayati niścitam // Rcūm_11.84 //
children.translated_text: and certainly destroys grey hair along with wrinkles. // Rcūm 11.84 //
{<s>Gairika</s> (ochre): subtypes}
One is stone-ochre (<s>pāṣāṇa-gairika</s>), and the second is gold-ochre (<s>svarṇa-gairika</s>).
{Stone-ochre: physical properties}
Stone-ochre is described as hard and copper-colored. // Rcūm 11.85 //

children.text: svādu snigdhaṃ himaṃ netryaṃ kaṣāyaṃ raktapittanut // Rcūm_11.86 //
children.translated_text: Sweet, unctuous, cooling, beneficial for the eyes, astringent — it removes <s>raktapitta</s> (blood-bile disorder). // Rcūm 11.86 //

body.translated_text: {Stone-ochre: medicinal properties}

children.translated_text: {Gold-ochre: medicinal properties}
Gold-ochre destroys hiccups, vomiting, and poison, and is a blood-purifier;
the other stone-ochre is inferior in qualities to the former. // Rcūm 11.87 //
{<s>Gairika</s>: purification}

children.text: gairikaṃ hi gavāṃ dugdhairbhāvitaṃ śuddhim ṛcchati /
children.translated_text: Ochre, steeped in cow's milk, attains purity.
{<s>Gairika</s>: extraction of essence}

children.text: gairikaṃ sattvarūpaṃ hi nandinā parikīrtitam // Rcūm_11.88 //
children.translated_text: Ochre is proclaimed by <s>Nandin</s> to be of the very nature of essence. // Rcūm 11.88 //
Some say that essence can be extracted from ochre steamed with alkalis and acids;
it unites with the lord of mercury, becoming one and endowed with superior qualities. // Rcūm 11.89 //
{The ordinary minerals (<s>sādhāraṇarasas</s>)}
<s>Kampilla</s>, and another — <s>gaurīpāṣāṇa</s>, <s>navasāra</s> (sal ammoniac),
<s>kaparda</s> (cowrie), <s>agnijāra</s> (ambergris), <s>girisindūra</s> (mountain-cinnabar), and <s>hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar), // Rcūm 11.90 //
and <s>boddāraśṛṅga</s> — these eight are regarded as ordinary minerals (<s>sādhāraṇa-rasas</s>);
they are declared to be effectors of success with mercury by those led by <s>Nāgārjuna</s>. // Rcūm 11.91 //
{<s>Kampilla</s>: physical properties and place of discovery}
Resembling brick-powder, rich in crystals, and strongly purgative,

children.text: saurāṣṭradeśasambhūtaḥ sa hi kampillako mataḥ // Rcūm_11.92 //
children.translated_text: born in the land of <s>Saurāṣṭra</s> — that is regarded as <s>kampillaka</s>. // Rcūm 11.92 //
{<s>Kampilla</s>: medicinal properties}
It destroys <s>pitta</s>, wounds, flatulence, and constipation; it opposes <s>kapha</s>, abdominal pain, parasites, and tumors (<s>gulma</s>);
it removes piles (<s>mūla</s>), indigestion, colic, fever, and swelling — <s>kampillaka</s> is a purgative that removes diseases. // Rcūm 11.93 //
{<s>Gaurīpāṣāṇa</s> (orpiment): physical properties}
<s>Gaurīpāṣāṇa</s> is yellow, rough, and powdery when crushed.
{<s>Gaurīpāṣāṇa</s>: medicinal properties}
It effects the binding of mercury, is unctuous, destroys <s>doṣas</s>, and enhances the potency of mercury. // Rcūm 11.94 //
{<s>Navasāra</s> (sal ammoniac): production}
It is produced when the wood of <s>karīra</s> (caper) and <s>pīlu</s> trees is being burned;
that alkali is <s>navasāra</s>, also called <s>cūlikā</s> salt. // Rcūm 11.95 //
The pale, light salt produced during the burning of bricks —

children.text: taduktaṃ navasārākhyaṃ cūlikālavaṇaṃ ca tat // Rcūm_11.96 //
children.translated_text: that is called <s>navasāra</s>, which is also <s>cūlikā</s> salt. // Rcūm 11.96 //
{<s>Navasāra</s>: medicinal properties}
It digests the lord of mercury, fluxes metals, and stimulates the digestive fire;
it destroys tumors (<s>gulma</s>), splenic disease, and oral dryness, and digests consumed meat and other [foods];

children.text: viḍākhyaṃ ca tridoṣaghnaṃ cūlikālavaṇaṃ matam // Rcūm_11.97 //
children.translated_text: called <s>viḍa</s> salt, it destroys the three <s>doṣas</s> — such is <s>cūlikā</s> salt. // Rcūm 11.97 //
{Money cowrie: physical properties}
Yellowish, with a knob on the back, with a long stalk — the cowrie (<s>varāṭikā</s>)
is designated by mercury-physicians as <s>carācara</s> (the moving-and-unmoving). // Rcūm 11.98 //
{Money cowrie: testing (<s>parīkṣā</s>)}
One weighing one and a half <s>niṣka</s>s is the best; one <s>niṣka</s> is medium;
and one weighing three-quarters of a <s>niṣka</s> is declared the lowest. // Rcūm 11.99 //
{Money cowrie: medicinal properties}
It destroys colic caused by indigestion (<s>pariṇāma</s>) and the like, destroys <s>grahaṇī</s> (irritable bowel) and wasting diseases;

children.text: kaṭūṣṇā dīpanī vṛṣyā netryā vātakaphāpahā // Rcūm_11.100 //
children.translated_text: it is pungent, hot, appetizing, aphrodisiac, good for the eyes, and removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>. // Rcūm 11.100 //
It is prescribed for digesting the lord of mercury, and recommended among <s>biḍa</s> substances.
{Cowries (in general): medicinal properties}

children.text: tadanye tu varāṭāḥ syur guravaḥ śleṣmapittalāḥ // Rcūm_11.101 //
children.translated_text: Other cowries are heavy and aggravate <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>. // Rcūm 11.101 //

children.text: hatvā hatvā guṇān bhūyo vikārān kurvate na hi /
children.translated_text: After being killed repeatedly, they further enhance their qualities and do not produce disorders.
{Money cowrie: purification}
Cowries steamed in <s>kāñjika</s> (sour gruel) for one <s>yāma</s> (three hours) attain purity. // Rcūm 11.102 //
{<s>Agnijāra</s> (ambergris): origin}
The afterbirth (<s>jarāyu</s>) of the fire-crocodile (<s>agninakra</s>) cast out by the ocean,

children.text: saṃśuṣko bhānutāpena so'gnijāra iti smṛtaḥ // Rcūm_11.103 //
children.translated_text: dried by the heat of the sun — that is known as <s>agnijāra</s> (ambergris). // Rcūm 11.103 //
{<s>Agnijāra</s>: medicinal properties}
<s>Agnijāra</s> destroys the three <s>doṣas</s>, removes <s>dhanurvāta</s> (tetanus) and other <s>vāta</s> disorders;
it increases the potency of mercury, is digestive-stimulant, and a digestor (<s>jāraṇa</s>). // Rcūm 11.104 //

body.translated_text:
{<s>Agnijāra</s>: purification}
Since it is already purified by the salt of the ocean, no [further] purification is desired.

children.translated_text: {<s>Girisindūra</s> (mountain-cinnabar): origin}
In great mountains, mercury that is small and situated inside stones,

children.text: śuṣkaḥ śoṇaḥ sa nirdiṣṭo rasasindūrasaṃjñayā // Rcūm_11.105 //
children.translated_text: dry and red — that is designated by the name <s>rasasindūra</s> (mountain cinnabar). // Rcūm 11.105 //
{<s>Girisindūra</s> (mountain cinnabar): medicinal properties}
It pacifies all three <s>doṣas</s>, is purgative, and foremost in binding mercury;
<s>girisindūra</s> is said to be a transformer of body and metals, and beneficial for the eyes. // Rcūm 11.106 //
{<s>Hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar): subtypes}
<s>Hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar) has two varieties: <s>śukatuṇḍa</s> (parrot-beak) and the other called <s>haṃsapāka</s>.
{<s>Śukatuṇḍa</s>: properties}
The first is of lesser quality; it is called a leather-worker (<s>carmāra</s>) [among cinnabar]. // Rcūm 11.107 //
{<s>Haṃsapāka</s>: physical properties}
Having white streaks and coral-like luster — that is called <s>haṃsapāka</s>.
{<s>Darada</s> (cinnabar ore): medicinal properties}
<s>Hiṅgula</s> destroys all diseases, is appetizing, and a supreme <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative). // Rcūm 11.108 //
It removes all diseases, is aphrodisiac, and especially praised for <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion of metals).
{<s>Hiṅgulākṛṣṭa</s> (mercury extracted from cinnabar)}
Mercury extracted from this is equal in qualities to mercury that has digested sulfur (<s>jīrṇagandha</s>). // Rcūm 11.109 //
{<s>Darada</s>: purification}
Seven times [soaked] with juice of fresh ginger (<s>ārdraka</s>), or with the juice of <s>lakuca</s> (breadfruit),

children.text: śoṣito bhāvayitvā ca nirdoṣo jāyate khalu // Rcūm_11.110 //
children.translated_text: dried after imbuing — it certainly becomes free of defects. // Rcūm 11.110 //
{<s>Boddāraśṛṅga</s>: place of discovery}
Having layers and of yellow color, it is found in the <s>Gujarat</s> region,

children.text: arbudasya gireḥ pārśve jātaṃ boddāraśṛṅgakam // Rcūm_11.111 //
children.translated_text: near the <s>Arbuda</s> mountain (Mt. Abu) — it is called <s>boddāraśṛṅga</s>. // Rcūm 11.111 //
{<s>Udāraśṛṅga</s>: medicinal properties}
It contains the essence of lead, pacifies wind (<s>marut</s>) and phlegm (<s>śleṣman</s>), and removes piles (<s>puṃgada</s>);
it is excellent for binding mercury and supreme for dyeing hair. // Rcūm 11.112 //
{<s>Sādhāraṇarasa</s> (common minerals): purification}
All common minerals, [when soaked] in citron (<s>mātuluṅga</s>) juice and water,
three times imbued and dried, become free from defects. // Rcūm 11.113 //
{<s>Sādhāraṇarasa</s> essences: purification}

children.text: yāni kāni ca sattvāni tāni śudhyantyaśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever essences (<s>sattvas</s>) there may be, they are all purified completely

children.text: dhmātāni śuddhivargeṇa milanti ca parasparam // Rcūm_11.114 //
children.translated_text: when smelted with the purifying group; and they combine with one another. // Rcūm 11.114 //
{Jewels}

children.text: māṇikyamuktāphalavidrumāṇi tārkṣyaṃ ca puṣpaṃ bhiduraṃ ca nīlam /
children.translated_text: Ruby (<s>māṇikya</s>), pearl (<s>muktāphala</s>), coral (<s>vidruma</s>), emerald (<s>tārkṣya</s>), topaz (<s>puṣpa</s>), diamond (<s>bhidura</s>), sapphire (<s>nīla</s>),

children.text: gomedakaṃ cātha vidūrakaṃ ca krameṇa ratnāni navagrahāṇām // Rcūm_12.1 //
children.translated_text: hessonite (<s>gomedaka</s>), and cat's eye (<s>vidūraka</s>) — these are the nine gems corresponding to the nine planets. // Rcūm 12.1 //

body.translated_text: <s>Rasendracūḍāmaṇi</s>, Chapter 12

children.translated_text: According to planetary friendship: ruby (<s>kuruvinda</s>), topaz (<s>puṣpa</s>), coral (<s>pravāla</s>), pearl (<s>muktāphala</s>), emerald (<s>tārkṣya</s>), diamond (<s>vajra</s>),
sapphire (<s>nīla</s>), hessonite (<s>gomeda</s>), and cat's eye (<s>vidūraka</s>) — worn in order as rings, they bring the fulfillment of one's desires. // Rcūm 12.2 //

children.text: rase rasāyane dāne dhāraṇe ca devatārcane /
children.translated_text: In alchemical processing, <s>rasāyana</s>, gift-giving, wearing, and worship of deities,
gems that are well-formed and of good lineage are prescribed for success. // Rcūm 12.3 //
{Ruby: subtypes}
<s>Māṇikya</s> (ruby) is of two kinds: <s>padmarāga</s> (lotus-colored) and the second, <s>nīlagandhi</s> (blue-scented).
{Ruby: examination — good quality}

children.text: śītaṃ kuśeśayacchāyaṃ svacchaṃ snigdhaṃ guru sphuṭam // Rcūm_12.4 //
children.translated_text: Cool, having the hue of a lotus (<s>kuśeśaya</s>), transparent, smooth, heavy, brilliant, // Rcūm 12.4 //
{<s>Nīlagandhi</s>: examination}
Blue, born from the waters of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, with a blue core and reddish hue —
excellent like the previously described ruby — that ruby is the <s>nīlagandhi</s> type. // Rcūm 12.5 //

body.translated_text: round or oval, of even body — such a ruby is said to be the best.

children.translated_text: {Ruby: examination — bad quality}
Having holes, roughness, dullness, dryness, pallor,

children.text: cipiṭaṃ laghu vakraṃ ca māṇikyaṃ duṣṭam aṣṭadhā // Rcūm_12.6 //
children.translated_text: flat, light, and crooked — a ruby defective in eight ways. // Rcūm 12.6 //
{Ruby: medicinal properties}
Ruby is appetizing, aphrodisiac, and removes phlegm (<s>kapha</s>), wind (<s>vāta</s>), wasting diseases, and pain;
it destroys spirits (<s>bhūta</s>), vampires (<s>vetāla</s>), and sins, and eradicates diseases born of past karma. // Rcūm 12.7 //
{Pearl (<s>mauktika</s>): examination — good quality}

children.text: hlādi śvetaṃ laghu snigdhaṃ raśmivannirmalaṃ mahat /
children.translated_text: Delightful, white, light, smooth, radiant like rays, spotless, large,

children.text: khyātaṃ toyaprabhaṃ vṛttaṃ mauktikaṃ navadhā śubham // Rcūm_12.8 //
children.translated_text: renowned for its water-like luster, round — a pearl is auspicious in nine ways. // Rcūm 12.8 //
{Pearl: examination — bad quality}
Rough-bodied, lacking luster, dark, copper-hued, salt-like,

children.text: ardhaśubhraṃ ca vikaṭaṃ granthilaṃ mauktikaṃ tyajet // Rcūm_12.9 //
children.translated_text: half-white, misshapen, and knotted — such a pearl should be rejected. // Rcūm 12.9 //
{Pearl: medicinal properties}
It destroys phlegm, bile, and wasting disease; removes cough, asthma, and digestive weakness;

children.text: puṣṭidaṃ vṛṣyamāyuṣyaṃ dāhaghnaṃ mauktikaṃ matam // Rcūm_12.10 //
children.translated_text: pearl is considered nourishing, aphrodisiac, life-prolonging, and heat-relieving. // Rcūm 12.10 //
{Coral: examination — good quality}
Having the hue of a ripe <s>bimba</s> fruit, round or oval, not crooked,

children.text: snigdham avraṇakaṃ sthūlaṃ pravālaṃ saptadhā matam // Rcūm_12.11 //
children.translated_text: smooth, without blemish, thick — coral is considered meritorious in seven ways. // Rcūm 12.11 //
{Coral: examination — bad quality}
Pale, grey, rough, blemished, with hollows,

children.text: nirbhāraṃ śubhravarṇaṃ ca pravālaṃ neṣyate'ṣṭadhā // Rcūm_12.12 //
children.translated_text: lightweight, and bright-white in color — coral is undesirable in eight ways. // Rcūm 12.12 //
{Coral: medicinal properties}
Coral destroys wasting disease, bile disorders, blood diseases, and cough; it is appetizing, digestive, and light;
it pacifies poison, spirits (<s>bhūta</s>), and such, and <s>vidruma</s> (coral) removes eye diseases. // Rcūm 12.13 //
{Emerald: examination — good quality}
Yellow-green in color, heavy, smooth, with radiating beams of light, auspicious,

children.text: masṛṇaṃ bhāsuraṃ tārkṣyaṃ gātraṃ saptaguṇaṃ matam // Rcūm_12.14 //
children.translated_text: soft, lustrous — <s>tārkṣya</s> (emerald) with an even body is considered meritorious in seven ways. // Rcūm 12.14 //
{Emerald: examination — bad quality}

children.text: kapiśaṃ karkaśaṃ nīlaṃ pāṇḍu kṛṣṇaṃ salāghavam /
children.translated_text: Brownish, rough, blue, pale, black, lightweight,

children.text: cipiṭaṃ vikaṭaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ rūkṣaṃ tārkṣyaṃ na śasyate // Rcūm_12.15 //
children.translated_text: flat, misshapen, dark, and dry — such an emerald (<s>tārkṣya</s>) is not approved. // Rcūm 12.15 //
{Emerald: medicinal properties}
It removes fever, vomiting, poison, asthma, <s>sannipāta</s> (combined derangement), and digestive weakness;
<s>tārkṣya</s> (emerald) destroys fistula (<s>durnāma</s>), anemia (<s>pāṇḍu</s>), and edema (<s>śopha</s>), and increases vitality (<s>ojas</s>). // Rcūm 12.16 //
{Topaz (<s>puṣparāga</s>): examination — good quality}

children.text: puṣparāgaṃ guru snigdhaṃ svacchaṃ sthūlaṃ samaṃ mṛdu /
children.translated_text: Topaz that is heavy, smooth, transparent, thick, even, soft,
having the hue of <s>karṇikāra</s> (Pterospermum) blossoms, and polished is auspicious in eight ways. // Rcūm 12.17 //
{Topaz: examination — bad quality}

children.text: niṣprabhaṃ karkaśaṃ rūkṣaṃ pītaṃ śyāmaṃ natonnatam /
children.translated_text: Lustreless, rough, dry, [merely] yellow, dark, uneven,

children.text: kapilaṃ kapiśaṃ pāṇḍu puṣparāgaṃ parityajet // Rcūm_12.18 //
children.translated_text: tawny, brownish, and pale — such a topaz should be abandoned. // Rcūm 12.18 //
{Topaz: medicinal properties}
Topaz removes poison, vomiting, phlegm, wind, and digestive weakness;
it pacifies burning sensations and skin diseases, and is appetizing, light, and digestive. // Rcūm 12.19 //
{Diamond (<s>vajra</s>): subtypes by gender}

children.text: vajraṃ ca trividhaṃ proktaṃ naro nārī napuṃsakam /
children.translated_text: Diamond is said to be of three types: male, female, and neuter;
each preceding one is far superior in <s>rasa</s> (essence), <s>vīrya</s> (potency), and <s>vipāka</s> (post-digestive effect). // Rcūm 12.20 //
{Diamond: male (<s>puṃvajra</s>)}
Eight-edged, with eight facets, hexagonal, extremely brilliant,
resembling water, the rainbow, and clouds — the male diamond is called <s>puṃvajra</s>. // Rcūm 12.21 //
{Female diamond (<s>strīvajra</s>)}
The same, but flat in shape, round-oval — that is the female diamond (<s>strīvajra</s>).
{Neuter diamond (<s>napuṃsaka</s>)}
Round, with blunt edges, and somewhat heavy — that is the neuter [diamond]. // Rcūm 12.22 //
Female, male, and neuter diamonds should be employed for female, male, and neuter [patients respectively];

children.text: vyatyāsānnaiva phaladaṃ puṃvajreṇa vinā kvacit // Rcūm_12.23 //
children.translated_text: if interchanged, they are not fruit-giving — without the male diamond, never effective anywhere. // Rcūm 12.23 //
{Diamond: subtypes by color}
Each type is further fourfold according to color distinctions beginning with white:
<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Kṣatriya</s>, <s>Vaiśya</s>, and <s>Śūdra</s> — each grants fruits appropriate to its own class. // Rcūm 12.24 //
The higher-colored one is indeed fruit-granting even for the lower class;
this principle, declared by <s>Bhairava</s>, applies to all substances whatsoever. // Rcūm 12.25 //
{Diamond: medicinal properties}

children.text: āyuṣpradaṃ jhaṭiti sadguṇadaṃ ca vṛṣyaṃ doṣatrayapraśamanaṃ sakalāmayaghnam /
children.translated_text: Life-giving, quickly bestowing good qualities, aphrodisiac, pacifying all three <s>doṣas</s>, destroying all diseases,

children.text: sūtendrabandhavadhasadguṇakṛt pradīpi mṛtyuṃ jayed amṛtopamayeva vajram // Rcūm_12.26 //
children.translated_text: producing the good qualities of binding and killing the lord of mercury, appetizing — diamond conquers death like ambrosia itself. // Rcūm 12.26 //
{Jewels: five common defects}
<s>Grāsa</s> (eclipse), <s>trāsa</s> (fright), <s>bindu</s> (spot), <s>rekhā</s> (line), and <s>jalagarbhatā</s> (water-inclusion) —

children.text: sarvaratneṣvamī pañca doṣāḥ sādhāraṇā matāḥ // Rcūm_12.27 //
children.translated_text: these five defects are considered common to all gems. // Rcūm 12.27 //

children.text: kṣetratoyabhavā doṣā ratneṣu na laganti ca /
children.translated_text: Defects arising from the mine and water do not attach to gems [permanently];

children.text: bhairavastu punaḥ prāha doṣo doṣe'sti sarvathā // Rcūm_12.28 //
children.translated_text: but <s>Bhairava</s> has again declared: a defect is absolutely a defect in all cases. // Rcūm 12.28 //
{Diamond: purification}
Sweated in a decoction of <s>kulattha</s> (horse gram), or boiled with <s>kodrava</s> (millet),

children.text: ekayāmāvadhi svinnaṃ vajraṃ śudhyati niścitam // Rcūm_12.29 //
children.translated_text: sweated for up to one <s>yāma</s> (three hours) — the diamond is certainly purified. // Rcūm 12.29 //
{Diamond: calcination (<s>māraṇa</s>)}
The diamond, imbued four times with the blood of bedbugs (<s>matkuṇa</s>),
wrapped with a paste made from the flesh of the fragrant rat (<s>sugandhamūṣikā</s>) — // Rcūm 12.30 //
it should be heated with <s>vārāha</s> (boar) <s>puṭas</s> thirty times; then

children.text: dhmātvā dhmātvā śataṃ vārān kulatthakvāthake kṣipet // Rcūm_12.31 //
children.translated_text: after smelting again and again a hundred times, it should be thrown into a decoction of horse gram (<s>kulattha</s>). // Rcūm 12.31 //
Others have stated that this procedural sequence should be performed a hundred times.
{Diamond: calcination — water-floating test (<s>vāritara</s>)}
With a paste of <s>lakuca</s> (breadfruit) juice mixed with horse gram (<s>kulattha</s>) decoction — // Rcūm 12.32 //

children.text: śilayā liptamūṣāyāṃ vajraṃ kṣiptvā nirudhya ca /
children.translated_text: having placed the diamond in a crucible smeared with that paste and sealed it,
it should be properly heated eight times with dried cow-dung cakes (<s>vanakotpala</s>). // Rcūm 12.33 //
Then, after smelting a hundred times, [the diamond] placed in pure mercury —

children.text: niścitaṃ mriyate vajraṃ bhasma vāritaraṃ bhavet // Rcūm_12.34 //
children.translated_text: the diamond is certainly killed; the ash becomes water-floating (<s>vāritara</s>). // Rcūm 12.34 //
The truth-speaking <s>Somasenāni</s> — this is his [method for] the killing of diamond,
endowed with tested results, declared by that alchemist enthusiast (<s>rasakautukī</s>). // Rcūm 12.35 //
{Diamond: calcination (method 2)}
Smeared with bedbug blood and dried seven times,
placed in an iron vessel filled with <s>kāsamarda</s> (Cassia) juice — // Rcūm 12.36 //
smelted seven times, it certainly becomes diamond-ash;
this procedure has been proclaimed by the great sage <s>Brahmajyotis</s>. // Rcūm 12.37 //
{Diamond: calcination (method 3)}
Ground on the tuber of <s>nīlajyotirlatā</s> (blue flame creeper) and dried in the sun,
the diamond attains the state of ash — like karma [destroyed] by the fire of knowledge (<s>jñānavahni</s>). // Rcūm 12.38 //
{Diamond: calcination (method 4)}
With the juice extracted from the fruit of <s>madana</s> (Randia), mixed with tin (<s>kṣoṇināga</s>),
made into a paste and smeared, it should be heated with <s>puṭa</s> twenty times. // Rcūm 12.39 //

body.translated_text: Then, having powdered that diamond with a little borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>) added — // Rcūm 12.40 //

children.translated_text: it should certainly be rolled with twenty [portions of] essence of donkey-earth-lead (<s>kharabhūnāgasattva</s>),
and that, smelted with an equal amount of gold, should be employed in mercurial and other [preparations]. // Rcūm 12.41 //
Triturated with three times its weight of mercury and made into a pill,
held in the mouth, it quickly produces firm binding of loose teeth. // Rcūm 12.42 //
{Diamond: uses of the killed (calcined) form}

children.text: triṃśadbhāgamitaṃ hi vajrabhasitaṃ svarṇaṃ kalābhāgikaṃ tāraṃ cāṣṭaguṇaṃ śivāmṛtavaraṃ rudrāṃśakaṃ cābhrakam /
children.translated_text: Thirty parts of diamond-ash, gold in one-sixteenth part, silver eight times [of gold], the excellent nectar of <s>Śiva</s> (mica-ash) in <s>Rudra</s>'s portion (eleven parts), mica,

children.text: pādāṃśaṃ khalu tāpyakaṃ vasuguṇaṃ vaikrāntakaṃ ṣaḍguṇaṃ bhāgo'pyuktarasādraso'yamuditaḥ ṣāḍguṇyasaṃsiddhaye // Rcūm_12.43 //
children.translated_text: a quarter-portion of <s>tāpya</s> (pyrites), <s>vaikrānta</s> in eight times [of pyrites], in six times — this mercury formulation proclaimed from the mineral king achieves six-fold perfection. // Rcūm 12.43 //
{<s>Jalanīla</s>: examination}
Having a blue hue with whiteness at its core, and lightweight — that is <s>jalanīla</s> (water-blue).
{<s>Indranīla</s>: examination}
Having a blue hue with blackness at its core, and heavy — that is <s>śakranīla</s> (Indra's blue). // Rcūm 12.44 //

body.translated_text:
{Sapphire: subtypes}
<s>Jalanīla</s> (water-blue) and <s>indranīla</s> (Indra's blue); also called <s>śakranīla</s> — of the two, the latter is superior.

children.translated_text: {Sapphire: examination — good quality}
Of uniform color, heavy, smooth, transparent, of compact body,
soft, with light radiating from its center — a sapphire (<s>nīla</s>) is excellent in seven ways. // Rcūm 12.45 //
{<s>Jalanīla</s>: examination (bad quality)}

children.text: komalaṃ vihitaṃ varṇaṃ nirbhāraṃ raktagandhi ca /
children.translated_text: Delicate, artificially colored, lightweight, reddish-scented,

children.text: cipiṭābhaṃ sarūkṣaṃ ca jalanīlaṃ ca saptadhā // Rcūm_12.46 //
children.translated_text: flat in appearance, and rough — <s>jalanīla</s> [is defective] in seven ways. // Rcūm 12.46 //
{Sapphire: medicinal properties}
Sapphire removes cough and asthma, is aphrodisiac, destroys all three <s>doṣas</s>, and is a good appetizer;
it destroys irregular fever, fistula (<s>durnāma</s>), and sins — thus <s>nīla</s> (sapphire) is described. // Rcūm 12.47 //
{Hessonite: examination — good quality}
Having the hue of bright cow-urine, transparent, smooth, even, heavy,

children.text: nirdalaṃ masṛṇaṃ dīptaṃ śastaṃ gomedamaṣṭadhā // Rcūm_12.48 //
children.translated_text: without layers, polished, lustrous — <s>gomeda</s> (hessonite) is praised in eight ways. // Rcūm 12.48 //

body.translated_text:
{Hessonite (<s>gomeda</s>): etymology}
Because of its cow-fat-like color, the gem is called <s>gomeda</s>.

children.translated_text: {Hessonite: examination — bad quality}
Lacking color, light, rough-bodied, flat, with layers —

children.text: niṣprabhaṃ pītakācābhaṃ gomedaṃ na śubhāvaham // Rcūm_12.49 //
children.translated_text: <s>Gomeda</s> (hessonite) that is lusterless and resembles yellow glass does not bring auspiciousness. [Rcūm 12.49]
{<s>Gomeda</s>: medicinal properties}
<s>Gomeda</s> destroys <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) and <s>pitta</s> (bile), cures consumption and pallor,

children.text: dīpanaṃ pācanaṃ rucyaṃ tvacyaṃ buddhiprabodhanam // Rcūm_12.50 //
children.translated_text: is a digestive stimulant, digestive, appetite-producing, beneficial for the skin, and an awakener of the intellect. [Rcūm 12.50]
{<s>Vaiḍūrya</s> (cat's eye/beryl): examination: good quality}

children.text: vaiḍūryaṃ śyāmaśubhrābhaṃ samaṃ svacchaṃ guru sphuṭam /
children.translated_text: <s>Vaiḍūrya</s> that is dark-and-bright in hue, even, clear, heavy, and well-defined,
with a shimmering upper veil enclosing [light within] — that is declared auspicious. [Rcūm 12.51]
{<s>Vaiḍūrya</s>: examination: bad quality}
That which is dark, water-like in appearance, flat, light, and rough,

children.text: raktagarbhottarīyaṃ ca vaiḍūryaṃ naiva śasyate // Rcūm_12.52 //
children.translated_text: with a red-veined interior — such <s>vaiḍūrya</s> is not praised. [Rcūm 12.52]
{<s>Vaiḍūrya</s>: medicinal properties}
<s>Vaiḍūrya</s> destroys blood-bile disorders, increases wisdom, longevity, and strength,
destroys diseases predominantly of <s>pitta</s>, stimulates digestion, and releases impurities. [Rcūm 12.53]
{Gemstones: purification (<s>śodhana</s>)}
Ruby (<s>māṇikya</s>) is purified by acid; pearl (<s>mauktika</s>) by [the juice of] <s>jayantī</s>,
coral (<s>vidruma</s>) by the group of alkalis; conch-shell (<s>tārkṣya</s>) by cow's milk. [Rcūm 12.54]
Topaz (<s>puṣparāga</s>) by grain-acid combined with horse-gram decoction,
diamond (<s>vajra</s>) by <s>taṇḍulīya</s> (Amaranthus) water, sapphire (<s>nīla</s>) by indigo (<s>nīlī</s>) juice,
<s>gomeda</s> by <s>rocanā</s> (ox bile), and <s>vaiḍūrya</s> by <s>triphalā</s> water. [Rcūm 12.55]
{Gemstones: calcination (<s>māraṇa</s>)}
Ground with <s>lakuca</s> (breadfruit) juice together with orpiment (<s>śilā</s>), sulphur, and realgar (<s>tālaka</s>),
all gems except diamond are killed (calcined) in eight firings. [Rcūm 12.56]
{Gemstones: liquefaction (<s>druti</s>)}
<s>Rāmaṭha</s> (a type of salt), the five salts (<s>pañcalavaṇa</s>), and the triad of alkalis,
flesh-dissolving [agent], <s>amlavetasa</s> (tamarind), and <s>cūlikā</s> salt, [Rcūm 12.57]
ripe fruit of land-pumpkin (<s>sthalakumbhī</s>), the excellent flame-mouth [plant] (<s>jvālāmukhī</s>),

children.text: dravantī ca rudantī ca payasyā citramūlakam // Rcūm_12.58 //
children.translated_text: <s>dravantī</s> and <s>rudantī</s>, <s>payasyā</s>, and <s>citramūlaka</s>, [Rcūm 12.58]
milk of <s>snuhī</s> (Euphorbia) and of <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) — all these should be carefully ground together.
Having made a ball, one should place the [gemstone] in its middle thereafter. [Rcūm 12.59]
Only gemstones that are of good quality, genuine class, and auspicious [should be used].

children.text: bhūrje taṃ golakaṃ kṛtvā sūtreṇāveṣṭya yatnataḥ // Rcūm_12.60 //
children.translated_text: Having made that ball on birch-bark, wrapping it carefully with thread, [Rcūm 12.60]
wrapping again with cloth and placing it in a <s>dolāyantra</s> (swing apparatus),
in the belly of a pot filled with all-acid fermented liquor, [Rcūm 12.61]
one should sweat it with intense fire for three days and nights.
Extracting it from there and washing, one should collect the gem-born liquefied substance. [Rcūm 12.62]
The liquefied substance of gems is of equal lustre [to the gem], light, body-and-metal-transforming, and auspicious.

children.text: durmelā rasarājena naikatvaṃ yāti tena sā // Rcūm_12.63 //
children.translated_text: Being difficult to combine with the king of mercury, it does not attain unity with it. [Rcūm 12.63]
By the group beginning with <s>rāmaṭha</s> [salt], it certainly becomes mixed.

children.text: suprasanne mahādeve drutiḥ kasya na sidhyati // Rcūm_12.64 //
children.translated_text: When <s>Mahādeva</s> is well pleased, for whom does the liquefaction not succeed? [Rcūm 12.64]
Rare is devotion to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, rare is the binding of mercury,
and rare in this world is the liquefaction [of gems] for men of little fortune. [Rcūm 12.65]

The wearing of gemstones removes the afflictions of the planets beginning with the sun, grants long life and health, brings the rise of good fortune, luck, power over others, wealth, enthusiasm, and courage,

children.text: duḥchāyāṃcaladhūlisaṅgatibhavālakṣmīharaṃ sarvadā ratnānāṃ paridhāraṇaṃ nigaditaṃ bhūtādinirṇāśanam // Rcūm_12.66 //
children.translated_text: always removes ill-fortune arising from bad shadows, dust, and inauspicious contacts, and is declared to destroy spirits and the like. [Rcūm 12.66]
The entire group of virtues of gemstones, and the foremost among the noble,

children.text: suratnamabravīt somo neti yadguṇitaṃ guṇī // Rcūm_12.67 //
children.translated_text: the illustrious <s>Soma</s> (Somadeva) spoke of the excellent gem [saying], "Its qualities are not exhausted" — [so said] the virtuous one. [Rcūm 12.67]
A gemstone endowed with color, weight, class, and [genuine] origin yields results —

children.text: rase rasāyane dāne dhāraṇe cānyathānyathā // Rcūm_12.68 //
children.translated_text: in mercury [work], in rejuvenation, in gifting, and in wearing — otherwise [it is] otherwise [ineffective]. [Rcūm 12.68]
{Ruby rejuvenative (<s>māṇikyarasāyana</s>)}
One <s>karṣa</s> of ash from a ruby of good quality and auspicious [nature],
and separately, ashes of gold, mica, copper, and lodite (<s>kānta</s>), [Rcūm 13.1]

body.translated_text: Rcūm, Chapter 13

children.translated_text: increased in threefold proportion, should be ground with equal [portions of] sulphur.
One should fire carefully five times with forest cow-dung cakes (<s>vanagiriṇḍa</s>). [Rcūm 13.2]
Similarly with orpiment (<s>śilā</s>) and realgar (<s>lakā</s>), and fire with <s>nīlāñjana</s> (antimony).
With equal [portions of] sulphur, rock, and mercury, one should prepare an auspicious black paste (<s>kajjalī</s>). [Rcūm 13.3]
Then, carefully taking that <s>kajjalī</s>,
melting it in an iron vessel with <s>bādara</s> (jujube) charcoal over a low fire, [Rcūm 13.4]
one should add and mix in the ashes of ruby and the other [gems].
Then, grinding that <s>kajjalī</s> with ginger juice, [Rcūm 13.5]
drying it well and powdering it, one should place it in an attractive container.
This rejuvenative of ruby and the like, measured with <s>vyoṣa</s> (three pungents) and ghee — [Rcūm 13.6]
licked with <s>vyoṣa</s> and ghee for six months by one observing a wholesome diet,
it destroys all diseases including old age and grey hair. [Rcūm 13.7]
One lives a hundred years, eating three meals [a day],
[and it destroys] all diseases beginning with consumption, with appropriate vehicles for each disease. [Rcūm 13.8]
{Pearl rejuvenative (<s>mauktikarasāyana</s>)}
Pearl ground with <s>jayantī</s> juice and calcined with peacock feather [ash],

children.text: mauktikaṃ rasamātraṃ hi dviguṇaṃ svarṇabhasmakam // Rcūm_13.9 //
children.translated_text: in the amount of one <s>rasa</s> (unit), with double that of gold ash, [Rcūm 13.9]
triple that of lodestone (<s>kānta</s>) ash, and quadruple of mica essence,

children.text: dattvā ca gandhasaubhāgyaṃ śṛṅgavereṇa bhāvitam // Rcūm_13.10 //
children.translated_text: adding sulphur and ginger (<s>saubhāgya</s>), processed with <s>śṛṅgavera</s> (dry ginger), [Rcūm 13.10]
one should fire twenty times, melt, and strain through cloth.
With mercury equal to the total and of full potency, having prepared a <s>kajjalī</s>, [Rcūm 13.11]
melting as before, one should add the ashes of pearl and the others.
Mixing and adding goat's milk therein, [Rcūm 13.12]
drying and powdering, one should place it in a glass bottle.
Taken with long pepper and honey in a dose of one <s>valla</s>, [Rcūm 13.13]
by the method of rejuvenation therapy, within one year it produces
freedom from wrinkles and grey hair, [immunity from] old age, [Rcūm 13.14]
full endowment of hearing, teeth, and the like, a lifespan of a hundred years, and [good] eyesight,
strength like that of a maddened elephant, and victory in disputes. [Rcūm 13.15]
Licked with honey, ghee, and oil, combined with <s>aśvagandhā</s> (Withania) and minute dose,
it certainly destroys consumption within half a <s>maṇḍala</s> (fortnight). [Rcūm 13.16]
With appropriate vehicles for each disease, it destroys all ailments.
It grants sons to barren women and destroys puerperal diseases. [Rcūm 13.17]
It is supremely wholesome for children, highly aphrodisiac, and the best bestower of longevity.

children.text: nāgodaropaviṣṭaṃ ca hanti strīṇāṃ ca vegataḥ // Rcūm_13.18 //
children.translated_text: It rapidly destroys <s>nāgodara</s> (ascites) and seated [conditions] in women. [Rcūm 13.18]
Combined with fresh butter and mixed with toddy-palm juice,
it is proclaimed as excellent in all diseases of pregnant women. [Rcūm 13.19]
{Coral rejuvenative (<s>pravālarasāyana</s>)}
Four <s>palas</s> of coral ash, calcined silver (<s>tāraka</s>)
equal to that, double [that amount of] copper, and half [the coral amount] of <s>mākṣika</s> (iron pyrite), [Rcūm 13.20]
one-thirtieth part of diamond, one-sixteenth part of sapphire,

children.text: vyomasattvaṃ samaṃ sarvaistālakaṃ sarvataḥ samam // Rcūm_13.21 //
children.translated_text: mica essence equal to all [combined], and realgar (<s>tālaka</s>) equal to the total, [Rcūm 13.21]
grinding with citron (<s>luṅga</s>) water for four days,
with pure mercury equal to half [the total], and double that of sulphur, [Rcūm 13.22]

children.text: vihitāṃ kajjalīṃ samyak drāvayitvā yathā purā /
children.translated_text: having properly prepared a <s>kajjalī</s> and melted it as before,

children.text: pravālādīni bhasmāni vinikṣipya vimiśrya ca // Rcūm_13.23 //
children.translated_text: one should add and mix in the ashes of coral and the rest. [Rcūm 13.23]
Quenching properly in cow's ghee aged twelve years,
sealing in a saucer-pair, smeared with ghee, one should sweat it gently. [Rcūm 13.24]
Powdering and processing with <s>bhṛṅga</s> (Eclipta) juice seven times,
taken with <s>vyoṣa</s> (three pungents) and ghee, it cures fever in three days. [Rcūm 13.25]
Consumption within half a <s>maṇḍala</s> (fortnight), <s>grahaṇī</s> (malabsorption), pallor, and jaundice,
<s>kumbhakāmalā</s> (hepatitis), and disease, <s>udāvarta</s> (reverse peristalsis), and <s>mahodara</s> (ascites), [Rcūm 13.26]
diabetes (<s>prameha</s>), increase of fat, <s>vātavyādhi</s> (wind disease), <s>kapha</s> disease,
hemorrhoids (<s>gudaroga</s>), weak digestive fire, and urinary wind disorders completely. [Rcūm 13.27]
Venereal disease, barrenness, and skin diseases —
with <s>vyoṣa</s>, ghee, and <s>citraka</s> (Plumbago) water as the complete vehicle. [Rcūm 13.28]

children.text: bhūyo bhūyo visūcyartir dehino yasya jāyate /
children.translated_text: For one to whom the agony of cholera (<s>visūci</s>) occurs again and again,

children.text: raso'yaṃ tasya dātavyo maṇḍalānāṃ trayaṃ khalu /
children.translated_text: this medicine should be given for three <s>maṇḍalas</s> (fortnights).
In diseases with <s>āma</s> (undigested matter), physicians should administer it for up to a year. [Rcūm 13.29]
{Conch-shell rejuvenative (<s>tārkṣyarasāyana</s>)}
One <s>śāṇa</s> of conch-shell (<s>tārkṣya</s>) ash, half that of diamond ash,
two <s>niṣkas</s> each, separately, of calcined gold, <s>arka</s> [mineral], and lodestone, [Rcūm 13.30]
iron ash, calcined mercury — all should be ground together.
One should fire twenty times with firings called <s>kukkuṭa</s> (hen-dung cake). [Rcūm 13.31]
With orpiment, sulphur, and realgar combined with <s>amṛtā</s> (Tinospora) water,

children.text: saptavāraṃ dravaiḥ sārdhaṃ daśabhiḥ piṣṭakaiḥ puṭet // Rcūm_13.32 //
children.translated_text: one should fire seven times with [those] liquids and ten [types of] cakes. [Rcūm 13.32]

children.text: evaṃ siddhaṃ prabhāvāḍhyaṃ tārkṣyaṃ nāma rasāyanam /
children.translated_text: Thus perfected, rich in power — this is the rejuvenative called <s>tārkṣya</s>.
Taken with <s>citraka</s> and ginger juice, measured as a mustard-seed [dose], [Rcūm 13.33]
it [cures] all diseases born of the three <s>doṣas</s>, and those arising from <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>,
[even those] incurable by all physicians and by crores of medicines.

children.text: karoti kṣudhamatyarthaṃ bhuktaṃ jarayati kṣaṇāt // Rcūm_13.34 //
children.translated_text: It produces extreme hunger and digests food in an instant. [Rcūm 13.34]
{Topaz rejuvenative (<s>puṣparāgarasāyana</s>)}
Half a <s>pala</s> of auspicious ash produced from topaz (<s>puṣparāga</s>),

children.text: tadardhaṃ pītakācaṃ ca tadardhaṃ tāmrabhasmakam // Rcūm_13.35 //
children.translated_text: half that of yellow glass (<s>pītakāca</s>), and half again of copper ash, [Rcūm 13.35]
half the copper of silver, half that of gold,

children.text: vajrabhasma tadardhaṃ ca sarvatulyaṃ mṛtābhrakam // Rcūm_13.36 //
children.translated_text: half that of diamond ash, and calcined mica equal to the total, [Rcūm 13.36]

children.text: tatsamaṃ sūryakāntaṃ ca māritaṃ balinā saha /
children.translated_text: and calcined sunstone (<s>sūryakānta</s>) equal to that, with mercury of full potency.

children.text: tulyena balinā sārdhaṃ daśavāraṃ puṭet khalu // Rcūm_13.37 //
children.translated_text: With equal potent mercury, one should fire ten times. [Rcūm 13.37]
With antimony (<s>nīlāñjana</s>), creeper, and <s>tāpya</s> — separate firings for each.
Thus perfected, this is declared the topaz rejuvenative. [Rcūm 13.38]
It destroys all diseases beginning with consumption, is supreme in curing leprosy (<s>kuṣṭha</s>),
pacifies hemorrhoidal tumors and abdominal pain, is fertility-granting, aphrodisiac, and excellent. [Rcūm 13.39]

children.text: rasāyanaṃ tathā caitat kṣipraṃ gulmaharaṃ striyāḥ /
children.translated_text: It is also a rejuvenative, quickly cures tumors (<s>gulma</s>) in women,
is declared the supreme digestive stimulant, and destroys jaundice and anemia.
Why say more? — it destroys all diseases. [Rcūm 13.40]
{Diamond rejuvenative (<s>vajrarasāyana</s>)}
One <s>karṣa</s> of calcined diamond, an equal amount of <s>bhūnāga</s> (lead) essence,

children.text: tataśca dviguṇaṃ svarṇaṃ svarṇatulyaṃ khasattvakam // Rcūm_13.41 //
children.translated_text: then double that of gold, and mica essence equal to the gold, [Rcūm 13.41]

children.text: tāvanmātraṃ ca kāntāyaḥ sarvaṃ vāritaraṃ kṛtam /
children.translated_text: and an equal amount of lodestone-iron — all made into fine particles.
And one-eighth of mercury compared to all [combined] is prescribed. [Rcūm 13.42]
Peacock feather [ash] equal to all — one should grind with sour chickpea [water].

children.text: vidhāya golakaṃ ramyaṃ chāyāśuṣkaṃ samācaret // Rcūm_13.43 //
children.translated_text: Having made an attractive ball, one should shade-dry it. [Rcūm 13.43]

children.text: tato bhūnāgasattvaṃ hi gandhakena samaṃ kṣipet /
children.translated_text: Then one should add <s>bhūnāga</s> essence equal to the sulphur.

children.text: puṭitaṃ śatavārāṇi śataṃ vārāṇi tāpyakaiḥ // Rcūm_13.44 //
children.translated_text: Fired a hundred times, [then] a hundred times with <s>tāpya</s> (pyrite) [fires], [Rcūm 13.44]
then twenty times with <s>sūryaparṇa</s> (sun-leaf) [plant] or with milk.
Covered with <s>guñjā</s>, borax, and beeswax dust of <s>bhūnāga</s>, [Rcūm 13.45]

children.text: vartayitvā tu taṃ golaṃ kalkenānena lepayet /
children.translated_text: having rolled that ball, one should coat it with this paste,
to a thickness of half an <s>aṅgula</s> leaf, and dry in intense sunlight. [Rcūm 13.46]
One should place it in a sand-bath apparatus and cook for five days.
Then, with the milk of triangular <s>gaṇḍīra</s> [plant] combined with sulphur, [Rcūm 13.47]

children.text: mardayitvā tu taṃ golaṃ puṭedvārāṇi viṃśatim /
children.translated_text: having ground that ball, one should fire twenty times.
Then making a cloth-fine powder, one should place it in an inner container. [Rcūm 13.48]
One should take one <s>guñjā</s> dose of this excellent diamond rejuvenative,

children.text: jñātājñāteṣu sarveṣu gadeṣu vividheṣu ca // Rcūm_13.49 //
children.translated_text: in all diseases, both known and unknown, and of various kinds. [Rcūm 13.49]
The physician should indeed administer it with the appropriate vehicle for each disease.

children.text: na so'sti rogo loke'sminyo hyanena na śāmyati // Rcūm_13.50 //
children.translated_text: there is no disease in this world that is not pacified by it. // Rcūm 13.50 //
Taken in the manner of a rejuvenative for three <s>maṇḍalas</s> (cycles),
it produces perfection of the body that causes astonishment to the universe;

children.text: bilvamekaṃ vinā sarvaṃ pathyamatra prakīrtitam // Rcūm_13.51 //
children.translated_text: everything except <s>bilva</s> (wood-apple) fruit is proclaimed as wholesome here. // Rcūm 13.51 //
{Blue rejuvenative (<s>nīlarasāyana</s>)}
Ash made from blue sapphire, one <s>pala</s> measure, and diamond,

children.text: svarṇaṃ raupyaṃ ca kāntaṃ ca tāpyakaṃ nṛpavartakam // Rcūm_13.52 //
children.translated_text: gold, silver, magnetic iron (<s>kānta</s>), pyrites (<s>tāpyaka</s>), and <s>nṛpavartaka</s> — // Rcūm 13.52 //

children.text: samāṃśaṃ sarvametat syāt sarvatulyaṃ ca śulvakam /
children.translated_text: all these in equal parts, and copper equal to the total of all;
all of these should be taken in calcined form, combined with an equal amount of sulphur. // Rcūm 13.53 //
One should grind with <s>kaṅguṇī</s> (Celastrus) oil for eight days,

children.text: ūrdhvādho gandhakaṃ dattvā puṭedvārāṇi viṃśatim // Rcūm_13.54 //
children.translated_text: placing sulphur above and below, and heat for twenty rounds. // Rcūm 13.54 //
Then one should saturate with white <s>muṇḍī</s> (Sphaeranthus) juices seven times;

children.text: iti siddhaṃ prabhāvāḍhyaṃ ramyaṃ nīlarasāyanam // Rcūm_13.55 //
children.translated_text: thus perfected is the efficacious and delightful blue rejuvenative (<s>nīlarasāyana</s>). // Rcūm 13.55 //
Taken in the dose of one <s>guñjā</s> (seed-measure), it destroys all diseases:

children.text: jvaraṃ pāṇḍuṃ kṣayaṃ kāsaṃ śūlamarśaśca gulmakam // Rcūm_13.56 //
children.translated_text: fever, anemia, consumption, cough, colic, piles, and tumors, // Rcūm 13.56 //

children.text: udaraṃ kuṣṭharogaṃ ca śvāsaṃ pañcavidhaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: abdominal diseases, leprosy (<s>kuṣṭha</s>), and the five types of asthma;
with appropriate medicinal adjuncts in each case, it eradicates each respective disease. // Rcūm 13.57 //
{<s>Gomeda</s> (hessonite) rejuvenative}
<s>Gomeda</s> (hessonite), combined with sulphur and <s>lakuca</s> juice,

children.text: puṭitvā daśavāraiśca jātaṃ bhasma palonmitam // Rcūm_13.58 //
children.translated_text: heated ten times, produces ash measuring one <s>pala</s>. // Rcūm 13.58 //
Gold, silver, and magnetic iron — all killed with medicines,
<s>krāmaṇa</s> (transmuting agent) added in quarter parts, moistened with <s>cūlikā</s> water; // Rcūm 13.59 //
pyrites (<s>tāpya</s>), heated ten times with castor oil (<s>gandharva-taila</s>),

children.text: nirutthaṃ jāyate bhasma sarvathaiva guṇādhikam // Rcūm_13.60 //
children.translated_text: becomes an irreversible (<s>niruttha</s>) ash, superior in all qualities. // Rcūm 13.60 //
With half that amount of mercury and sulphur, having made <s>kajjalī</s> (black preparation), in the molten state,

children.text: pūrvabhasmatrayaṃ kṣiptvā vimiśrya ca samāharet // Rcūm_13.61 //
children.translated_text: adding the three previous ashes, mixing, and collecting — // Rcūm 13.61 //
one should powder and saturate with <s>muṇḍikā</s> juices seven times,
making it into cloth-filtered powder, and then place inside a container. // Rcūm 13.62 //
This is indeed the supreme and best <s>gomeda</s> (hessonite) rejuvenative,
applicable in all diseases, with appropriate disease-specific adjuncts. // Rcūm 13.63 //

children.text: karoti dīpanaṃ tīvraṃ sarvārhaṃ ca priyaṃkaram /
children.translated_text: It powerfully kindles digestion, makes all things agreeable and pleasing,
bestows supreme nourishment and strength comparable to that of <s>Bhīma</s>,
is supremely aphrodisiac, life-prolonging, beneficial for the eyes, and removes oral diseases. // Rcūm 13.64 //
{<s>Vaidūrya</s> (cat's-eye) rejuvenative}
<s>Vaidūrya</s> (cat's-eye gem) is calcined with magnetic iron paste and sulphur;
of that ash, eight <s>śāṇas</s> in measure, and half that amount of calcined gold, // Rcūm 13.65 //

children.text: tayoḥ samaṃ tīkṣṇarajo mṛtaṃ rūpyaṃ ca tatsamam /
children.translated_text: equal to both of those, calcined steel (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>) powder, and an equal amount of calcined silver,

children.text: mṛtaṃ ca vimalaṃ sarvaiḥ samaṃ sarvaṃ vimarditam // Rcūm_13.66 //
children.translated_text: and calcined <s>vimala</s> — all equal [in amount], all ground together, // Rcūm 13.66 //
mixed with plantain extract, formed into pills, and dried;
with half a finger-width of <s>śilājatu</s> (mineral pitch), one should grind it. // Rcūm 13.67 //
Placed in a sand-bath apparatus, one should cook slowly for half a <s>pakṣa</s> (fortnight);
when self-cooled, collecting it, from the root-extract of <s>kumārī</s> (aloe), // Rcūm 13.68 //
grinding and drying, then with the water of <s>pīlu</s> root,
likewise with the water of <s>citramūla</s> (Plumbago) root, and the extract of <s>kanthārī</s> root, // Rcūm 13.69 //
with the water of long-aged <s>bilva</s> (wood-apple), drying and powdering —
this is verily the reviver of the dead (<s>mṛtasaṃjīvana</s>), the <s>vaidūrya</s> rejuvenative. // Rcūm 13.70 //
Combined with fresh ginger juice, the rejuvenative in <s>guñjā</s>-measure dose
should be administered, or with <s>citra</s> (Plumbago) water, in <s>sannipāta</s> (triple-humoral) fever with loss of consciousness. // Rcūm 13.71 //
When lockjaw (<s>dantabandha</s>) has occurred, this medicine in <s>valla</s>-measure
should be rubbed on the feet with effort — then the patient regains movement. // Rcūm 13.72 //
When movement has returned, cool water should be poured on the head,

children.text: śatakumbhamitaṃ svādu tīvrā kṣujjāyate tataḥ // Rcūm_13.73 //
children.translated_text: sweet, measured at a hundred <s>kumbhas</s> — then intense hunger arises. // Rcūm 13.73 //
Whatever the patient requests, that desired thing should be given;

children.text: āyuṣye vidyamāne sa sukhī jīvati mānavaḥ // Rcūm_13.74 //
children.translated_text: with life-span remaining, that person lives happily. // Rcūm 13.74 //
In diseases arising from all three <s>doṣas</s>, it should be given in rice-grain measure,
combined with half a <s>pala</s> of sugar — otherwise it kills the patient. // Rcūm 13.75 //
In diseases arising from a single <s>doṣa</s>, or those arising from a combination [of two],

children.text: na dātavyaṃ hi bhiṣajā vaidūryakarasāyanam // Rcūm_13.76 //
children.translated_text: the physician should not administer the <s>vaidūrya</s> rejuvenative. // Rcūm 13.76 //

children.text: dhṛtāni vā tāni samarcitāni sujātiyuktāni ca saṃstutāni /
children.translated_text: When gems are worn, properly worshipped, set in proper metals, and praised with hymns,

children.text: haranti ratnānyakhilaṃ duriṣṭaṃ kurvantyabhīṣṭaṃ satataṃ yatheṣṭam // Rcūm_13.77 //
children.translated_text: they remove all misfortune and constantly fulfill wishes as desired. // Rcūm 13.77 //

children.text: harantyalakṣmīṃ satataṃ samastān duṣkarmajātān iha sarvarogān /
children.translated_text: They constantly remove ill-fortune and all diseases born of evil deeds in this world;
the rejuvenatives produced from all gems are life-prolonging and beneficial. // Rcūm 13.78 //
{Classes of metals}

children.text: śuddhaṃ lohaṃ kanakarajataṃ bhānulohāśmasāraṃ pūtīlohaṃ dvitayamuditaṃ nāgavaṅgābhidhānam /
children.translated_text: Pure metals (<s>śuddha loha</s>) are gold and silver; sun-metal (<s>bhānuloha</s>, copper) and iron (<s>aśmasāra</s>); impure metals (<s>pūtīloha</s>), two in number, are called lead (<s>nāga</s>) and tin (<s>vaṅga</s>);

children.text: miśraṃ lohaṃ tritayamuditaṃ pittalaṃ kāṃsyavartaṃ dhātur lohe luha iti mataḥ so'pi kaṣārthavācī // Rcūm_14.1 //
children.translated_text: mixed metals (<s>miśra loha</s>), three in number, are brass (<s>pittala</s>), bell-metal (<s>kāṃsya</s>), and <s>varta</s>; the mineral in metal is called <s>luha</s> — and that word also means 'to test.' // Rcūm 14.1 //

body.translated_text: <s>Rasendracūḍāmaṇi</s>, Chapter 14

children.translated_text: {Gold: subtypes}
Primordial (<s>prākṛta</s>), innate (<s>sahaja</s>), fire-born (<s>vahnisambhūta</s>), mine-born (<s>khanisambhava</s>),
and born from mercury-transmutation (<s>rasendravedha</s>) — gold is remembered as fivefold. // Rcūm 14.2 //
{Primordial gold}
That by which the cosmic egg (<s>brahmāṇḍa</s>) was enveloped, born of the quality of <s>rajas</s>,
is called primordial (<s>prākṛta</s>) — it is unobtainable even by the gods. // Rcūm 14.3 //
{Innate gold}
<s>Brahmā</s>, who was born enveloped in a golden membrane (<s>jarāyu</s>),

children.text: tanmerurūpatāṃ jātaṃ suvarṇaṃ sahajaṃ hi tat // Rcūm_14.4 //
children.translated_text: that [gold] which has assumed the form of Mount <s>Meru</s> — that is innate (<s>sahaja</s>) gold. // Rcūm 14.4 //
{Fire-born gold}
The radiance of <s>Śiva</s>, yellow and unbearably intense, released by fire,
became gold — that is designated as fire-born (<s>vahnisambhava</s>) gold. // Rcūm 14.5 //
These three types of divine gold are endowed with sixteen degrees of color;
merely by wearing them, they would make the body free from aging and immortal. // Rcūm 14.6 //
{Mine-born gold}

children.text: tatra tatra girīṇāṃ hi jātaṃ khaniṣu yadbhavet /
children.translated_text: That which is born in the mines of various mountains —
rich in fourteen degrees of color, when consumed, it cures all diseases. // Rcūm 14.7 //
{Transmutation-born gold}
That born from the transmutation by the lord of mercury — that is called transmutation-born (<s>vedhaja</s>);

children.text: rasāyanaṃ mahāśreṣṭhaṃ pāpaghnaṃ vedhajaṃ hi tat // Rcūm_14.8 //
children.translated_text: it is a supremely excellent rejuvenative and destroyer of sins — such is transmutation-born gold. // Rcūm 14.8 //
Silver, copper, mercury-tin, tin-mica alloy, pyrites-tin, and mercury —

children.text: yattārajaṃ hi pravadanti rāgataḥ svarṇaṃ kalāvarṇacaturguṇaṃ hi // Rcūm_14.9 //
children.translated_text: that which is born of silver and [other metals], they declare by tinging degree, is gold with quadrupled fractional color. // Rcūm 14.9 //
{Gold: testing for good quality}

children.text: ghṛṣṭaṃ varṇe ghusṛṇasadṛśaṃ raktavarṇaṃ ca dāhe chede kiṃcit sitam akapilaṃ nirdalaṃ bhūribhāram /
children.translated_text: When rubbed, resembling saffron in color, red in color when heated, slightly white and not brownish when cut, without layers, very heavy,

children.text: snigdhaṃ svarṇaṃ ravivirahitaṃ styānaraktaprabhāḍhyaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ diṣṭam atulitalasaccāruvarṇaṃ ca svarṇam // Rcūm_14.10 //
children.translated_text: unctuous, without sun-like streaks, rich in dense red luster — the finest gold is declared to be of incomparably beautiful and true color. // Rcūm 14.10 //
{Gold: testing for bad quality}

children.text: rūkṣaṃ vivarṇaṃ malinaṃ kaṭhoraṃ kṛṣṇaṃ ca dāhe nikaṣe ca pāṇḍu /
children.translated_text: Rough, discolored, dirty, hard, black when heated, pale on the touchstone,

children.text: sthūlāṅgakaṃ nirbharakaṃ kaḍāraṃ sphuṭatsuvarṇaṃ daśadhā na śastam // Rcūm_14.11 //
children.translated_text: coarse-grained, lightweight, brownish, cracking — gold is not recommended if having these ten defects. // Rcūm 14.11 //
{Purification: purpose}

children.text: svarṇakāryaṃ na tena syāttasmāt śuddhir vidhīyate /
children.translated_text: Gold-work cannot be done with that; therefore purification is prescribed.

children.text: śodhyaṃ na kevalaṃ svarṇaṃ lohānyanyāni śodhayet // Rcūm_14.12 //
children.translated_text: Not only gold should be purified — one should purify other metals too. // Rcūm 14.12 //

body.translated_text:
{Mixed metal: production}
From the combination of gold, silver, etc., mixed metals are produced.

children.translated_text: {Gold: refreshing its color}
A gold leaf measuring one <s>karṣa</s>, sealed in a saucer-lid, combined with a sharp mineral,

children.text: aṅgārasaṃsthaṃ praharārdhamānaṃ dhmātena tatsyānnanu pūrṇavarṇam // Rcūm_14.13 //
children.translated_text: placed on charcoal for half a <s>prahara</s> (one and a half hours), blown upon — that will surely become full in color. // Rcūm 14.13 //
{Metals: types of calcination}
The best calcination of all metals is by mercury-ash;
middling is declared to be by herbal roots; inferior is by sulphur and the like. // Rcūm 14.14 //
Calcination of a metal by its enemy-metal produces bad qualities.
{Gold: calcination}
Having made gold leaves perforated by thorns, one should smear [them] // Rcūm 14.15 //
with <s>luṅga</s> water, ash, and mercury — they die (are calcined) in ten heatings.
{Gold: calcination (alternative)}

children.text: drute vinikṣipet svarṇe lohamānaṃ mṛtaṃ rasam // Rcūm_14.16 //
children.translated_text: Into molten gold, one should introduce calcined mercury equal to the metal's weight; // Rcūm 14.16 //
powdering with <s>luṅga</s> water, combined with cinnabar (<s>darada</s>),

children.text: jāyate kuṅkumacchāyaṃ svarṇaṃ dvādaśabhiḥ puṭaiḥ // Rcūm_14.17 //
children.translated_text: gold attains saffron-colored [ash] in twelve heatings. // Rcūm 14.17 //
{Gold: calcination to irreversible state}
With the stem of <s>śleṣmāntaka</s> (Cordia) and gold-<s>rasa</s> powder, in cock-type heatings,

children.text: triṃśatpramāṇair apunarbhavaṃ syānniḥśeṣayogeṣu ca yojanīyam // Rcūm_14.18 //
children.translated_text: thirty in number, it becomes irreversible (<s>apunarbhava</s>) and should be employed in all formulations. // Rcūm 14.18 //
{Gold: calcination (another method)}

children.text: sūtena piṣṭikāṃ kṛtvā svarṇaṃ ruddhvā śarāvake /
children.translated_text: Having made a <s>piṣṭī</s> (paste) with mercury and sealing the gold in a saucer,
with a small amount of antimony (<s>nīlāñjana</s>), burnt with a small quantity of cow-dung cakes, // Rcūm 14.19 //
the ash becomes saffron-colored — it should be employed in mercury and rejuvenative preparations.
{Gold: calcination (yet another method)}
With <s>snuk</s> (Euphorbia) milk, asafoetida (<s>hiṅgu</s>), cinnabar (<s>hiṅgūla</s>), orpiment (<s>śilā</s>), red lead (<s>sindūra</s>), and acid, // Rcūm 14.20 //
heated ten times, gold becomes lifeless (fully calcined);
it is highly praised for mercury [preparations], rejuvenatives, and metal-tinging. // Rcūm 14.21 //
{Gold: calcined, medicinal properties}

children.text: snigdhaṃ medhyaṃ viṣagaraharaṃ bṛṃhaṇaṃ vṛṣyamagryaṃ yakṣmonmādapraśamanaparaṃ deharogapramāthi /
children.translated_text: Unctuous, intellect-promoting, destroying poison and artificial toxins, nourishing, supremely aphrodisiac, excelling in calming consumption and madness, destroying bodily diseases,

children.text: medhābuddhismṛtisukhakaraṃ sarvadoṣāmayaghnaṃ rucyaṃ dīpi praśamitajaraṃ svādupākaṃ suvarṇam // Rcūm_14.22 //
children.translated_text: producing intellect, wisdom, memory, and happiness, destroying all <s>doṣas</s> and diseases, promoting taste and digestion, pacifying old age, sweet in post-digestive effect — such is gold. // Rcūm 14.22 //
{Gold: calcined, medicinal use}

children.text: etadbhasma suvarṇajaṃ kaṭughṛtopetaṃ dviguñjonmitaṃ līḍhaṃ hanti nṛṇāṃ kṣayāgnisadanaṃ śvāsaṃ sakāsārucim /
children.translated_text: This ash born of gold, combined with pungent ghee in double-<s>guñjā</s> dose, when licked, destroys in people: consumption, digestive weakness, asthma with cough and loss of appetite,

children.text: ojodhātuvivardhanaṃ balakaraṃ pāṇḍvāmayadhvaṃsanaṃ vṛṣyaṃ sarvaviṣāpahaṃ garaharaṃ duṣṭagrahaṇyādinut // Rcūm_14.23 //
children.translated_text: it enhances <s>ojas</s> (vital essence) and <s>dhātus</s> (tissues), gives strength, destroys anemia and acid reflux, is aphrodisiac, removes all poisons and artificial toxins, and cures chronic bowel disease and the like. // Rcūm 14.23 //
It destroys all diseases without remainder, removes fear of evil spirits and ghosts,
it prevents future diseases, and removes the fear of the three types of poison. // Rcūm 14.24 //
Everything except <s>bilva</s> (wood-apple) fruit is commended here as wholesome;
gold taken for ten years [allows] one to eat and live as one pleases;
no disease afflicts [such a person] for the span of life — there is no doubt. // Rcūm 14.25 //
{Silver: subtypes}

children.text: sahajaṃ khanisaṃjātaṃ kṛtrimaṃ ca tridhā matam /
children.translated_text: Innate (<s>sahaja</s>), mine-born (<s>khanisaṃjāta</s>), and artificial (<s>kṛtrima</s>) — silver is regarded as threefold;
each earlier type is successively superior in its own qualities. // Rcūm 14.26 //
{Silver: innate}
Silver born from mountains such as <s>Kailāsa</s> is innate (<s>sahaja</s>);

children.text: tatspṛṣṭaṃ hi mahāvyādhināśanaṃ dehināṃ bhavet // Rcūm_14.27 //
children.translated_text: merely by touching it, the great diseases of beings are destroyed. // Rcūm 14.27 //
{Silver: mine-born}

children.text: himācalādrikūṭeṣu yad rūpyaṃ jāyate hi tat /
children.translated_text: That silver which is born in the peaks of the <s>Himācala</s> mountains —

children.text: khanijaṃ kathyate tajjñaiḥ paramaṃ hi rasāyanam // Rcūm_14.28 //
children.translated_text: that is called mine-born by the experts; it is the supreme rejuvenative. // Rcūm 14.28 //
{Silver: <s>pādarūpya</s> (foot-silver)}
Tin that was placed at the sandals of <s>Śrī Rāma</s> and became silver —

children.text: tat pādarūpyam ityuktaṃ kṛtrimaṃ sarvaroganut // Rcūm_14.29 //
children.translated_text: that is called <s>pādarūpya</s> (foot-silver), artificial, and it cures all diseases. // Rcūm 14.29 //
{Silver: testing for good quality}

children.text: ghanaṃ snigdhaṃ mṛdu svacchaṃ dāhe chede sitaṃ guru /
children.translated_text: Dense, unctuous, soft, clear, white when heated and cut, heavy,

children.text: śaṅkhābhaṃ masṛṇaṃ sphoṭarahitaṃ rajataṃ śubham // Rcūm_14.30 //
children.translated_text: resembling a conch-shell, smooth, free from blisters — such silver is auspicious. // Rcūm 14.30 //
{Silver: testing for bad quality}

children.text: dāhe raktaṃ ca pītaṃ ca kṛṣṇaṃ rūkṣaṃ sphuṭaṃ laghu /
children.translated_text: Red, yellow, or black when heated, rough on the touchstone, cracking, light,

children.text: sthūlāṅgaṃ karkaśāṅgaṃ ca rajataṃ tyājyam aṣṭadhā // Rcūm_14.31 //
children.translated_text: coarse-grained, harsh-bodied — silver is to be rejected in these eight ways. // Rcūm 14.31 //
{Silver: purification}
On a <s>kharpara</s> (calamine dish), surrounded by ash and powder, one should arrange a rim;
therein one should place silver, combined with an equal amount of lead, // Rcūm 14.32 //
blowing repeatedly until the lead is consumed —

children.text: svacchaṃ saṃśodhitaṃ rūpyaṃ yojanīyaṃ rasādiṣu // Rcūm_14.33 //
children.translated_text: Pure, purified silver should be employed with mercury and other [substances]. // Rcūm 14.33 //
{Silver: calcination (<s>māraṇa</s>)}
One should make a cake (<s>piṣṭī</s>) of silver with <s>lakuca</s> (breadfruit) juice and mercury;

children.text: ūrdhvādho gandhakaṃ dattvā mūṣāgarbhe nirudhya ca // Rcūm_14.34 //
children.translated_text: placing sulphur above and below, sealing inside a crucible, // Rcūm 14.34 //
one should steam it in a sand-bath apparatus for one day with strong fire.

children.text: svāṅgaśītāṃ ca tāṃ piṣṭīṃ sāmlatālena marditām // Rcūm_14.35 //
children.translated_text: The self-cooled cake, ground with sour orpiment (<s>sāmlatāla</s>), // Rcūm 14.35 //
should be fired (<s>puṭa</s>) twelve times — the silver becomes ash (<s>bhasma</s>).
{Silver: calcination}
Ground with <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrites) powder and citron acid, fired gradually, // Rcūm 14.36 //
{Effect of over-calcination of an ash}

children.text: rāgaḥ syāt sarvalohānāṃ puṭādhikye na saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: With excess firings, a reddish tinge arises in all metals, without doubt;
the reddened [ashes] tinge [other substances] — serving both body and metal purposes. // Rcūm 14.37 //

body.translated_text: in thirty firings, that silver certainly becomes ash.

children.translated_text: {Silver: killed: medicinal properties}

children.text: rūpyaṃ vipākamadhuraṃ tuvarāmlasāraṃ śītaṃ saraṃ paramalekhanakaṃ ca rucyam /
children.translated_text: Silver is sweet in post-digestive taste, astringent-sour in essence, cooling, laxative, supremely scraping, and appetizing;

children.text: snigdhaṃ ca vātakaphajijjaṭharāgnidīpi balyapradaṃ sthiravayaskaraṇaṃ ca vṛṣyam // Rcūm_14.38 //
children.translated_text: unctuous, it conquers <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>, kindles the stomach-fire, bestows strength, stabilizes age, and is an aphrodisiac. // Rcūm 14.38 //
{Silver: killed: medicinal use}

children.text: bhasmībhūtaṃ rajatamamalaṃ tatsamau vyomabhānū sarvaistulyaṃ trikaṭukalitaṃ sāraghājyena yuktam /
children.translated_text: Spotless calcined silver, with equal [portions of] mica (<s>vyoma</s>) and sun-[metal] (<s>bhānu</s>), equal to all, combined with <s>trikaṭuka</s> (three pungents) and mixed with <s>sāragha</s> (mustard) ghee,

children.text: līḍhaṃ prātaḥ kṣapayatitarāṃ yakṣmapāṇḍūdarārśaḥ kāsaṃ śvāsaṃ nayanajarujaḥ pittarogānaśeṣān // Rcūm_14.39 //
children.translated_text: licked in the morning, it thoroughly destroys consumption (<s>yakṣma</s>), jaundice (<s>pāṇḍu</s>), enlargement of the abdomen (<s>udara</s>), hemorrhoids (<s>arśas</s>), cough, asthma, eye diseases, and all <s>pitta</s> disorders without remainder. // Rcūm 14.39 //
{Copper: subtypes}
<s>Mleccha</s> (foreign) and <s>Nepāla</s> (Nepalese) — of these two, <s>Nepāla</s> is the best.
That which is produced from mines other than <s>Nepāla</s> is called <s>mleccha</s> (foreign). // Rcūm 14.40 //
{<s>Mleccha</s> copper: physical properties}
White-black-reddish in hue, emetic, purgative, and hard;
even when washed, it becomes black again — this is <s>mleccha</s> copper. // Rcūm 14.41 //
