{<s>Nepāla</s> copper: physical properties}
Very unctuous, soft, red, able to withstand heavy hammering, heavy,

children.text: nirvikāraṃ guṇaiḥ śreṣṭhaṃ tāmraṃ nepālamucyate // Rcūm_14.42 //
children.translated_text: unchanged [in color], superior in qualities — that copper is called <s>Nepāla</s>. // Rcūm 14.42 //
{Copper: quality test: bad quality}
Pale, blackish-red, light, prone to cracking,

children.text: rūkṣāṅgaṃ sadalaṃ tāmraṃ neṣyate rasakarmaṇi // Rcūm_14.43 //
children.translated_text: rough-bodied, flaky copper is not desired for alchemical work (<s>rasakarma</s>). // Rcūm 14.43 //
{Copper: impure: defects}
Nausea, stupor, vertigo, burning, and diarrhea — these are the defects of copper, truly hard to bear;

children.text: viśodhanāt tad vigatasvadoṣaṃ sudhāmayaṃ syādrasavīryapāke // Rcūm_14.44 //
children.translated_text: through purification, it becomes free from its defects, nectar-like in taste (<s>rasa</s>), potency (<s>vīrya</s>), and post-digestive effect (<s>pāka</s>). // Rcūm 14.44 //
{Copper: purification}
Copper combined with alkali and acid, melted, mixed with ochre (<s>gairika</s>),
cast into buffalo buttermilk [containing] cow-dung, seven times — // Rcūm 14.45 //
it becomes free from the five defects and suitable for calcination.
{Copper purification}
Thin copper leaves smeared with rock-salt (<s>sindhu</s>), // Rcūm 14.46 //
blown [with bellows] and cast into antimony (<s>sauvīra</s>) [solution] — they are purified in eight repetitions.
{Copper: purification}
Smeared with neem water and alum, heated eight times, // Rcūm 14.47 //
the <s>arka</s>-leaf[-shaped copper pieces] are purified by immersion in <s>nirguṇḍī</s> (Vitex) juice.
{Copper: purification}
One should make copper leaves as thin as palm-leaves; // Rcūm 14.48 //

children.text: niṣkvāthya kāñjike yāmaṃ bhasmanā pariśodhya ca /
children.translated_text: boiling in sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>) for one <s>yāma</s> and cleaning with ash,

children.text: yāmaṃ kṣīreṇa niṣkvāthya tatraiva sthāpayeddinam // Rcūm_14.49 //
children.translated_text: boiling in milk for one <s>yāma</s> and keeping therein for one day, // Rcūm 14.49 //
for one day with salt in tamarind fruit paste,
wrapping with alum ground in lemon juice, // Rcūm 14.50 //
blowing and immersing once in goat's urine —
half the [weight of] copper, with rock-salt, [smeared] with cooked lemon water, // Rcūm 14.51 //
coated, blown, and cast into buttermilk mixed with buffalo dung.
That copper, with an equal portion of gold-colored <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrites), // Rcūm 14.52 //
should be blown with very strong charcoal once more;

children.text: vinā tāpyaistrivāraṃ ca cakrikāṃ kalpayettataḥ // Rcūm_14.53 //
children.translated_text: without pyrites, [blow] three times, then make it into discs. // Rcūm 14.53 //
Then in <s>trikaṭuka</s> (three pungents) decoction, keep for three days;

children.text: utkvāthya bhasmanā mṛjya jalaiḥ prakṣālya sāraghaiḥ // Rcūm_14.54 //
children.translated_text: then boiling, cleaning with ash, washing with water and mustard, // Rcūm 14.54 //
smearing with mustard-mixed sugar three times,

children.text: puṭed vanotpalaistāmraṃ bhavet svarṇasamaṃ guṇaiḥ // Rcūm_14.55 //
children.translated_text: one should fire the copper with forest-lotus — it becomes equal to gold in qualities. // Rcūm 14.55 //
A copper leaf placed inside an aloe (<s>kumārī</s>) leaf

children.text: puṭitaṃ doṣanirmuktaṃ pāṇḍuraṃ ca prajāyate // Rcūm_14.56 //
children.translated_text: and fired becomes free from defects and turns white. // Rcūm 14.56 //
Copper thus purified, free from all defects,
becomes suitable for rejuvenation (<s>rasāyana</s>), supreme for body and metal [transmutation]. // Rcūm 14.57 //

children.text: imāṃ śuddhiṃ vijānāti śivo vā nandikeśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: This purification is known [only to] <s>Śiva</s> or <s>Nandikeśvara</s>,

children.text: sarvalokāśrayaḥ śrīmān somadevo na cāparaḥ // Rcūm_14.58 //
children.translated_text: and the revered <s>Somadeva</s>, the refuge of all people — and no other. // Rcūm 14.58 //
{Copper: calcination}
Copper struck with <s>bali</s> (tin/alloy) and raised seven times,
becomes free from all defects and nectar-like. // Rcūm 14.59 //
Coating with a paste of <s>lakuca</s> (breadfruit) juice-ground sulphur,

children.text: tāmrapatrāṇi saṃsthāpya sthālīmadhye nirudhya ca // Rcūm_14.60 //
children.translated_text: placing copper leaves in a pot and sealing, // Rcūm 14.60 //
one should cook properly for one <s>yāma</s>; extracting the killed [product], one should powder it.
{Copper: killed: medicinal use}
That ash (<s>bhasma</s>), measured by a <s>valla</s>, wrapped in a betel leaf, // Rcūm 14.61 //
consumed, first causing vomiting and then purging after two <s>yāmas</s>,
destroys people's fever accompanied by colic and flatulence. // Rcūm 14.62 //

children.text: viṣaṃ garaṃ ca vegena vāmayatyeva niścitam /
children.translated_text: It certainly causes rapid vomiting of poison and [slow] toxic preparations (<s>gara</s>);
the prescribed diet should be cow's buttermilk with food. // Rcūm 14.63 //
In case of excess [reaction], excessive vomiting, or extreme burning,
one should apply cooling treatments appropriate to each condition. // Rcūm 14.64 //
In excessive vomiting, one should take cooled roasted sugarcane pieces,

children.text: yadvā bilvabhavaṃ kvāthaṃ sitayā saha pāyayet // Rcūm_14.65 //
children.translated_text: or one should administer <s>bilva</s> (Aegle) decoction with sugar. // Rcūm 14.65 //
<s>Barbūra</s> (Clerodendrum) bark juice should be drunk; for purging, with buttermilk.
{Copper: calcination}

children.text: śulbatulyena sūtena balinā tatsamena ca // Rcūm_14.66 //
children.translated_text: With mercury equal to the copper, with <s>bali</s> (tin) equal to that, // Rcūm 14.66 //
with orpiment (<s>tāla</s>) half that amount, and realgar (<s>śilā</s>) half of that,
making a fine black compound (<s>kajjalī</s>) resembling broken collyrium, // Rcūm 14.67 //
inside the womb-apparatus described in the chapter on apparatus,
one should place the <s>kajjalī</s> and copper leaves alternately,
cook for one <s>yāma</s>, and when self-cooled, powder it. // Rcūm 14.68 //
{Copper: killed: medicinal properties}

children.text: tāmraṃ tiktakaṣāyakaṃ ca madhuraṃ pāke ca vīryoṣṇakaṃ sāmlaṃ pittakaphāpahaṃ jaṭhararukkuṣṭhāmajūrttyantakṛt /
children.translated_text: Copper is bitter, astringent, and sweet, hot in potency after digestion, slightly sour; it removes <s>pitta</s> and <s>kapha</s>, ends stomach pain, leprosy (<s>kuṣṭha</s>), undigested toxins (<s>āma</s>), and fever;

children.text: ūrdhvādhaḥ pariśodhanaṃ viṣayakṛtsthaulyāpahaṃ kṣutkaraṃ durnāmakṣayapāṇḍurogaśamanaṃ netryaṃ paraṃ lekhanam // Rcūm_14.69 //
children.translated_text: it purges upward and downward, counteracts poison, removes obesity, produces hunger; it alleviates hemorrhoids (<s>durnāma</s>), consumption, and jaundice; it is excellent for the eyes and supremely scraping. // Rcūm 14.69 //

children.text: tattadrogaharānupānasahitaṃ tāmraṃ dvivallonmitaṃ saṃlīḍhaṃ pariṇāmaśūlamudaraṃ śūlaṃ ca pāṇḍuṃ jvaram /
children.translated_text: Copper, measured as two <s>vallas</s>, combined with the appropriate disease-specific vehicle (<s>anupāna</s>) and licked, [destroys] colic after digestion, abdominal enlargement (<s>udara</s>), colic, and jaundice, fever,

children.text: gulmaplīhayakṛtkṣayāgnisadanaṃ mehaṃ ca mūlāmayaṃ duṣṭāṃ ca grahaṇīṃ hared dhruvamidaṃ tatsomanāthābhidham // Rcūm_14.70 //
children.translated_text: abdominal tumors (<s>gulma</s>), splenic and hepatic [disorders], consumption, digestive weakness, urinary diseases (<s>meha</s>), hemorrhoids (<s>mūlāmaya</s>), and corrupt intestinal disease (<s>grahaṇī</s>) — this is certain. It is named <s>Somanātha</s> [formula]. // Rcūm 14.70 //
Nothing else equals this copper [preparation] — sweet and free from defects;
nothing else destroys all defects completely — aphrodisiac and suitable for the healthy. // Rcūm 14.71 //
{Copper: calcination}
With one <s>pala</s> of <s>bali</s> (tin), and equal [amounts of] the following powdered substances:
aconite (<s>viṣa</s>), Cyperus (<s>tindu</s>), <s>agni</s>, <s>śamyāka</s>, <s>vatsanābha</s>, and superior alum (<s>paṭu</s>), // Rcūm 14.72 //
glory-lily (<s>kalihāri</s>), realgar (<s>śilā</s>), three pungents (<s>vyoṣa</s>), orpiment (<s>tāla</s>), areca (<s>pūga</s>), and <s>karañjaka</s>,
making a powder thoroughly liquefied with lemon juice, // Rcūm 14.73 //

children.text: tatsarvaṃ khalvake bhāṇḍe vinikṣipya tataḥ param /
children.translated_text: placing all of it in a mortar vessel, then
copper leaves of one <s>pala</s>, pricked with thorns,
coated with one-quarter [weight of] mercury, should be buried in that paste. // Rcūm 14.74 //

children.text: etat sarvaguṇāḍhyatāprabhavitaṃ śrīsomadevoditaṃ guñjāyugmamitaṃ kaṇājyasahitaṃ saṃsevitaṃ hanti vai /
children.translated_text: This, endowed with all qualities, proclaimed by the revered <s>Somadeva</s>, measured as two <s>guñjās</s>, taken with gruel and ghee, truly destroys

children.text: gulmaplīhayakṛdvibandhajaṭharaṃ śūlāgnimāndyāmayaṃ vātaśleṣmasaśoṣapāṇḍunivahaṃ jūrttyāmayaṃ bhakṣitam // Rcūm_14.75 //
children.translated_text: abdominal tumors (<s>gulma</s>), splenic and hepatic [disorders], constipation, stomach [pain], colic, digestive weakness, <s>vāta</s>-<s>kapha</s> [disorders] with wasting and jaundice, and fever-disease. // Rcūm 14.75 //
A diet appropriate to the disease should be given; sour mercury [preparations] should be avoided.

children.text: etatsātmyīkṛtaṃ yena tena mṛtyur vinirjitaḥ // Rcūm_14.76 //
children.translated_text: He who has habituated himself to this has conquered death. // Rcūm 14.76 //
{Iron: subtypes}

children.text: muṇḍaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ ca kāntaṃ ca triḥprakāramayaḥ smṛtam /
children.translated_text: Iron (<s>ayas</s>) is known to be of three types: <s>muṇḍa</s> (wrought iron), <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (steel), and <s>kānta</s> (magnetic iron).
{<s>Muṇḍa</s>: subtypes}

children.text: mṛdu kuṇṭhaṃ kaḍāraṃ ca trividhaṃ muṇḍamucyate // Rcūm_14.77 //
children.translated_text: <s>Muṇḍa</s> (wrought iron) is said to be threefold: <s>mṛdu</s> (soft), <s>kuṇṭha</s> (medium), and <s>kaḍāra</s> (hard). // Rcūm 14.77 //

body.text:
{mṛdu:: phys. properties}
drutadrāvam avisphoṭaṃ cikkaṇaṃ mṛdulaṃ śubham /

children.translated_text: {<s>Kuṇṭha</s>: physical properties}
That which, when struck, spreads with difficulty — that <s>muṇḍa</s> is considered middling.
{<s>Kaḍāra</s>: physical properties}

children.text: yanmuṇḍaṃ bhajyate bhaṅge kṛṣṇaṃ syāttatkaḍārakam // Rcūm_14.78 //
children.translated_text: That <s>muṇḍa</s> which breaks upon bending and is black — that is <s>kaḍāra</s>. // Rcūm 14.78 //

body.translated_text:
{<s>Mṛdu</s>: physical properties}
Quick-melting, non-sputtering, smooth, soft, and auspicious.

children.translated_text: {<s>Muṇḍa</s>: soft: medicinal properties}
The supreme soft <s>muṇḍa</s> removes <s>kapha</s>, <s>vāta</s>, colic, hemorrhoids, undigested toxins, urinary diseases (<s>meha</s>), jaundice (<s>kāmalā</s>), and jaundice (<s>pāṇḍu</s>);

children.text: gulmāmavātajaṭharārttiharaṃ pradīpi śophāpahaṃ rudhirakṛt khalu koṣṭhaśodhi // Rcūm_14.79 //
children.translated_text: it removes abdominal tumors, <s>āma</s>, <s>vāta</s>-[disorder], and stomach pain; it kindles digestion, removes edema (<s>śopha</s>), produces blood, and purifies the bowels. // Rcūm 14.79 //
{<s>Tīkṣṇa</s> (steel): subtypes}

children.text: kharaṃ sāraṃ ca honnālaṃ tārāpaṭṭaṃ ca bhājaram /
children.translated_text: <s>Khara</s>, <s>sāra</s>, <s>honnāla</s>, <s>tārāpaṭṭa</s>, <s>bhājara</s>,
and <s>kālaloha</s> (black iron) — steel (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>) is said to be sixfold. // Rcūm 14.80 //
{<s>Khara</s> (rough steel): physical properties}
Rough, released from the mould (<s>pogara</s>), with a mercury-like sheen at the fracture,

children.text: namate bhaṅguraṃ yattat kharaloham udāhṛtam // Rcūm_14.81 //
children.translated_text: that which bends and is brittle — that is called <s>kharaloha</s> (rough steel). // Rcūm 14.81 //
{<s>Sāra</s> (core steel): physical properties}
That which has a quickly-breaking edge — that is called <s>sāraloha</s> (core steel).
With granular luster, pale, earthen — <s>sāra</s> is so described. // Rcūm 14.82 //
{<s>Honnāla</s>: physical properties}
Dark-pale in body, with granules like <s>cañcu</s> (tamarind) seeds, very granular,

children.text: chedane cātiparuṣaṃ honnālam iti kathyate // Rcūm_14.83 //
children.translated_text: and very rough when cut — that is called <s>honnāla</s>. // Rcūm 14.83 //
{<s>Bhājara</s>: physical properties}
Studded with diamond-like granules and dense fine lines,

children.text: nicitaṃ śyāmalāṅgaṃ ca bhājaraṃ tat prakīrtitam // Rcūm_14.84 //
children.translated_text: dark-bodied — that is proclaimed as <s>bhājara</s>. // Rcūm 14.84 //
{<s>Kālaloha</s> (black iron): physical properties}
Blue-black in luster, dense, smooth, heavy, and brilliant,
with an edge unbroken even when struck against [other] iron — that is considered <s>kālāyasa</s> (black iron). // Rcūm 14.85 //

body.translated_text: Each [successive variety] from <s>kharaloha</s> onward is a hundredfold better than the preceding one. // Rcūm 14.86 //

children.translated_text: {<s>Kharaloha</s>: medicinal properties}

children.text: rūkṣaṃ syāt kharalohakaṃ sumadhuraṃ pāke ca vīrye himaṃ tiktoṣṇaṃ kaphapittakuṣṭhajaṭharaplīhāmapāṇḍvartinut /
children.translated_text: <s>Kharaloha</s> (rough steel) is dry, very sweet, cooling in potency, bitter, hot; it thoroughly removes <s>kapha</s>, <s>pitta</s>, leprosy (<s>kuṣṭha</s>), stomach [pain], splenic [disease], undigested toxins, and jaundice;

children.text: sadyaḥ śūlayakṛdgadakṣayajarāmehāmavātāpahaṃ dīptaṃ cātirasāyanaṃ balakaraṃ durnāmamedo'paham // Rcūm_14.87 //
children.translated_text: it instantly removes colic, hepatic disease, consumption, old age, urinary diseases (<s>meha</s>), <s>āma</s>, and <s>vāta</s>; it kindles digestion, is a supreme rejuvenative, gives strength, and removes hemorrhoids and obesity. // Rcūm 14.87 //
{<s>Kānta</s> (magnetic iron): subtypes}
Magnetic iron (<s>kāntaloha</s>) is said to be fourfold: <s>romaka</s>, <s>bhrāmaka</s>,

children.text: cumbakaṃ drāvakaṃ ceti teṣu śreṣṭhaṃ paraṃ param // Rcūm_14.88 //
children.translated_text: <s>cumbaka</s>, and <s>drāvaka</s> — each successive one being superior. // Rcūm 14.88 //
{<s>Romaka</s>: origin}
From the magnetic stone being mined, there emerge

children.text: satejāṃsi hi romāṇi kāntaṃ tadromakaṃ matam // Rcūm_14.89 //
children.translated_text: lustrous hair-like [filings] — that magnetic [stone yielding them] is considered <s>romaka</s>. // Rcūm 14.89 //
{<s>Bhrāmaka</s>: origin}
On certain great mountains, the <s>bhrāmaka</s> stone is readily found;

children.text: tanmukhe kṣepaṇāllohaṃ cakravad bhramati dhruvam // Rcūm_14.90 //
children.translated_text: iron thrown near its face spins like a wheel, certainly. // Rcūm 14.90 //
{<s>Cumbaka</s>: origin}
On the <s>Vindhya</s> mountain, <s>cumbaka</s> stones kiss (attract) iron nails,
drawing them quickly, just as a woman [draws] the minds of young men. // Rcūm 14.91 //
{<s>Drāvaka</s> (flux): origin}
That which, upon contact, melts metals such as gold completely —
it is obtained with great difficulty on the <s>Tuṣāradhara</s> (snow-bearing) mountain. // Rcūm 14.92 //
{<s>Kāntaloha</s> (magnetic iron): testing}

children.text: pātre yasya prasarati jale tailabindurna lipto hiṅgurgandhaṃ visṛjati nijaṃ tiktatāṃ nimbakalkaḥ /
children.translated_text: In whose vessel a drop of oil does not spread on water; <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida) releases its own fragrance; <s>nimba</s> (neem) paste [retains] its bitterness;

children.text: pācyaṃ dugdhaṃ bhavati śikharākārakaṃ naiti bhūmau kāntaṃ lohaṃ tadidamuditaṃ lakṣaṇoktaṃ na cānyat // Rcūm_14.93 //
children.translated_text: boiled milk becomes dome-shaped and does not fall to the ground — that is <s>kānta</s> (magnetic) iron, described with these characteristics, and no other. // Rcūm 14.93 //
{<s>Kāntaloha</s>: medicinal properties}

children.text: kāntāyo 'tirasāyanottarataraṃ svasthe cirāyuḥpradaṃ snigdhaṃ mehaharaṃ tridoṣaśamanaṃ śūlāmamūlāpaham /
children.translated_text: <s>Kāntāyas</s> (magnetic iron) is supreme among all <s>rasāyanas</s>; in health, it grants long life; it is unctuous, removes urinary diseases (<s>meha</s>), pacifies the three <s>doṣas</s>, removes colic, indigestion, and piles;

children.text: gulmaplīhayakṛtkṣayāmayaharaṃ pāṇḍūdaravyādhinut tiktoṣṇaṃ himavīryakaṃ kimaparaṃ yogena sarvārtinut // Rcūm_14.94 //
children.translated_text: it removes tumors (<s>gulma</s>), splenic disease, liver disease, wasting, <s>pāṇḍu</s> (anemia), and abdominal disorders; it is bitter, hot, cooling in potency — what more? Through formulation, it removes all afflictions. // Rcūm 14.94 //
Each successive iron is superior in quality by a hundred-thousand fold;

children.text: kāntaṃ koṭiguṇaṃ tatra tadapyevaṃ guṇottaram // Rcūm_14.95 //
children.translated_text: <s>kānta</s> (magnetic) iron therein is ten-million-fold [superior], and even that is progressively superior in quality. // Rcūm 14.95 //
{Iron: purification}
Smeared with the blood of a hare and heated three times,
all iron beginning with <s>muṇḍa</s> (wrought iron) releases all its defects. // Rcūm 14.96 //
{Iron purification (method 2)}
Mixed with sea salt, heated, and quenched
in a decoction of <s>triphalā</s> (three myrobalans) — iron certainly sheds its mountain-impurities. // Rcūm 14.97 //
{Iron purification (method 3)}
A decoction of tamarind (<s>ciñcā</s>) fruit and leaves removes the impurity.
{Iron purification (method 4)}

children.text: yadvā phalatrayopetaṃ gomūtre kvathitaṃ kṣaṇam // Rcūm_14.98 //
children.translated_text: Alternatively, combined with <s>triphalā</s> and boiled briefly in cow's urine — // Rcūm 14.98 //
{Iron: calcination — water-floating test (<s>vāritara</s>)}
Having filed the iron, moistened it with ghee, and placed it in a shallow pan, one should heat it,

children.text: cālayan lohadaṇḍena yāvat kṣiptaṃ tṛṇaṃ dahet // Rcūm_14.99 //
children.translated_text: stirring with an iron rod until the added straw ignites. // Rcūm 14.99 //
Having ground and ground, one should thus heat it five more times;
alternatively, with the juice of <s>dhātrī</s> (āmalaka) leaves or with water boiled with <s>triphalā</s>, // Rcūm 14.100 //
the iron, heated four times by <s>puṭa</s>, certainly becomes water-floating (<s>vāritara</s>).
{<s>Tīkṣṇaloha</s> (cast iron): calcination}
Leafless sheets of <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (cast) iron [should be placed] in a strong fire; // Rcūm 14.101 //
having heated and immediately thrown them into water, in a stone mortar,
one should pound them with very heavy blows using a thick iron pestle. // Rcūm 14.102 //
The large pieces from that [mass], sealed between two crucibles,

children.text: dhmātvā siktvā jalaiḥ samyak pūrvavat kaṇḍayet khalu // Rcūm_14.103 //
children.translated_text: having heated and sprinkled with water properly, should be pounded as before. // Rcūm 14.103 //
That powder should be heated by <s>puṭa</s> with jaggery and <s>gandha</s> (sulphur) twenty times;

children.text: puṭe puṭe vidhātavyaṃ peṣaṇaṃ dṛḍhavattaram // Rcūm_14.104 //
children.translated_text: at each <s>puṭa</s>, thorough grinding must be performed. // Rcūm 14.104 //
Iron thus reduced to ash should be applied in the respective diseases.
{<s>Tīkṣṇaloha</s>: calcination [alternate method]}
Now, the aforementioned <s>tīkṣṇa</s> iron, with <s>vasubhallaka</s> (a type of tree) bark — // Rcūm 14.105 //
heated by <s>puṭa</s> with its leaf-juice thirty times with care,
a red ash is produced, resembling [the appearance of] cinnabar (<s>sindūra</s>). // Rcūm 14.106 //
{Iron ash}
Alternatively, the powder (<s>rajas</s>) obtained from <s>tīkṣṇa</s> iron filings, with <s>triphalā</s> water,

children.text: piṣṭvā dattvaudanaṃ kiṃciccakrikāṃ pravidhāya ca // Rcūm_14.107 //
children.translated_text: should be ground, a little rice added, and made into a disk (<s>cakrikā</s>); // Rcūm 14.107 //
having dried it with great care, it should be heated with five <s>puṭas</s>;

children.text: raktavarṇaṃ hi tadbhasma yojanīyaṃ yathāyatham // Rcūm_14.108 //
children.translated_text: that ash, red in color, should be employed as appropriate. // Rcūm 14.108 //
{Iron: calcination — non-reverting test (<s>niruttha</s>)}
With <s>matsyākṣī</s> (wild asparagus), <s>gandha</s> (sulphur), <s>vāhlīka</s> (saffron), ground with <s>lakuca</s> (breadfruit) juice,
smearing all the iron and covering it with <s>matsyākṣī</s> paste, // Rcūm 14.109 //
having heated it firmly with bellows until the <s>triśūlī</s> (trident-like flame) emerges,
then removing it and throwing it into a decoction of <s>triphalā</s> and cow's urine, // Rcūm 14.110 //
extracting it therefrom and hammering, taking out the killed iron,
and heating again as before — one should kill all the iron. // Rcūm 14.111 //
Having ground it, then with <s>gandha</s> (sulphur), jaggery, and <s>triphalā</s>,

children.text: puṭed viṃśativāreṇa nirutthaṃ jāyate dhruvam // Rcūm_14.112 //
children.translated_text: heated by <s>puṭa</s> twenty times — it certainly becomes non-reverting (<s>niruttha</s>). // Rcūm 14.112 //
{Iron ash}
Iron powder mixed with equal <s>gandha</s> (sulphur), ground with <s>kumārī</s> (aloe vera) water,

children.text: puñjīkṛtaṃ kiyatkālaṃ chāyāsthaṃ mriyate hyayaḥ // Rcūm_14.113 //
children.translated_text: heaped up and kept in the shade for some time — the iron is killed. // Rcūm 14.113 //
{Killed iron: medicinal use}

children.text: etatsyādapunarbhavaṃ hi bhasitaṃ lohasya divyāmṛtaṃ samyak siddharasāyanaṃ trikaṭukīvellājyamadhvanvitam /
children.translated_text: This non-reverting (<s>apunarbhava</s>) ash of iron is indeed a divine nectar; a perfectly accomplished <s>rasāyana</s>, combined with <s>trikaṭukī</s> (three pungents), cardamom (<s>vellā</s>), ghee, and honey,

children.text: hanyānniṣkamitaṃ jarāṃ ca maraṇaṃ vyādhīṃśca satputradaṃ diṣṭaṃ śrīgiriśena kālayavanodbhūtyai purā tatpituḥ // Rcūm_14.114 //
children.translated_text: in a <s>niṣka</s>-measure dose, it destroys old age, death, and diseases, and grants good offspring — ordained by the glorious <s>Giriśa</s> (Śiva) formerly for the father of <s>Kālayavana</s>, for his prosperity. // Rcūm 14.114 //
For those who regularly consume this, no accumulation of diseases arises,

children.text: jāyate ca sutaḥ śrīmān dhīdhairyyabalasaṃyutaḥ // Rcūm_14.115 //
children.translated_text: and a glorious son is born, endowed with wisdom, fortitude, and strength. // Rcūm 14.115 //
{<s>Kālaloha</s> and <s>kāntaloha</s>: superior quality of ash}
This ash should be prepared with <s>kālaloha</s> (black iron) or <s>kānta</s> (magnetic iron);
ash made from other irons does not possess such qualities. // Rcūm 14.116 //
{Iron: calcination}
That iron, ground with <s>matsyākṣī</s> milk, <s>gandha</s> (sulphur), and <s>aśman</s> (mica),

children.text: viṃśatiḥ puṭitaṃ vārānnirutthaṃ bhasma jāyate // Rcūm_14.117 //
children.translated_text: heated by <s>puṭa</s> twenty times — a non-reverting (<s>niruttha</s>) ash is produced. // Rcūm 14.117 //
{Killed iron: medicinal use}
Eight <s>palas</s> of that ash, with eight times the amount of cow's urine,
should be cooked in an iron vessel, stirring with an iron ladle. // Rcūm 14.118 //
This iron thus prepared, in a dose of two <s>vallas</s>,
destroys all diseases arising from the respective <s>doṣas</s>: // Rcūm 14.119 //

children.text: kṣayaṃ pāṇḍugadaṃ gulmaṃ śūlaṃ mūlāmayaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: wasting, <s>pāṇḍu</s> (anemia), tumors (<s>gulma</s>), colic, piles,

children.text: mehaṃ medo'gnimāndyaṃ ca yakṛtplīhaṃ ca kāmalām // Rcūm_14.120 //
children.translated_text: urinary diseases (<s>meha</s>), obesity, digestive weakness, liver and splenic diseases, and jaundice, // Rcūm 14.120 //

body.text: śvāsaṃ kāsaṃ ca kuṣṭhaṃ ca jvaraṃ śūlānvitaṃ tathā // Rcūm_14.121 //
body.translated_text: asthma, cough, skin diseases (<s>kuṣṭha</s>), and fever accompanied by colic. // Rcūm 14.121 //

children.translated_text: {<s>Kāntaloha</s>: medicinal use}

children.text: kāntaṃ tulyābhrasattvaṃ caraṇaparimitaṃ hema tattulyamarkaṃ vaikrāntaṃ tāpyarūpyaṃ krimiripukaṭukais tulyabhāgaiḥ sametam /
children.translated_text: <s>Kānta</s> (magnetic iron) with an equal portion of mica essence, one-quarter portion of gold, an equal amount of <s>arka</s> (calotropis) [ash], <s>vaikrānta</s>, <s>tāpya</s> (pyrites), silver — combined with equal parts of <s>viḍaṅga</s> (embelia), <s>kaṭuka</s> (picrorhiza), and other [pungent substances],

children.text: līḍhaṃ devadrutailaiḥ pravitarati nṛṇāṃ dehasiddhiṃ samṛddhāṃ pathyaṃ pūrvoktavat taddharati ca sakalaṃ rogapūgaṃ javena // Rcūm_14.122 //
children.translated_text: licked with <s>devadru</s> (deodar) oil, it bestows abundant bodily perfection upon people; with wholesome diet as stated before, it swiftly removes the entire mass of diseases. // Rcūm 14.122 //
This <s>kānta-rasāyana</s> (magnetic iron rejuvenative) destroys all diseases and is delightful;

children.text: balyaṃ vṛṣyaṃ suputrīyaṃ maṅgalyaṃ dīpanaṃ param // Rcūm_14.123 //
children.translated_text: it is strengthening, aphrodisiac, grants good offspring, auspicious, and a supreme appetizer. // Rcūm 14.123 //
{Iron: calcination}
Half a <s>pala</s> of filed iron, with the juice of young <s>bilva</s> (wood-apple) fruit,

children.text: piṣṭvā piṣṭvā pacetkṣipraṃ bhasmasājjāyate khalu // Rcūm_14.124 //
children.translated_text: ground repeatedly and heated quickly — it certainly becomes ash. // Rcūm 14.124 //
Likewise, with the juice of <s>liṅgī</s> (mallow) fruit or with the juice of <s>dhātrī</s> (āmalaka) fruit,
one should kill the iron as before — it becomes of superior quality. // Rcūm 14.125 //
{Killed iron: medicinal use}
With the alkalis of <s>punarbhū</s> (boerhavia), <s>sindhu</s> (rock-salt plant), <s>apāmārga</s> (prickly chaff flower), <s>vajriṇī</s> (euphorbia), and tamarind bark,

children.text: kṣāraiḥ sarvāyasāṃ bhasma sevitaṃ śāṇamātrataḥ // Rcūm_14.126 //
children.translated_text: the ash of all irons, taken in a <s>śāṇa</s>-measure dose, // Rcūm 14.126 //
combined with <s>triphalā</s> decoction, a person should drink monthly.
{<s>Maṇḍūra</s> (iron slag)}
For the purification of iron slag (<s>lohakiṭṭa</s>) — otherwise urinary stones (<s>aśmarī</s>) may form. // Rcūm 14.127 //
Unpurified iron [preparations] are regarded as emetics, like poison;

children.text: nandinā tu viśuddhyarthaṃ lohaṃ proktaṃ sudhāsamam // Rcūm_14.128 //
children.translated_text: but <s>Nandin</s> has declared that purified iron is equal to nectar. // Rcūm 14.128 //
{Iron: medicinal use}

children.text: rātrau kāntaśarāvake sthitavarāmitrājalaiḥ svādubhiḥ prātarmuṣṭimitaṃ khalu pratidinaṃ ṣaṇmāsam āsevitam /
children.translated_text: Kept overnight in a <s>kānta</s> (magnetic iron) vessel with the sweet waters of <s>varā</s> (triphalā) and <s>amitra</s> (enemy-plant), a fistful taken daily in the morning for six months —

children.text: hanyātpittakaphāmayān bahuvidhānkuṣṭhapramehāṃstathā pāṇḍuṃ yakṣmagadaṃ ca kāmalagadaṃ mūlāmayaṃ vātajān // Rcūm_14.129 //
children.translated_text: it destroys the many types of <s>pitta</s> and <s>kapha</s> diseases, skin diseases (<s>kuṣṭha</s>), urinary disorders (<s>prameha</s>), <s>pāṇḍu</s> (anemia), consumption (<s>yakṣma</s>), jaundice (<s>kāmala</s>), piles, and <s>vāta</s>-born diseases. // Rcūm 14.129 //
{Unpurified iron: medicinal properties}
Unpurified iron, even if non-reverting (<s>punarbhava</s>), displays its qualities only slightly and then causes
indigestion, digestive weakness, loss of appetite, tumors (<s>gulma</s>), swelling, fecal obstruction, laziness, and chest congestion. // Rcūm 14.130 //
{Tin (<s>vaṅga</s>): subtypes}
<s>Khuraka</s> and <s>miśraka</s> — tin is said to be of two types;

children.text: khuraṃ tatra guṇaiḥ śreṣṭhaṃ miśrakaṃ na hitaṃ matam // Rcūm_14.131 //
children.translated_text: of these, <s>khura</s> is superior in qualities, while <s>miśraka</s> is not considered beneficial. // Rcūm 14.131 //
{<s>Khuraka</s>: physical properties}

children.text: dhavalaṃ ca mṛdu snigdhaṃ drutadrāvaṃ sagauravam /
children.translated_text: White, soft, unctuous, quickly melting, and heavy.
{<s>Miśraka</s>: physical properties}

children.text: niḥśabdaṃ khuravaṅgaṃ syān miśrakaṃ śyāmaśubhrakam // Rcūm_14.132 //
children.translated_text: <s>Khura</s> tin is soundless [when bent], while <s>miśraka</s> is dark-whitish. // Rcūm 14.132 //
{Tin: medicinal properties}
Tin is bitter, hot, dry, and slightly aggravates <s>vāta</s>;
it destroys diseases of fat and <s>kapha</s>, kills parasites, and removes urinary disorders (<s>meha</s>). // Rcūm 14.133 //
{<s>Khura</s> tin: purification}
Having melted it and adding turmeric (<s>niśā</s>), thrown into <s>nirguṇḍī</s> (five-leaved chaste tree) juice,

children.text: viśudhyati trivāreṇa khuravaṅgaṃ na saṃśayaḥ // Rcūm_14.134 //
children.translated_text: <s>khura</s> tin is purified in three rounds — there is no doubt. // Rcūm 14.134 //
{<s>Miśraka</s> tin: purification}
With sour buttermilk ground with <s>varṣābhū</s> (a rainy-season herb), poison, and <s>sindhu</s> (rock salt),
the second [type of] tin, placed in a <s>kaṭvalā</s> vessel, becomes purified. // Rcūm 14.135 //
{Tin: calcination (<s>vaṅgamāraṇa</s>)}
Having smeared tin sheets with <s>arka</s> (calotropis) milk along with <s>satāla</s>,
light <s>puṭas</s> should be given with the alkalis of <s>bodhi</s> (fig) and tamarind (<s>ciñcā</s>) bark. // Rcūm 14.136 //
Having ground it, the resulting ash should be used — it is recommended for mercury and other preparations.
{Tin: calcination (method 2)}

children.text: pradrāvya kharpare vaṅgaṃ ṣoḍaśāṃśaṃ rasaṃ kṣipet // Rcūm_14.137 //
children.translated_text: Having melted tin in a shallow pan, mercury in one-sixteenth part should be added; // Rcūm 14.137 //
adding tiny bits of alkali little by little from <s>bhāradvāja</s> (broom) wood,
having ground it, the resulting ash is recommended for mercury and other preparations. // Rcūm 14.138 //
{Killed tin: medicinal use}
Tin ash in equal amount with <s>kānta</s> (magnetic iron), and mica ash equal to that,
should be ground with <s>kanyakā</s> (aloe vera) water and also with neem leaf juice; // Rcūm 14.139 //
then adding <s>bhūpāla</s> and <s>āvarta</s> (lapis lazuli) ash in equal parts,
it should be thoroughly ground with cow's urine and the mineral waters of <s>śilādhātu</s>; // Rcūm 14.140 //
then ground for eight days with <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium) water,
dried, powdered, and then combined in equal parts // Rcūm 14.141 //
with roasted <s>barbūra</s> (a resin) extract and <s>vākucī</s> (psoralea) seed powder;
then it should be placed in a container, strained through cloth. // Rcūm 14.142 //
It should be administered with turmeric (<s>rajanī</s>) essence ground in cow's buttermilk;
in a dose of four <s>vallakas</s> — this delightful tin <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative) — // Rcūm 14.143 //
certainly destroys urinary diseases (<s>meha</s>) of twenty varieties.
Rice (<s>śāli</s>), green gram soup (<s>mudgasūpa</s>), sesame-derived butter (<s>navanīta</s>),

children.text: paṭolaṃ tiktatuṇḍīraṃ takraṃ pathyaṃ praśasyate // Rcūm_14.144 //
children.translated_text: <s>paṭola</s> (pointed gourd), bitter <s>tuṇḍīra</s>, and buttermilk are praised as wholesome diet. // Rcūm 14.144 //
{Lead: testing when pure}
Quickly melting, very heavy, black and lustrous when cut,
foul-smelling, black on the outside — such is pure lead; otherwise [it is impure]. // Rcūm 14.145 //
{Lead: medicinal properties}
Lead is very hot, unctuous, bitter, and removes <s>vāta</s>;
it destroys <s>prameha</s> (urinary disorders), dropsy (<s>toya-doṣa</s>), stimulates digestion, and removes <s>āmavāta</s> (rheumatism). // Rcūm 14.146 //
{Lead: purification}
In a decoction of <s>sinduvāra</s> (five-leaved chaste tree) roots, turmeric powder should be added;

children.text: drutaṃ nāgaṃ ca nirguṇḍyāstrivāraṃ nikṣipedrase // Rcūm_14.147 //
children.translated_text: molten lead (<s>nāga</s>) should be thrown three times into <s>nirguṇḍī</s> juice. // Rcūm 14.147 //
{<s>Bhrāṣṭra</s> apparatus}
In a sideways-shaped furnace (<s>cullī</s>), a pot with a sideways opening should be placed;

children.text: taṃ ca vaktraṃ vinā sarvaṃ gopayedyatnato mṛdā /
children.translated_text: its entire opening should be carefully covered with clay, except [the main vent];
this is called the <s>bhrāṣṭra</s> apparatus — it is the best for the calcination of lead. // Rcūm 14.148 //

body.translated_text: Lead thus becomes pure and does not cause fainting, blisters, and the like.

children.translated_text: {Lead: calcination}
In that apparatus called <s>bhrāṣṭra</s>, lead should be placed —
twenty <s>palas</s> of lead — with intense fire below. // Rcūm 14.149 //

children.text: drute nāge kṣipetsūtaṃ śuddhaṃ karṣamitaṃ śubham /
children.translated_text: When the lead melts, pure mercury in one <s>karṣa</s> measure, auspicious, should be added;

children.text: vighaṭṭya nikṣipet kṣāramekaikaṃ hi palaṃ palam // Rcūm_14.150 //
children.translated_text: stirring well, alkali should be added, one <s>pala</s> at a time. // Rcūm 14.150 //
Of the tree called <s>arjuna</s>, and also of <s>mahārājagiri</s> —

children.text: dāḍimasya mayūrasya kṣiptvā kṣāraṃ pṛthak pṛthak // Rcūm_14.151 //
children.translated_text: throwing in the alkali of pomegranate (<s>dāḍima</s>) and peacock [feather ash] separately — // Rcūm 14.151 //
thus one should cook for twenty nights with fierce fire,

children.text: vighaṭṭayan dṛḍhaṃ dorbhyāṃ darvyā cātha prayatnataḥ // Rcūm_14.152 //
children.translated_text: stirring vigorously with both arms using a ladle, carefully. // Rcūm 14.152 //
A red ash is produced, also of pigeon-grey hue;

children.text: nāgaṃ doṣavinirmuktaṃ jāyate tu rasāyanam // Rcūm_14.153 //
children.translated_text: the lead (<s>nāga</s>) becomes freed from defects and turns into a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative). // Rcūm 14.153 //
{Lead: calcination — <s>niruttha</s> (non-adhering) test}
Lead that has been killed and revived ten times becomes perfected;
that dead lead, freed from all defects, is a <s>rasāyana</s>. // Rcūm 14.154 //
{Lead: uses of the calcined form}
Thus, lead-ash, with half the amount of <s>tāpya</s> (pyrites) ash,

children.text: pādaṃ pādaṃ kṣipedbhasma śulbasya rajatasya ca // Rcūm_14.155 //
children.translated_text: and a quarter each of the ash of copper and silver — // Rcūm 14.155 //
and also of the essences of magnetic iron (<s>kānta</s>) and mica (<s>abhra</s>), and of crystal (<s>sphaṭika</s>), separately —
all should be powdered together and heated with <s>triphalā</s> (three myrobalans) water. // Rcūm 14.156 //
With thirty dried cow-dung cakes from the forest, heated thirty times, and that [powder] ground,
should be combined with equal parts of <s>vyoṣa</s> (ginger, pepper, long-pepper) and <s>vellaka</s> (cardamom) powders. // Rcūm 14.157 //
Taken with honey and ghee, licked in the measure of a <s>valla</s> (small amount),

children.text: aśītiṃ vātajān rogān dhanurvātān viśeṣataḥ // Rcūm_14.158 //
children.translated_text: it destroys eighty diseases born of <s>vāta</s> (wind), especially <s>dhanurvāta</s> (tetanus), // Rcūm 14.158 //
all diseases of <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) without remainder, and all urinary diseases,

children.text: śvāsaṃ kāsaṃ kṣayaṃ pāṇḍuṃ śvayathuṃ śītakaṃ jvaram // Rcūm_14.159 //
children.translated_text: asthma (<s>śvāsa</s>), cough (<s>kāsa</s>), wasting (<s>kṣaya</s>), anemia (<s>pāṇḍu</s>), edema (<s>śvayathu</s>), chills (<s>śītaka</s>), and fever (<s>jvara</s>), // Rcūm 14.159 //
sprue (<s>grahaṇī</s>), <s>āma</s>-disorders (indigestion), and intractable digestive weakness,
and all rectal diseases — [each] with an appropriate vehicle (<s>anupāna</s>) for the respective disease. // Rcūm 14.160 //
{<s>Rītikā</s>: identification}

children.text: saṃtaptā kāñjike kṣiptā tāmrābhā rītikā matā /
children.translated_text: When heated and thrown into sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>), it appears copper-colored — that is considered <s>rītikā</s>.
{<s>Rājarīti</s>: identification}

children.text: evaṃ prajāyate kṛṣṇā kākatuṇḍīti sā matā // Rcūm_14.161 //
children.translated_text: Similarly, that which turns black is considered <s>kākatuṇḍī</s>. // Rcūm 14.161 //

body.translated_text:
{Brass (<s>pittala</s>)}
Brass is of two kinds: <s>rītikā</s> and <s>kākatuṇḍī</s> (crow-beak).

children.translated_text: {<s>Rītikā</s>: examination — good quality}

children.text: gurvī mṛdvī ca pītābhā sārāṅgī tāḍanakṣamā /
children.translated_text: Heavy, soft, yellowish in color, having a firm core, capable of being hammered,

children.text: susnigdhā masṛṇāṅgī ca rītikā tādṛśī śubhā // Rcūm_14.162 //
children.translated_text: very smooth and polished-bodied — such <s>rītikā</s> is auspicious. // Rcūm 14.162 //
{<s>Rītikā</s>: examination — bad quality}
Palish, coarse, dry, rough, unable to withstand hammering,

children.text: pūtigandhā tathā laghvī rītirneṣṭā rasādiṣu // Rcūm_14.163 //
children.translated_text: foul-smelling, and lightweight — such <s>rīti</s> is undesirable for alchemical and other [purposes]. // Rcūm 14.163 //
{<s>Rītikā</s>: medicinal properties}
<s>Rīti</s> (brass) is bitter in taste, dry, destroys parasites, and removes blood and bile disorders;

children.text: krimikuṣṭhaharā yogāt soṣṇavīryā ca śītalā // Rcūm_14.164 //
children.translated_text: it destroys worms and skin diseases; by [different] preparations, it is hot in potency yet cooling. // Rcūm 14.164 //
{<s>Rājarīti</s>: medicinal properties}
<s>Kākatuṇḍī</s> (prince's brass) is devoid of unctuousness, bitter, hot, and removes <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>;
it is proclaimed to destroy liver and spleen [diseases] and is cold in potency. // Rcūm 14.165 //
{<s>Rītikā</s>: purification}
Heated and thrown into the juice of <s>nirguṇḍī</s> (five-leaved chaste tree) mixed with <s>śyāmā</s> (black creeper) powder —
<s>rīti</s> (brass) certainly achieves purification in five [immersions]. // Rcūm 14.166 //
{Brass calcination}
Wrapped with lemon (<s>nimbū</s>) juice, realgar (<s>śilā</s>), and sulfur (<s>gandha</s>), and heated eight times —

children.text: rītirāyāti bhasmatvaṃ tato yojyā yathāyatham // Rcūm_14.167 //
children.translated_text: <s>rīti</s> (brass) attains the state of ash, and then should be employed as appropriate. // Rcūm 14.167 //
{<s>Rītikā</s>: production of <s>druti</s> (metallic exudate)}
The powder of golden brass (<s>suvarṇarītikā</s>), eaten and then excreted

children.text: chāgena kṛṣṇavarṇena mattena taruṇena ca // Rcūm_14.168 //
children.translated_text: by a black, intoxicated, young goat — // Rcūm 14.168 //

children.text: talliptaṃ kharpare dagdhaṃ drutiṃ muñcati śobhanām /
children.translated_text: that [excrement], smeared on a potsherd (<s>kharpara</s>) and burned, releases a beautiful <s>druti</s> (metallic exudate),
having a hue resembling the lustrous color of fourteen-[karat] gold. // Rcūm 14.169 //
It is said to be a transformer of body and metals, useful in mercury-based <s>rasāyana</s>.
{Brass: uses of the calcined form}

children.text: mṛtārakūṭakaṃ kāntaṃ vyomasattvaṃ ca māritam // Rcūm_14.170 //
children.translated_text: Killed tin (<s>arakūṭa</s>), magnetic iron (<s>kānta</s>), and killed mica-essence (<s>vyomasattva</s>) — // Rcūm 14.170 //
these three in equal parts, combined with equal amounts of <s>vyoṣa</s> (three pungents) and <s>jantu</s>-destroying [herbs],
combined with <s>brahmabīja</s> (nutmeg), <s>ajamodā</s> (celery seed), <s>agni</s> (Plumbago), <s>bhallātaka</s> (marking nut), and sesame (<s>tila</s>) — // Rcūm 14.171 //
consumed in the measure of one <s>niṣka</s>, it destroys parasites and skin diseases,
especially leucoderma (<s>śvetakuṣṭha</s>); it is appetizing, digestive, and beneficial. // Rcūm 14.172 //
{Bronze (<s>kāṃsya</s>): production}
With eight parts of copper and two parts of tin (<s>kuṭila</s>),

children.text: vidrutena bhavet kāṃsyaṃ tat saurāṣṭrabhavaṃ śubham // Rcūm_14.173 //
children.translated_text: melted together, bronze (<s>kāṃsya</s>) is produced — that from <s>Saurāṣṭra</s> is auspicious. // Rcūm 14.173 //
{Bronze: examination — good quality}
Sharp-sounding, soft, smooth, slightly dark yet bright,

children.text: nirmalaṃ dāharaktaṃ ca ṣoḍhā kāṃsyaṃ praśasyate // Rcūm_14.174 //
children.translated_text: spotless, and red when heated — bronze is praised in six ways. // Rcūm 14.174 //
{Bronze: examination — bad quality}

children.text: yatpītaṃ dahane tāmraṃ kharaṃ rūkṣaṃ ghanāsaham /
children.translated_text: That which is yellowish, copper-red when heated, rough, dry, unable to withstand hammering,
producing a dull sound, and lacking luster — bronze should be rejected in seven ways. // Rcūm 14.175 //
{Bronze: medicinal properties}

children.text: kāṃsyaṃ laghu ca tiktoṣṇaṃ lekhanaṃ dṛkprasādanam /
children.translated_text: Bronze is light, bitter-hot, scraping, and clarifies vision;
it destroys multitudes of worms and removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>; it is beneficial [when used] in vessels. // Rcūm 14.176 //
{Bronze: suitable for vessels}
Except for ghee alone, everything else consumed from bronze vessels by people

children.text: bhuktam ārogyasukhadaṃ hitaṃ sātmyakaraṃ tathā // Rcūm_14.177 //
children.translated_text: is health-giving, comfort-bringing, beneficial, and conducive to well-being. // Rcūm 14.177 //
{Bronze purification}

children.text: taptaṃ kāṃsyaṃ gavāṃ mūtre vāpitaṃ pariśudhyati /
children.translated_text: Bronze heated and quenched in cow's urine is purified.
{Bronze: calcination — <s>niruttha</s>}

children.text: mriyate gandhatālābhyāṃ nirutthaṃ pañcabhiḥ puṭaiḥ // Rcūm_14.178 //
children.translated_text: It is killed with sulfur (<s>gandha</s>) and orpiment (<s>tāla</s>), and becomes <s>niruttha</s> (non-adhering) in five <s>puṭas</s>. // Rcūm 14.178 //
{<s>Vartaloha</s> (bell-metal): production}
Bronze, lead, brass, iron, and snake-metal (<s>ahi</s>) — that born from these is <s>vartaloha</s> (bell-metal);
the same is called <s>pañcaloha</s> (five-metal alloy) by those who know metals. // Rcūm 14.179 //
{<s>Vartaloha</s>: medicinal properties}
Cold, sour, pungent, dry, and destructive of <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>;

children.text: rucyaṃ tvacyaṃ krimighnaṃ ca netryaṃ malaviśodhanam // Rcūm_14.180 //
children.translated_text: it promotes taste, is good for the skin, destroys worms, benefits the eyes, and cleanses waste. // Rcūm 14.180 //
{<s>Vartaloha</s>: food in vessels made of it}
All food, condiments, and soups prepared in vessels made of it,

children.text: amlena varjitaṃ cāpi dīpanaṃ pācanaṃ śubham // Rcūm_14.181 //
children.translated_text: excluding sour [items], are appetizing, digestive, and auspicious. // Rcūm 14.181 //
{<s>Vartaloha</s> purification}
<s>Vartaloha</s> (bell-metal), melted and thrown into horse urine (<s>aśvajala</s>), is purified.
{<s>Vartaloha</s> calcination}
<s>Vartaloha</s>, heated with sulfur (<s>gandha</s>) and orpiment (<s>tāla</s>), is killed (calcined). // Rcūm 14.182 //
In each of these formulations, it should be employed according to proper method,
with minerals, sub-minerals, metals and the like that are of good lineage, purified, and properly processed;
mercury succeeds [only] thus, not otherwise. // Rcūm 14.183 //
{General principle}
Gems, metals, cowries, shells, stones, horn, hoof, and thorns —

children.text: mahārasādyeṣu kaṭhoradehaṃ bhasmīkṛtaṃ tatkhalu sūtayogyam // Rcūm_14.184 //
children.translated_text: whatever is hard-bodied among the great minerals and others, when calcined to ash, that indeed becomes fit for mercury. // Rcūm 14.184 //
{<s>Bhūnāga</s> (earth-snake/earthworm): essence — used for dissolution}
For the dissolution (<s>drāvaṇa</s>) of diamond-class [substances], I declare the essence obtained from <s>bhūnāga</s> (earthworm);
that is the supreme brilliance for both the king of mercury and diamond. // Rcūm 14.185 //
{<s>Bhūnāga</s> essence: extraction}
The washed <s>bhūnāga</s>-born [substance] should be ground with juices of <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> (Eclipta),
with lemon (<s>nimbu</s>) juice, and with the expressed juice of <s>nirguṇḍī</s>, for three days separately. // Rcūm 14.186 //
That, combined with the fluxing group (<s>drāvaṇagaṇa</s>), well-ground and made into pellets,

children.text: nirudhya dṛḍhamūṣāyāṃ dvidaṇḍaṃ pradhamed dṛḍham // Rcūm_14.187 //
children.translated_text: sealed in a sturdy crucible, should be blown firmly for two <s>daṇḍas</s> (about 48 minutes). // Rcūm 14.187 //

children.text: svataḥ śītaṃ samāhṛtya paṭṭake viniveśya yat /
children.translated_text: After it cools naturally, taking out [the ingot] and placing it on a plate,
the granules, equal to mustard seeds, weighty even as fine particles — // Rcūm 14.188 //
combined with a twelfth part of gold (<s>arka</s>), smelted and made into granules,
one should perform the dissolution of diamond and similar [hard substances] with it as desired. // Rcūm 14.189 //
This essence of the donkey (<s>khara</s>) [variety of earthworm] is proclaimed as an unsurpassed <s>rasāyana</s>;

children.text: dvitrimūṣāsu caikasyāṃ sattvaṃ bhavati niścitam // Rcūm_14.190 //
children.translated_text: the essence is certainly obtained in two or three crucibles [i.e., attempts]. // Rcūm 14.190 //
{<s>Bhūnāga</s> essence: extraction (method 2)}
Earth-born snakes (<s>bhūnāga</s>, earthworms) produced from gold, silver, copper, iron, and magnetic iron [mines] —
having collected [them] in the measure of four <s>prasthas</s> — // Rcūm 14.191 //
washing them with turmeric (<s>rajanī</s>) water and also with cool water,

children.text: upoṣitaṃ mayūraṃ vā śūraṃ vā caraṇāyudham // Rcūm_14.192 //
children.translated_text: then a fasting peacock or a bold rooster (<s>caraṇāyudha</s>, "foot-armed") — // Rcūm 14.192 //
having fed [them to the bird] sequentially, one should then collect its excrement;

children.text: kṣārāmlaiḥ saha saṃpeṣya viśoṣya ca kharātape // Rcūm_14.193 //
children.translated_text: grinding it with alkalis and acids, and drying it in harsh sunlight — // Rcūm 14.193 //

children.text: tataḥ kharparake kṣiptvā bharjayitvā maṣīṃ caret /
children.translated_text: then placing it in a potsherd, roasting it, and extracting the soot;
the soot, combined with the fluxing group and well-ground — // Rcūm 14.194 //
sealing it inside a furnace, one should blow for two <s>ghaṭikās</s> (about 48 minutes);
from the cooled crucible, extracting the ingot (<s>khoṭa</s>), one should grind it. // Rcūm 14.195 //
Washing and quickly collecting the granules carefully,

children.text: suvarṇamānavad dhmātvā ravaṃ kṛtvā niyojayet // Rcūm_14.196 //
children.translated_text: smelting like gold and making into granules, one should employ them. // Rcūm 14.196 //
{<s>Bhūnāga</s> essence: ring made from it}

children.text: bhūnāgodbhavasattvam uttamatamaṃ śrīsomadevoditaṃ dattaṃ pādamitaṃ dviśāṇakanake kurvīta tenormikām /
children.translated_text: The supreme essence of <s>bhūnāga</s> (earthworm), as described by the illustrious <s>Somadeva</s> — one-quarter part given, combined with gold of two <s>śāṇa</s> weight, one should make a ring from it;

children.text: taddhautāmbuvilepanaṃ sthiracarodbhūtaṃ viṣaṃ netraruk śūlaṃ mūlagadaṃ ca karṇajarujo hanyāt prasūtigraham // Rcūm_14.197 //
children.translated_text: its wash-water applied as an ointment destroys poison from all living beings, eye disease, colic, hemorrhoids, and ear diseases, and overcomes complications of childbirth. // Rcūm 14.197 //
{Extraction of <s>aṅkola</s> oil (method 1)}
Now is described the <s>aṅkola</s> oil, with which mercury-ash and other [preparations] are made,
by the illustrious sons of the gods, the great ministers of holy fame. // Rcūm 14.198 //
Having made a thick paste of aged <s>aṅkola</s> (Alangium) seeds,

children.text: āḍhakapramitaṃ kumbhe vinidhāya nirudhya ca // Rcūm_14.199 //
children.translated_text: placing it in a pot in the measure of one <s>āḍhaka</s> and sealing it — // Rcūm 14.199 //
in the hole at the bottom of the pot, one should insert an iron rod;
in a deep, well-made pit, one and a half <s>hastas</s> in width — // Rcūm 14.200 //

children.text: tatra prādeśike gartte sīsapātraṃ nidhāya ca /
children.translated_text: in a small pit of one <s>prādeśa</s> therein, placing a lead vessel,

children.text: paṭaṃ ca paribaddhvā tu sandhibandhaṃ samācaret // Rcūm_14.201 //
children.translated_text: and tying a cloth, one should seal the joints. // Rcūm 14.201 //

children.text: laddibhiḥ pūrayed gartaṃ kaṇṭhāvadhi tataḥ param /
children.translated_text: The pit should be filled with dried cow-dung cakes (<s>laddi</s>) up to the brim; then
after six months, the oil collected in the lead vessel should be gathered. // Rcūm 14.202 //
{<s>Aṅkola</s> oil: medicinal use}

children.text: tena tailena saṃklinnāḥ pāṣāṇā ye bhuvartikāḥ /
children.translated_text: Stones and earth-wicks (<s>bhuvartikā</s>) soaked with that oil,

children.text: kūpe prakṣālitāḥ kṣiptā jvalanti niśi te ciram // Rcūm_14.203 //
children.translated_text: when washed and thrown into a well, burn for a long time at night. // Rcūm 14.203 //
A seed smeared with it will certainly germinate, as stated;
mercury is bound and killed by this oil without doubt. // Rcūm 14.204 //
A split pulse (<s>dāli</s>) made from gram (<s>caṇa</s>), kept in that oil for one month —
if one-quarter of it is eaten, it purges sixty times. // Rcūm 14.205 //

children.text: takraṃ bhaktaṃ tataḥ pathyaṃ dātavyaṃ rekaśāntaye /
children.translated_text: Buttermilk and rice should then be given as diet to calm the purgation;
at the end of a fortnight, with half the [previous] quantity of <s>dāli</s>, one should indeed purge again as before. // Rcūm 14.206 //

children.text: tato dālī tripādena cūrṇārdhena tataḥ param /
children.translated_text: Then with three-quarters of <s>dāli</s>, and after that with half the [amount of] powder —

children.text: pakṣe pakṣe virekeṇa sarvaṃ kuṣṭhaṃ vinaśyati // Rcūm_14.207 //
children.translated_text: fortnight by fortnight, through purgation, all skin diseases (<s>kuṣṭha</s>) are destroyed. // Rcūm 14.207 //
All diseases curable by purgation are destroyed — there is no doubt;
all diseases curable by purgation, especially leucoderma (<s>śvetakuṣṭha</s>). // Rcūm 14.208 //
{<s>Aṅkola</s> oil: medicinal use (continued)}
With a mere drop of that oil, purified mercury in the measure of a <s>guñjā</s> (rosary pea seed),
ground on a leaf of <s>ahilatā</s> (snake-creeper) and consumed along with the leaf — // Rcūm 14.209 //
it immediately produces a blazing, intense digestive fire,

children.text: saṃsevinaṃ naraṃ cāpi vṛkasyevāti bhojinam // Rcūm_14.210 //
children.translated_text: making the person who takes it like a wolf in voracious eating. // Rcūm 14.210 //
This <s>aṅkola</s> oil is indeed a transformer of body and metals;
by application of this oil, leucoderma (<s>śvetakuṣṭha</s>) is destroyed. // Rcūm 14.211 //
This <s>aṅkola</s> oil is declared to be a great essence (<s>mahāsattva</s>);
it becomes thick like ghee — thus is described all about it. // Rcūm 14.212 //
{<s>Aṅkola</s> oil: extraction method (2)}
Peeled <s>aṅkola</s> seeds, slightly crushed,

children.text: ruddhvā vidyādhare yantre daṇḍārdhaṃ prapacecchanaiḥ // Rcūm_14.213 //
children.translated_text: sealed in a <s>vidyādhara</s> apparatus, should be cooked slowly for half a <s>daṇḍa</s> (about 12 minutes). // Rcūm 14.213 //
The oil that collects in the upper vessel should be poured onto a betel leaf (<s>nāgavallī</s>).
{<s>Aṅkola</s> oil: medicinal use}

children.text: tasminguñjāmitaṃ sūtaṃ vimardya sadalaṃ graset // Rcūm_14.214 //
children.translated_text: One should grind a <s>guñjā</s>-measure of mercury in that and consume it with lentils. [Rcūm 14.214]

children.text: kuryād dīpanam uddhataṃ gurutaradravyādisaṃcūrṇanaṃ hanyādaṣṭavidhaṃ ca gulmam aruciṃ plīhāmayaṃ svāmayam /
children.translated_text: It produces intense digestive stimulation and the powdering of heavy substances; it destroys the eight types of <s>gulma</s> (abdominal tumor), loss of appetite, splenic disease, one's own disease,

children.text: śvitrādyaṃ sakalaṃ ca kuṣṭhamacirātpāṇḍvāmayaṃ ca jvaraṃ śūlaṃ mūlagadaṃ tathā śvayathukaṃ śvāsaṃ ca kāsaṃ nṛṇām // Rcūm_14.215 //
children.translated_text: <s>śvitra</s> (leucoderma) and all types of <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin disease), pallor, fever, colic, hemorrhoidal disease, swelling, asthma, and cough in humans. [Rcūm 14.215]
{Method for extracting <s>aṅkola</s> oil (3)}
The seeds of <s>aṅkola</s>, deprived of their stones, [made] fine, with hot water,

children.text: goṇyāṃ nikṣipya nistvañci vidhāya tadanantaram // Rcūm_14.216 //
children.translated_text: placing them in a cloth bag and removing the skins thereafter, [Rcūm 14.216]
then in alkaline water placed in a vessel, one should add
the pounded root of <s>tilaparṇī</s> therein in proper measure. [Rcūm 14.217]
Having rested for two nights therein, one should transfer it to another vessel.

children.text: śuṣke tu nirgataṃ tailaṃ kṣipennāgakaraṇḍake // Rcūm_14.218 //
children.translated_text: When dry, the oil that has emerged should be placed in a lead container. [Rcūm 14.218]
Split chickpeas should remain therein for three months.
At first, one should give only a quarter [dose] to a patient with <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin disease). [Rcūm 14.219]
By this, [the patient is] quickly purged thirty times; then thereafter

children.text: sasaṃbhaktaṃ tathā pathyaṃ dātavyaṃ śākavarjitam // Rcūm_14.220 //
children.translated_text: wholesome food should be given along with meals, but without leafy vegetables. [Rcūm 14.220]
One thus purged continuously for ten days

children.text: sarvakuṣṭhair vimucyeta vāraiḥ ṣaṭsaptabhiḥ khalu // Rcūm_14.221 //
children.translated_text: is certainly freed from all skin diseases in six or seven rounds. [Rcūm 14.221]
This is declared equal in qualities to the oil previously described.
{Method for extracting <s>aṅkola</s> oil (4)}
The roots of <s>uttaravāruṇī</s>, having been crushed, [should be mixed] with sour gruel. [Rcūm 14.222]
One should add the crushed paste of <s>aṅkola</s> seeds.

children.text: tattailaṃ ghṛtavatstyānaṃ paraṃ grāhyaṃ yathāvidhi // Rcūm_14.223 //
children.translated_text: That oil, thick like ghee, is the best and should be collected properly. [Rcūm 14.223]
{Method for extracting <s>aṅkola</s> oil (5)}
Having ground with <s>uttaravāruṇī</s>, one should then make leaf-cakes.
Then with that sour gruel, one should grind with the paste. [Rcūm 14.224]
The powder of <s>aṅkola</s> seeds, having bound that in a loose cloth,
suspending it in intense sunlight, one should place a cup beneath it. [Rcūm 14.225]
The oil that drips therein should be collected — it destroys <s>śvitra</s> (leucoderma).
{Method for extracting <s>aṅkola</s> oil (6)}
Powder produced from <s>aṅkola</s> seeds, ground with sour gruel, [Rcūm 14.226]
having rested for one night, that should then be made into a ball.

children.text: svedayet kanduke yantre ghaṭikādvitayaṃ tataḥ // Rcūm_14.227 //
children.translated_text: One should sweat it in the ball-apparatus (<s>kandukayantra</s>) for two <s>ghaṭikās</s> (48 minutes). [Rcūm 14.227]

children.text: tāṃ ca piṇḍīṃ dṛḍhe vastre baddhvā niṣpīḍya kāṣṭhataḥ /
children.translated_text: Having bound that ball in a strong cloth and pressing it with wood,
the oil that collects in the vessel below should be gathered and employed.
In this way, with the ball-apparatus, all oils may be extracted. [Rcūm 14.228]
Rcūm, Chapter 15
By the oceans of mercury [literature], not everything has been revealed.

children.text: daśāṣṭabhiḥ kriyāṃ vakṣye rasarājasya sāmpratam // Rcūm_15.1 //
children.translated_text: I shall now describe the eighteen operations of the king of mercury. [Rcūm 15.1]
The essence of all medicines beginning with nectar (<s>sudhā</s>) is established in mercury.

children.text: amartyā bhavituṃ martyā niṣevadhvaṃ mitho yutam // Rcūm_15.2 //
children.translated_text: O mortals, in order to become immortal, employ [mercury] combined with [other substances]. [Rcūm 15.2]
{Mercury: properties}

children.text: āyurvajraṃ vitarati nṛṇām aṅgavarṇaṃ suvarṇaṃ sattvaṃ vyomno madakaribalaṃ tāmram ugrāṃ kṣudhāṃ ca /
children.translated_text: It grants men a thunderbolt of longevity, excellent golden complexion, the essence of mica, the strength of a maddened elephant, copper, and intense hunger,

children.text: māyoḥ śāntiṃ rajatamamalaṃ kāntametatsamastaṃ śrīmān sūtaḥ sakalagadahṛd dehalohe tu siddhaḥ // Rcūm_15.3 //
children.translated_text: the pacification of death (<s>māyu</s>), the stainless purity of silver, and the attractiveness [of gold] — all this the illustrious mercury [provides], destroyer of all diseases, when perfected in body-metal [transmutation]. [Rcūm 15.3]
{Mercury: mythological origin}
At the beginning of the <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic age), out of the mutual love between <s>Śiva</s> and [<s>Pārvatī</s>], and from mutual desire to conquer,
their lovemaking commenced, causing agitation in the three worlds. [Rcūm 15.4]
<s>Agni</s> (Fire) was sent by the gods to stop the intercourse,
with the desire that a son be born from it to slay the demon <s>Tārakāsura</s>. [Rcūm 15.5]
Fire, having come in the form of a pigeon to the cave of <s>Himavat</s> (the Himalayas),
was agitated by the lack of wings (?), [and saw] the smiling amorous glance [of the couple]. [Rcūm 15.6]
Seeing him, <s>Śambhu</s> became embarrassed and ceased his lovemaking.
The semen that had flowed from within himself — he caught it with one hand. [Rcūm 15.7]

children.text: nikṣiptaṃ vadane vahner gaṅgāyām apatacca tat /
children.translated_text: It was placed in the mouth of Fire and fell into the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,

children.text: gaṅgayā ca bahiḥkṣiptaṃ nitarāṃ dahyamānayā // Rcūm_15.8 //
children.translated_text: and was cast out by the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, who was exceedingly burned [by it]. [Rcūm 15.8]
From this, minerals of superior qualities, equal to nectar, were born.

children.text: śivahastacyutaṃ yattat samabhūt khalu pāradaḥ // Rcūm_15.9 //
children.translated_text: That which fell from <s>Śiva</s>'s hand became mercury (<s>pārada</s>). [Rcūm 15.9]
By it, the foremost among the thirty [gods] became immortal and free from old age.
From the impurities of that [semen], the eight metals were born. [Rcūm 15.10]
That which fell from Fire's mouth — that truly became <s>rasa</s> (mercury).

children.text: sevitaḥ sa hi nāgendrair jarāmṛtyujigīṣayā // Rcūm_15.11 //
children.translated_text: It was consumed by the serpent-kings, desirous of conquering old age and death. [Rcūm 15.11]
That which fell from the mouths of the serpents while being drunk, due to its heaviness,
fell indeed into a well a hundred <s>yojanas</s> deep. [Rcūm 15.12]

body.text: īṣat pītāntaro rūkṣaḥ sa sūto dehalohakṛt /

children.translated_text: {Extraction of mercury using naked women}

children.text: snātāmādyarajasvalāṃ hayagatāṃ prāptāṃ jighṛkṣuśca tāṃ so'pyāgacchati yojanaṃ hi paritaḥ pratyeti kūpaṃ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: A woman just bathed after her first menstruation, mounted on a horse and approaching — desirous of seizing her, that [mercury] also comes forth for a <s>yojana</s> all around, and returns again to the well.

children.text: tanmārge kṛtagarttake ca bahuśaḥ saṃtiṣṭhate sūtarāṭ so'yaṃ tatra nivāsibhiḥ khalu janairevaṃ samānīyate // Rcūm_15.13 //
children.translated_text: In pits dug along its path, the king of mercury settles abundantly — thus it is collected by the people dwelling there. [Rcūm 15.13]

body.translated_text: Slightly yellowish inside, dry — that mercury is the maker of body-metal.

children.translated_text: {Mercury: extraction from earth}
That which, being carried from the <s>Gaṅgā</s> by wind and due to its heaviness,

children.text: apatad dūradeśe vai sa deśaḥ pāradaḥ smṛtaḥ // Rcūm_15.14 //
children.translated_text: fell in a distant land — that land is known as <s>Pārada</s> (the mercury-land). [Rcūm 15.14]
The mercury present in the earth there, by the method of distillation,

children.text: ānīyate sa vijñeyaḥ pārado gadapāradaḥ // Rcūm_15.15 //
children.translated_text: is extracted — it should be known as <s>pārada</s>, the disease-ferrying one. [Rcūm 15.15]

children.text: evaṃ caturvidhaṃ jātaṃ śaṃkaraṃ śāṅkaraṃ mahaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus fourfold was born the radiance of <s>Śaṅkara</s>, pertaining to <s>Śaṅkara</s>.

children.text: itthaṃ sūtodbhavaṃ jñātvā na rogair bādhyate naraḥ // Rcūm_15.16 //
children.translated_text: Having known the origin of mercury thus, a person is not afflicted by diseases. [Rcūm 15.16]
<s>Rasendra</s> (lord of mercury) and <s>rasa</s> (mercury) — both are perfected mercury.
The other two, born after a long time from the earth and the like due to regional conditions, require processing. [Rcūm 15.17]
{Mercury: etymology (<s>nirukti</s>)}
Because it savors (<s>rasanā</s>) old age, untimely death, misfortune, and disease — hence <s>rasa</s>.
[This is] by the meaning of the root <s>ras</s> meaning 'to savor/taste.' [Rcūm 15.18]
Because it produces (<s>sūte</s>) the perfection consisting of body-metal — hence it is considered <s>sūta</s>.
Because it ferries one across (<s>pārayati</s>) the ocean of disease — hence it is called <s>pārada</s>. [Rcūm 15.19]
When being purified by distillation, one quarter remains,

children.text: tripādī ca kṣayaṃ yāti tena pādarasaḥ smṛtaḥ // Rcūm_15.20 //
children.translated_text: and three quarters undergo decay — hence it is called <s>pādarasa</s> (quarter-mercury). [Rcūm 15.20]
{Mercury: defects (<s>doṣa</s>): mythological origin}
Having seen that mercury thus constituted, destroyer of death and disease for mortals,
[had made] humans equal to gods in strength and lifespan, [Rcūm 15.21]
<s>Indra</s> beseeched <s>Rudra</s>, who then endowed mercury with twelve defects —

children.text: yojayāmāsa taṃ pūrvaṃ vinā śuddhyāpi siddhidam // Rcūm_15.22 //
children.translated_text: that which previously, even without purification, granted perfection. [Rcūm 15.22]
{The defects of mercury (<s>pāradadoṣāḥ</s>)}

children.text: doṣo malo viṣaṃ vahnir mado darpaśca tatphalam /
children.translated_text: Defect (<s>doṣa</s>), impurity (<s>mala</s>), poison (<s>viṣa</s>), fire (<s>vahni</s>), intoxication (<s>mada</s>), pride (<s>darpa</s>), and [their] results:

children.text: mūrcchā mṛtyuḥ sadādāho visphoṭaśca śirobhramaḥ // Rcūm_15.23 //
children.translated_text: fainting (<s>mūrcchā</s>), death (<s>mṛtyu</s>), chronic burning (<s>sadādāha</s>), eruptions (<s>visphoṭa</s>), and vertigo (<s>śirobhrama</s>). [Rcūm 15.23]
{Mercury: sheaths (<s>kañcuka</s>)}
Born from earth, stone, water, copper, iron,

children.text: kañcukāḥ sapta sūtasya tābhiḥ sūto viṣopamaḥ // Rcūm_15.24 //
children.translated_text: lead, and tin — these are the seven sheaths (<s>kañcuka</s>) of mercury; through them, mercury becomes like poison. [Rcūm 15.24]

children.text: kuṣṭhaṃ jāḍyaṃ ca vātārtiṃ dāhaṃ cāvṛtakaṇṭhatām /
children.translated_text: They cause leprosy (<s>kuṣṭha</s>), numbness (<s>jāḍya</s>), wind-pain (<s>vātārti</s>), burning (<s>dāha</s>), throat obstruction,

children.text: unmādaṃ ca mahāśūlaṃ kramātkurvanti kañcukāḥ // Rcūm_15.25 //
children.translated_text: madness (<s>unmāda</s>), and severe colic — the sheaths produce these in succession. [Rcūm 15.25]

children.text: etān sūtagatān doṣān pañca sapta ca kañcukāḥ /
children.translated_text: Without removing these defects present in mercury — the five [defects] and seven sheaths —

children.text: anapākṛtya yo dadyāt sa vaidyo brahmahā bhavet // Rcūm_15.26 //
children.translated_text: the physician who [nevertheless] administers it becomes a killer of <s>Brahman</s> (guilty of mortal sin). [Rcūm 15.26]
The physician who removes these twelve great defects and then administers mercury

children.text: sa labheta mahatpuṇyam agaṇyaṃ ca mahadyaśaḥ // Rcūm_15.27 //
children.translated_text: obtains great merit, immeasurable, and great fame. [Rcūm 15.27]
{The eighteen <s>saṃskāras</s> (purificatory operations)}

children.text: sūte 'ṣṭādaśasaṃskriyā nigaditāḥ syuḥ svedanaṃ mardanaṃ mūrcchotthāpanapātarodhaniyamāḥ proddīpanaṃ grāsajam /
children.translated_text: Eighteen operations are prescribed for mercury: <s>svedana</s> (sudation), <s>mardana</s> (grinding), <s>mūrcchā</s> (solidification), <s>utthāpana</s> (revivification), <s>pātana</s> (distillation), <s>rodhana</s> (restraining), <s>niyama</s> (controlling), <s>proddīpana</s> (activation), <s>grāsa</s>-born

children.text: mānaṃ cāraṇagarbhabāhyajanitadrutiśca tajjāraṇā rāgaḥ sāraṇakaṃ parikramavidhir vedhastataḥ sevanam // Rcūm_15.28 //
children.translated_text: <s>māna</s> (measure), <s>cāraṇa</s> (impelling), internal and external <s>druti</s> (liquefaction), <s>jāraṇā</s> (digestion), <s>rāga</s> (coloring), <s>sāraṇaka</s> (streaming), <s>parikrama</s> (circulating), <s>vedha</s> (transmutation), and then <s>sevana</s> (therapeutic use). [Rcūm 15.28]
Now, by the method taught by <s>Nandi</s>, there is revealed
the complete purification of the defects and the sheaths. [Rcūm 15.29]
Mercury less than five <s>palas</s>, if purified, yields little result.
Above ten <s>palas</s>, it attains complete purification. [Rcūm 15.30]
{Mercury: purification (<s>śodhana</s>)}
By sudation, grinding, solidification, and seven upward distillations,
the king of mercury becomes freed from all defects. [Rcūm 15.31]
Sudation, grinding, and similarly seven-fold solidification —

children.text: sa hi siddhikaraṃ prāha guṇakāri ca bhāskaraḥ // Rcūm_15.32 //
children.translated_text: <s>Bhāskara</s> has declared that this produces perfection and virtue. [Rcūm 15.32]
By grinding, sweating, and deposition, it is purified — so says <s>Dineśvara</s>.
By upward and downward distillation, complete purification [is achieved] — so opines <s>Bhāluki</s>. [Rcūm 15.33]

children.text: svedanaṃ mardanaṃ mūrcchā pratyutthānaṃ ca pātanam /
children.translated_text: Sudation, grinding, solidification, revivification, and distillation,
restraining, and controlling — purification is considered sevenfold.
This is determined for the king of mercury by the venerable Lord <s>Govinda</s>. [Rcūm 15.34]
Now, the purification according to the method taught by the illustrious <s>Nandi</s>,
which destroys all the defects of the king of mercury, is described. [Rcūm 15.35]
{1. <s>Svedana-saṃskāra</s> (sudation operation)}
With radish, <s>agnipaṭu</s> (a pungent substance), mustard, and fresh ginger,

children.text: sveditastridivasaṃ hi dolayā kāñjikena malamuktaye rasaḥ // Rcūm_15.36 //
children.translated_text: and <s>vyoṣa</s> (three pungents), each one-sixteenth of the mercury — mercury should be sweated for three days in a swing-apparatus with sour gruel, for the removal of impurity. [Rcūm 15.36]
{2. <s>Mardana-saṃskāra</s> (grinding operation)}
With burnt wool, household soot, lotus, mustard, and <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery) with bricks,

children.text: mardyo rasaḥ ṣoḍaśāṃśais tryahaṃ tadvahniśāntaye // Rcūm_15.37 //
children.translated_text: mercury should be ground with one-sixteenth [of each], for three days, for the pacification of its fire [quality]. [Rcūm 15.37]

children.text: jīrṇe jīrṇe sadāgrāse mardanīyo rasaḥ khalu /
children.translated_text: Whenever each consumed dose is digested, mercury should indeed be ground.
By these very herbs, when pure, it receives coloring. [Rcūm 15.38]
{3. <s>Mūrchana</s> (solidification)}
By grinding with <s>vyoṣa</s>, <s>saubhāgya</s> (ginger), and <s>lakuca</s> (breadfruit) juice,

children.text: mūrchitastridinaṃ sūto madaṃ muñcati durdharam // Rcūm_15.39 //
children.translated_text: mercury solidified for three days releases its intractable intoxication (<s>mada</s>). [Rcūm 15.39]
{Removal of the poison-defect (<s>viṣadoṣa</s>)}
With <s>saubhāgya</s> (ginger), <s>triphalā</s>, black pepper (<s>śyāmā</s>), and borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), together with sour gruel,

children.text: tridinaṃ saṃsthitaḥ sūto viṣaṃ saṃtyajati svakam // Rcūm_15.40 //
children.translated_text: mercury stationed for three days releases its own poison. [Rcūm 15.40]
{Removal of the pride-defect (<s>darpadoṣa</s>)}
Raised by boiling with the juices of <s>sarpākṣikā</s>, <s>kamā</s>, and <s>vyoṣa</s>,

children.text: darpaṃ muñcati ca kṣipramiti doṣaviśodhanam // Rcūm_15.41 //
children.translated_text: it quickly releases pride — thus is the purification of defects. [Rcūm 15.41]
With alkalis, acids, and warm water, placed in a windless location,
[this] produces coolness of the potency of mercury — that is the destruction of [excessive] potency. [Rcūm 15.42]
{Removal of the earth-sheath (<s>bhūkañcuka</s>)}
Mercury ground for one day with <s>kāṃkṣī</s>, green vitriol (<s>kāsīsa</s>), and citron (<s>luṅga</s>) water,
washed with sour gruel, sheds its earth-sheath. [Rcūm 15.43]
{Stone-sheath (<s>adrikañcuka</s>)}
Mercury processed with the own juices of <s>girikarṇī</s> and <s>jayantī</s>,
in three rounds, sheds the mountain-born (stone) sheath from itself. [Rcūm 15.44]
{Water-sheath (<s>jalakañcuka</s>)}
Boiled for three days in a decoction of jaggery (<s>guḍa</s>), <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium), and <s>nimba</s> (neem),
mercury sheds the water-born sheath, which causes many defects. [Rcūm 15.45]
{Copper-sheath (<s>tāmrakañcuka</s>)}
Ground with sugar (<s>sitā</s>), fresh ginger (<s>sārdraka</s>), and buttermilk (<s>takra</s>), and then raised,
washed with warm cow's urine — it sheds the copper-born sheath. [Rcūm 15.46]
{Iron-sheath (<s>ayaḥkañcuka</s>)}
Mercury ground with the juices of <s>kāravellī</s> (bitter gourd) and <s>karkoṭī</s> (spiny gourd)
releases the iron sheath, as a fickle [person] releases friendship. [Rcūm 15.47]
{Lead- and tin-sheath (<s>nāga-, vaṅgakañcuka</s>)}
Mercury made into a paste with copper, distilled through a distillation apparatus,
quickly sheds the sheath born of lead and tin. [Rcūm 15.48]
{Tin-sheath (<s>vaṅgakañcuka</s>)}

Mercury smeared with <s>varā</s> (Terminalia chebula), <s>agnipaṭu</s>, drumstick (<s>śigru</s>), mustard, and antimony (<s>añjana</s>), ground to paste, [applied] on the upper part of the distillation apparatus —

children.text: bhāṇḍodare bhṛtajale parito vimuñcenmṛdvagninā tyajati kañculikāṃ hi vāṅgīm // Rcūm_15.49 //
children.translated_text: inside a vessel filled with water on all sides, with gentle fire it sheds its tin-jacket. // Rcūm 15.49 //
Mercury thus distilled, shining like a trembling streak of lightning,
freed from lead and tin — then this is produced. // Rcūm 15.50 //
Whenever mercury becomes afflicted by undigested bolus,
by this very method it should be distilled each time. // Rcūm 15.51 //
{Mercury: reviving (<s>āpyāyana</s>)}
After distillation, mercury maltreated by steaming and other purifications
becomes weak in potency; therefore one should perform reviving (<s>āpyāyana</s>). // Rcūm 15.52 //
Mercury placed in water with rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>) for up to three days,

children.text: punar āpyāyanaṃ prāpya na syāt ṣaṇḍho bhavedbalī // Rcūm_15.53 //
children.translated_text: having regained revitalization, becomes not impotent but powerful. // Rcūm 15.53 //
{Method of sweating (<s>svedanavidhi</s>)}
<s>Bhāluki</s> prescribes sweating and depositing, beyond the prescribed regimen,

children.text: bhakṣituṃ sarvalohāni mukhaṃ kartuṃ viniścitam // Rcūm_15.54 //
children.translated_text: in order to make mercury eat all metals and to open its mouth. // Rcūm 15.54 //
Having placed mercury in a vessel set on charcoal, one should assimilate

children.text: ṣoḍaśāṃśena citrāṃ tu tadatra svedanaṃ matam // Rcūm_15.55 //
children.translated_text: one-sixteenth part of <s>citrā</s> (Plumbago) — this is considered the sweating method here. // Rcūm 15.55 //
Endowed with potency and superior qualities, it cures all diseases;

children.text: vegena phaladāyitvaṃ jāyate nātra saṃśayaḥ // Rcūm_15.56 //
children.translated_text: it becomes swiftly efficacious — there is no doubt about this. // Rc��m 15.56 //
{Method of depositing (<s>saṃnyāsavidhi</s>)}
With alkalis, acids, and salts, likewise by the depositing method,
in the manner prescribed in the fourth chapter, in mercury — // Rcūm 15.57 //
hunger [for metals], pervasiveness, intensity, swift action,
the power to cure all diseases, and freedom from defects are produced. // Rcūm 15.58 //
{Kindling process (<s>dīpanasaṃskāra</s>)}
With pepper, lotus, mustard (<s>asurī</s>), <s>śigru</s> (drumstick), <s>bhūkhaga</s>, and borax,

children.text: sasaṃdhānais tryahaṃ svedād bhavetsūtasya dīpanam // Rcūm_15.59 //
children.translated_text: with decoctions, steamed for three days — thus is the kindling of mercury. // Rcūm 15.59 //
Also with the kindling group prescribed in the ninth chapter,

children.text: rasasya dīpanaṃ kuryāt tad atyantaguṇāvaham // Rcūm_15.60 //
children.translated_text: one should perform the kindling of mercury — that brings exceedingly great qualities. // Rcūm 15.60 //
{Mouth-opening (<s>mukhakaraṇa</s>)}
Mercury steamed with one-eighteenth part of gold —
with alkalis, acids, and defect-free [substances], its mouth opens to eat. // Rcūm 15.61 //
{Demon's mouth (<s>rākṣasavaktra</s>)}
With one-sixteenth part of pyrites essence (<s>tāpya-sattva</s>) and twice that of gold,

children.text: yuktaṃ yuktaṃ hi cukreṇa cūlikālavaṇena ca // Rcūm_15.62 //
children.translated_text: combined with vinegar (<s>cukra</s>) and <s>cūlikā</s>-salt, // Rcūm 15.62 //
with chickpea-alkali water and <s>rājanimbuka</s> (citrus) water,
one should grind in a heated mortar with great force. // Rcūm 15.63 //
For twenty-one days, one <s>yāma</s> (three hours) each day;

children.text: evaṃ rākṣasavaktraḥ syātsarvāśī ca na saṃśayaḥ // Rcūm_15.64 //
children.translated_text: thus it acquires the demon's mouth (<s>rākṣasavaktra</s>) — it devours everything, without doubt. // Rcūm 15.64 //

children.text: aṣṭādaśakriyā nṛṇāṃ na sidhyanti rasasya hi /
children.translated_text: The eighteen processes of mercury do not succeed for people

children.text: vinā bhāgyena tapasā prasādeneśvarasya ca // Rcūm_15.65 //
children.translated_text: without fortune, austerity, and the grace of the Lord. // Rcūm 15.65 //

children.text: sarvairyuktā vividhavidhibhiḥ saṃskṛtībhiḥ suramyaiḥ sūto muñcatyakhilavikṛtīn śvitrarogapramāthī /
children.translated_text: Endowed with all [processes], processed with various lovely procedures, mercury sheds all deformities and destroys leprosy (<s>śvitra</s>);

children.text: tāvacchuddhiṃ kṛtabahuguṇāṃ nandinoktāṃ susādhyāṃ pathyāyuktāṃ puravarapatiḥ somadevo'bhidhatte // Rcūm_15.66 //
children.translated_text: the lord of cities, <s>Somadeva</s>, proclaims that purification of many qualities, taught by <s>Nandin</s>, easily accomplished and joined with wholesome diet. // Rcūm 15.66 //
{Removing defects}

children.text: trikṣāraiḥ paṭupañcakāmlasahitaiḥ saṃkhalvasūtastryahaṃ bāhlīkāsuriviśvapiṇḍajaṭhare ruddhvātha saṃveśayet /
children.translated_text: Mercury ground with the three alkalis and the five sharp acids in a mortar for three days, then sealed inside a ball of <s>bāhlīka</s> (saffron), mustard, and <s>viśva</s> (dry ginger), one should place it

children.text: sandhāne tridinaṃ hi mandaśikhinā dolākhyayantre paceddoṣonmuktarasaḥ sudhārasasamaḥ pathyair vinā siddhidaḥ // Rcūm_15.67 //
children.translated_text: in a decoction in the <s>dolāyantra</s> (swing apparatus) for three days with mild fire — the mercury freed from defects becomes equal to the nectar of ambrosia, giving success even without dietary restrictions. // Rcūm 15.67 //
However, in this [procedure], the exact quantities of mustard, <s>viśva</s> (dry ginger), and asafoetida
should be learned from the guru's instruction — otherwise it does not bear fruit. // Rcūm 15.68 //
{Lead and tin: removal}
Lead and tin are great defects, unconquerable even by crores of purification;
since distillation purifies them, [distilled mercury] is considered greatly purified. // Rcūm 15.69 //
By ten distillations, the odor arising from lead and tin

children.text: gandho vināśamāyāti rasaḥ syānnaiva durguṇaḥ // Rcūm_15.70 //
children.translated_text: is destroyed — mercury then has no bad qualities. // Rcūm 15.70 //

children.text: daśavārāt paraṃ nārvāk śatavāraṃ ca pātanāḥ /
children.translated_text: From ten times upward, up to a hundred times, distillations

children.text: mahāguṇakarāḥ proktāḥ yathāvidhi kṛtā rase // Rcūm_15.71 //
children.translated_text: are said to produce great qualities when performed according to proper method on mercury. // Rcūm 15.71 //

children.text: mahāguṇatvaṃ śikhinaḥ sakhitvaṃ svalpeṣu rogeṣu ca tulyavīryam /
children.translated_text: Great qualities, friendship with fire, equal potency even in minor diseases,

children.text: rasāyanatvaṃ ca mahāprabhāvo bhavedrasendrasya ca pātanābhiḥ // Rcūm_15.72 //
children.translated_text: rejuvenative power, and great efficacy result from distillation of the lord of mercury. // Rcūm 15.72 //
<s>Rasendracūḍāmaṇi</s>, Chapter 16
Now is described the sacred <s>jāraṇā</s> (assimilation), the bestower of mercurial perfection,
easy to perform, requiring readily available materials, and previously accomplished. // Rcūm 16.1 //
{Mica: assimilation}
He who gives mercury a bolus of mica leaves to devour —
the Lord of <s>Gaurī</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), bowed to by the three worlds, is pleased by him. // Rcūm 16.2 //
{Wing-clipping leads to binding}
He who desires to bind mercury without clipping its wings,

children.text: bījaiḥ sa viṣayāsaktyā muktimicchati duṣṭadhīḥ // Rcūm_16.3 //
children.translated_text: is like one who, attached to sense-objects through his seeds [of desire], wishes for liberation — he is of corrupt intellect. // Rcūm 16.3 //
{Mica essence: for wing-clipping}
There is no other wing-clipper of mercury than mica essence (<s>ghanasattva</s>);

children.text: kṛttapakṣo niruddhādhvā rajyate badhyate rasaḥ // Rcūm_16.4 //
children.translated_text: with wings clipped and path restrained, mercury is tinged and bound. // Rcūm 16.4 //
Even moonless leaf-mica, when assimilated into mercury,

children.text: taccaretsaptadhā bhinnaṃ cīrṇaṃ cāpi samudgiret // Rcūm_16.5 //
children.translated_text: processes through it sevenfold; split and digested, it rises up. // Rcūm 16.5 //
Mercury with even a quarter-part of assimilated essence, employed in various formulations,

children.text: tattadroge phalaṃ śīghraṃ raso dhatte'dhikaṃ yataḥ // Rcūm_16.6 //
children.translated_text: quickly yields results in respective diseases, because mercury carries superior [potency]. // Rcūm 16.6 //
Where the essence is melted as a seed in the process of mercury-assimilation,

children.text: utkṛṣṭaṃ cāpi taddiṣṭaṃ guṇairaṣṭaguṇaṃ tathā // Rcūm_16.7 //
children.translated_text: that which is supreme is declared to have eightfold qualities. // Rcūm 16.7 //
The final mineral of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Pārvatī</s> is mica and mercury respectively;

children.text: etayor melanān nḥṇāṃ kva mṛtyuḥ kva daridratā // Rcūm_16.8 //
children.translated_text: from the union of these two, where for people is death? Where is poverty? // Rcūm 16.8 //
{Mercury: does not consume pure mica essence alone}
Mercury does not consume pure mica essence alone;
even if consumed, with great difficulty, it does not pervade all parts [of the body]. // Rcūm 16.9 //
Therefore, combined with other metals and mineral essences,
perfected with mica and alkali — the pure [mercury] alone grants bodily perfection. // Rcūm 16.10 //

body.translated_text: The unification of metals with mica is now described. // Rcūm 16.11 //

children.translated_text: {Pairing agent (<s>dvandvamelāpaka</s>) for metals}
With lac, jaggery, and <s>sarja</s> (resin) juices of magnetic iron, with <s>dhātakī</s>, <s>guggulu</s>, and borax,
