ground with woman's breast-milk in equal parts — even incompatible metals are fused. // Rcūm 16.12 //
{Pairing agent for metals (alternative)}
A metal pair combined with pyrites powder will certainly fuse,
by two or three rounds of blowing, like milk [mixing] with milk, certainly. // Rcūm 16.13 //
{Preparation of mica essence for assimilation}
Mica essence combined with an equal part of pyrites essence,
processed until mica predominates by blowing — that becomes easy to assimilate. // Rcūm 16.14 //
{Preparation of mica essence for assimilation (alternative)}
Alternatively, twice the amount of pyrites extracted into mica essence —
that, assimilated internally, quickly brings about the perfection of mercury. // Rcūm 16.15 //

children.text: {preparation of abhrasattva for cāraṇa with lead and tin}
children.translated_text: {Preparation of mica essence for streaming with lead and tin}
Similarly, with tin and lead, mercury should stream through mica essence;
that essence is suitable for metallurgical transmutation but condemned for bodily perfection. // Rcūm 16.16 //
These two impure [metals] — lead and tin — are of no excellence, being great defects;

children.text: rogāṃśca tanutaḥ śīghraṃ sevyamānau paraṃ khalu // Rcūm_16.17 //
children.translated_text: yet when properly consumed, they quickly thin out diseases indeed. // Rcūm 16.17 //
{Internal melting (<s>garbhadruti</s>)}
That essence, filtered through cloth, combined with <s>ravaka</s> (a flux),
ground with the lord of mercury in a copper vessel at one-tenth the amount, // Rcūm 16.18 //
that [substance] combined in one-sixty-fourth proportion with pure mercury,
with alkalis, acids, and salts, heated in a mortar for three days, // Rcūm 16.19 //
washed with hot decoctions, placed in a glass container,
with auxiliary substance (<s>viḍa</s>) placed above and below at one-eighth the amount of mercury, // Rcūm 16.20 //
placing birch-bark (<s>bhūrja</s>) at its mouth, wrapping with a single thread,
wrapping the container in cloth, by the swing-apparatus method, // Rc��m 16.21 //
one should steam for three days with all acids, cow-urine water, and sour gruel;
then placing it in a vessel of stone called <s>lohāśma-kambū</s>, // Rcūm 16.22 //
washing with hot decoctions, extracting the liquid through cloth,

children.text: viśoṣya lagnaṃ hastena mardayitvā kṣaṇaṃ rasam // Rcūm_16.23 //
children.translated_text: drying, rubbing the adhered mercury by hand for a moment, // Rcūm 16.23 //
placing in four-layered cloth and squeezing firmly — if all mercury

children.text: sarvo'pi yadi nirgacched garbhe grāsastathā drutaḥ // Rcūm_16.24 //
children.translated_text: passes through, the bolus in the womb is melted (<s>garbhadruti</s>). // Rcūm 16.24 //
{Internal melting: failure and repetition}
If some bolus remains, one should steam again with auxiliary substance;

children.text: evaṃ grāsatrayaṃ bhūyaḥ sampradāya prayatnataḥ // Rcūm_16.25 //
children.translated_text: thus giving up to three boluses again with effort, // Rcūm 16.25 //
when sixty boluses remain, after the internal melting process,
in the tortoise-apparatus (<s>kacchapayantra</s>) prescribed in the fifth chapter, // Rcūm 16.26 //
mercury combined with auxiliary substance should be heated with gentle fire and cow-dung cakes;
removing from the apparatus and washing again with hot sour gruel, // Rcūm 16.27 //
one should grind for one <s>yāma</s> (three hours) by the prescribed grinding method,
for the purpose of achieving clarity — when clear, it takes on color. // Rcūm 16.28 //

children.text: tasmānmardyo raso yatnād grāsaṃ grāse puṭe puṭe /
children.translated_text: Therefore mercury should be ground with effort, bolus by bolus, heating by heating;
well-ground, it acquires the power to destroy diseases. // Rcūm 16.29 //
{Mercury: streaming (<s>cāraṇa</s>)}
The substance for streaming is combined with <s>bhūsarjikā</s> (sodium carbonate), salt groups, <s>kāñcī</s> (a plant), and sour gruel.
{Mercury: streaming (continued)}

children.text: sattvopalādisakalaṃ varatāmrapatrairjuṣṭaṃ ca hyamlamuditaṃ rasacāraṇāya // Rcūm_16.30 //
children.translated_text: All essences, minerals, and the like, combined with excellent copper leaves, and acid — for the streaming of mercury. // Rcūm 16.30 //
{Assimilation (<s>jāraṇa</s>)}

With plantain, <s>paṭu</s> (sharp substance), <s>triphala</s>, <s>lāṅgalī</s> (Gloriosa), turmeric, half-portion of <s>śobhāñjana</s> (Moringa), and <s>aṅghri</s>, <s>kharamañjarikā</s>, and <s>aṅghrisaṃkhya</s> (specified amounts),

children.text: saptāhakaṃ parivibhāvitakāñjiko'sau klinnaṃ hi lohanivahaṃ grasatīha sūtaḥ // Rcūm_16.31 //
children.translated_text: with sour gruel saturated for seven days — thus prepared, mercury devours the mass of metals. // Rcūm 16.31 //
{Auxiliary substance (<s>viḍa</s>) for internal melting}

children.text: kṣāraiścaturbhir lavaṇaiśca ṣaḍbhir dravāmlamiśrair daśadhā vibhāvitaiḥ /
children.translated_text: With four alkalis and six salts, mixed with liquid acids and saturated tenfold,
this auxiliary substance (<s>viḍa</s>) is prescribed for the internal melting (<s>garbhadruti</s>) of gold and other metals and mica essences. // Rcūm 16.32 //
{Staff-bearer (<s>daṇḍadhārī</s>)}

children.text: vīthītulye gatamalarasaḥ pañcaśāṇapramāṇaṃ bhuktvā sattvaṃ gaganajanitaṃ ṣaṣṭikākṣāravahnau /
children.translated_text: Mercury freed from impurities, weighing five <s>śāṇas</s>, on an even surface, having devoured the sky-born (mica) essence, in the fire of sixty [measures of] alkali,

children.text: tattvaṃ hyetad vrajati sa javātsāradhūmāyanāni tattulyo'sau munibhirudito daṇḍadhārī ca nāmnā // Rcūm_16.33 //
children.translated_text: this truth [is that] it swiftly enters the streaming and fumigation processes; one equal to that is called by the sages the 'staff-bearer' (<s>daṇḍadhārī</s>) by name. // Rcūm 16.33 //
{Staff-bearer: test}
In mercury that has undergone internal melting, a straw cast upon it stands erect;

children.text: ūrdhvadaṇḍadharaḥ so'yaṃ daṇḍadhārī raso mataḥ // Rcūm_16.34 //
children.translated_text: this, holding a staff upright, is considered mercury of the 'staff-bearer' grade. // Rcūm 16.34 //
{Mercury: mica-digested, medicinal use}

children.text: yadi bhajati hi martyastulyajīrṇābhrasūtaṃ pratidinamiha guñjāmātrayā māsamātram /
children.translated_text: If a mortal consumes mercury with equally-digested mica, daily in <s>guñjā</s>-measure dose for one month,

children.text: śaśadharaparipāṭyā grāsayogena sa syāt sasukhahitaśatāyurmuktavārdhakyadoṣaḥ // Rcūm_16.35 //
children.translated_text: by the method of the moon-cycle, with the bolus regimen, he becomes one of pleasant and beneficial hundred-year lifespan, freed from the defect of old age. // Rcūm 16.35 //

body.translated_text: He too becomes free from wrinkles and grey hair, and free from disease. // Rcūm 16.36 //

children.text: tena tena hi yogena yojanīyo mahārasaḥ /
children.translated_text: By these various formulations, the great mercury should be employed.
{Mica essence: medicinal properties}

children.text: khasattvaḥ kurute tīvrāṃ kṣudhaṃ rogagaṇaṃ haret // Rcūm_16.37 //
children.translated_text: Mica essence (<s>khasattva</s>) produces intense hunger and destroys the host of diseases. // Rcūm 16.37 //
{Second bolus: mercury with double mica-digestion}
The second bolus should be given in one-eighth proportion;

children.text: cāraṇaṃ drāvaṇaṃ caivaṃ yathāpūrvaṃ prakalpyate // Rcūm_16.38 //
children.translated_text: the streaming and dissolving are performed as before. // Rcūm 16.38 //
The assimilation should also be done in the tortoise-apparatus;
the tortoise-apparatus is described in the fifth chapter. // Rcūm 16.39 //

children.text: ghanodbhūtaṃ sattvaṃ palaparimitaṃ viṃśatipuṭe rase catvāriṃśat parikalitacāraṃ ca jaritam /
children.translated_text: The dense-born essence, measured at one <s>pala</s>, in twenty firings for mercury, forty [firings] with measured processing and digestion,

children.text: payaḥpaṅkaprāyaṃ dviguṇajaritābhre vararase yadā tadvikṣiptaṃ rasitarasarūpaṃ saninadam // Rcūm_16.40 //
children.translated_text: becoming like a milk-paste, when digested with double mica in the supreme mercury — when that is cast, it assumes the form of sounding, resonant mercury. // Rcūm 16.40 //
{Mercury: digested with double mica: medicinal properties}

children.text: dviguṇagaganajīrṇaḥ sevitaḥ sūtarājaḥ pratidinamiha guñjāmātrayā varṣamātram /
children.translated_text: The king of mercury digested with double mica, consumed daily in a <s>guñjā</s> measure for one year,

children.text: vidadhati varakalpaṃ sindhukandarpatulyaṃ daśaśatamitavarṣaprāptadīrghāyuṣaṃ ca // Rcūm_16.41 //
children.translated_text: produces the state of a supreme <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic age), [making one] equal to <s>Kandarpa</s> (Cupid) the ocean-born, with a lifespan reaching a thousand years. // Rcūm 16.41 //
This lord of mercury, in a <s>guñjā</s> measure, consumed with <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) water,

children.text: kṣayādyān akhilān rogān duḥsādhyānapi sādhayet // Rcūm_16.42 //
children.translated_text: cures all diseases beginning with consumption, even those deemed incurable. // Rcūm 16.42 //
{Mercury: digested with triple mica}
By this sequential method, the third feeding (<s>grāsa</s>) should be given;
in the apparatus described in the fifth chapter, in the interior space,

children.text: nirudhya jāraṇāṃ kuryāt dravyasya vārttikaḥ // Rcūm_16.43 //
children.translated_text: sealing [it], the practitioner should perform the digestion (<s>jāraṇā</s>) of the substance. // Rcūm 16.43 //
{Third feeding ⇒ leech[-form] ⇒ upward sublimation ⇒ wing-clipping (<s>pakṣaccheda</s>)}

children.text: pariphalaghanayuktas triṃśatā tulyavārair grasati yadi rasendro yo jalaukākṛtiḥ saḥ /
children.translated_text: When the lord of mercury, endowed with dense [mica] fruits, consumes with thirty equal feedings, it assumes the form of a leech;

children.text: nikhilanihitamūrtiḥ niṣpatedudgato'sau punarapi nijapātre chinnapakṣaḥ sa sūtaḥ // Rcūm_16.44 //
children.translated_text: with its entire form deposited, it rises and emerges upward; [then] that mercury, with clipped wings, falls back into its own vessel. // Rcūm 16.44 //
{Mercury: digested with triple mica: medicinal use}

children.text: jātaḥ sūtas triguṇagaganagrāsasaṃpuṣṭamūrtir bhasmībhūtaṃ yavaparimitaṃ vajrabhasmādiyuktam /
children.translated_text: Mercury that has attained a body nourished by the consumption of triple mica, calcined, measured as a barley-grain, combined with diamond-ash and other [substances] —

children.text: taṃ cenmartyo bhajati hi sadā jāyate divyadeho jīvet kalpatridaśaśatikān vatsarāṇāṃ prakāmam // Rcūm_16.45 //
children.translated_text: if a mortal consumes that always, he obtains a divine body and lives for three hundred divine <s>kalpas</s> of years, at will. // Rcūm 16.45 //
Stupefied with pyrites ash in the measure of two mustard seeds,

children.text: hinasti sakalān rogān saptavāreṇa rogiṇam // Rcūm_16.46 //
children.translated_text: it destroys all diseases of the afflicted in seven doses. // Rcūm 16.46 //
{Fourth feeding}

children.text: baddho vā bhasmatāṃ nītaḥ siddhārthapramito naraiḥ /
children.translated_text: Bound or reduced to ash, measured as a mustard seed, by people,
combined with <s>vyoṣa</s> (three pungents), cardamom (<s>vellam</s>), and honey, consumed for four months, // Rcūm 16.47 //
it certainly makes a person free from wrinkles and grey hair,
full of the pride of an intoxicated biped, like <s>Kandarpa</s> (Cupid) in beauty. // Rcūm 16.48 //
Beautiful in a form that conquers the pride of <s>Kandarpa</s>, free from the torment of sin,
a person lives three thousand eight hundred years in this world;
and through its use, he delights a hundred women. // Rcūm 16.49 //
A thick [piece], as large as a <s>varā</s> (cowrie), equal to metal, merely by touch, effortlessly —
that mercury, having attained the bound state, certainly brings delight. // Rcūm 16.50 //
A mortal can raise the dead merely by casting [it] into the eyes;

children.text: nihanti sakalānrogānghrātaḥ śīghraṃ na saṃśayaḥ // Rcūm_16.51 //
children.translated_text: merely smelled, it quickly destroys all diseases — there is no doubt. // Rcūm 16.51 //
{Fifth feeding}
Thus the fifth feeding should be given in one-eighth portion;

children.text: sa pātrastho'gnisaṃtapto na gacchati kathañcana // Rcūm_16.52 //
children.translated_text: placed in a vessel and heated by fire, it does not escape in any way. // Rcūm 16.52 //
That is called 'wing-clipped' (<s>pakṣacchinna</s>); it is freed from all defects.
This mercury, consumed for three months in the measure of a mustard seed, // Rcūm 16.53 //
with <s>viḍaṅga</s> (Embelia), <s>triphalā</s>, and honey, [causes one to] meet the gods in the sky.
Merely by smelling, the lord of mercury cuts through all diseases. // Rcūm 16.54 //
These qualities of mercury have been declared by the practitioners of alchemy (<s>rasavādin</s>);

children.text: sakalāste guṇāḥ satyā bhairaveṇa prakīrtitāḥ // Rcūm_16.55 //
children.translated_text: all those qualities are true, proclaimed by <s>Bhairava</s> (Śiva). // Rcūm 16.55 //
{Sixth feeding}
The sixth feeding also should be given with four <s>palas</s>, as before;
digested with six times [its weight of] mica, the rise of its qualities equals nectar. // Rcūm 16.56 //
In the measure of a mustard seed, for one month, combined with sugar crystals (<s>khaṇḍopala</s>),
within a month it makes the body live for a hundred times [its normal] lifespan. // Rcūm 16.57 //

children.text: baddho'yaṃ kurute caiva mukhasthaḥ khecarīṃ gatim /
children.translated_text: This [mercury], when bound, placed in the mouth, produces the <s>khecarī</s> state (levitation);
it repels even a thousand divine weapons. // Rcūm 16.58 //
Having the strength of ten elephants, glorious, worshipped in all worlds,
when tinged (<s>rañjita</s>), made to flow (<s>sārita</s>), and properly endowed with transmuting power (<s>krāmaṇa</s>),
it becomes a ten-million-piercer; unbound, it pierces [even] a spear-[sized mass]. // Rcūm 16.59 //

children.text: samartho na rasasyāsya guṇān vaktuṃ mahītale /
children.translated_text: No one on the earth's surface is capable of describing the qualities of this mercury —

children.text: ko'pi śrīsomadevo vā prabhāvaṃ vetti śaṅkaraḥ // Rcūm_16.60 //
children.translated_text: only the revered <s>Somadeva</s>, or <s>Śaṅkara</s> [himself], knows its power. // Rcūm 16.60 //
{Seventh feeding}
The seventh feeding should be given with a double combination;

children.text: drāvaṇaṃ jāraṇaṃ tasya yathāpūrvaṃ prakalpayet // Rcūm_16.61 //
children.translated_text: its melting and digestion should be arranged as before. // Rcūm 16.61 //
This mercury, calcined, consumed in the measure of a nit (<s>likṣā</s>),
with <s>triphalā</s>, sugar (<s>malla</s>), and sugar-candy (<s>khaṇḍa</s>), within half a month, [transforms] a person — // Rcūm 16.62 //
rich in the beauty of ten million <s>Kandarpa</s>s (Cupids), with prowess equal to <s>Indra</s>,
worshipped by all the gods, with a lifespan of <s>Veda</s>-<s>kalpas</s> and <s>yugas</s>, // Rcūm 16.63 //
full of knowledge and [mastery of] time, endowed with knowledge of the three times,
powerful in cursing and blessing, delighting a hundred celestial women —

children.text: kurute nātra sandeho nandino vacanaṃ yataḥ // Rcūm_16.64 //
children.translated_text: it produces [all this] without doubt, for this is the word of <s>Nandin</s>. // Rcūm 16.64 //
This [mercury], tinged, made to flow, and endowed with transmuting power,

children.text: dhūmavedhī bhavennūnaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā // Rcūm_16.65 //
children.translated_text: surely becomes a smoke-piercer — no deliberation is needed here. // Rcūm 16.65 //
{Eighth feeding}
Then the eighth feeding should be given in equal portions;
the lord of mercury, having digested eight times [its weight of] mica-essence, even with hundreds of bellows-blasts, // Rcūm 16.66 //
does not flee at all, nor does anything [of it] diminish;
it is called 'fire-resistant' (<s>agnisaha</s>) by name, with qualities beyond enumeration. // Rcūm 16.67 //
Rich in power beyond enumeration, of wondrous potency and great strength —

children.text: likṣāmātro rasendro'yaṃ sevitaḥ sitayā saha // Rcūm_16.68 //
children.translated_text: this lord of mercury, in the measure of a nit (<s>likṣā</s>), consumed with sugar, // Rcūm 16.68 //
makes a person beautiful in all limbs in a single dose,
with sovereignty equal to <s>Rudra</s>, prowess equal to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, // Rcūm 16.69 //
beauty equal to the moon, brilliance equal to the sun,
lifespan equal to <s>Brahmā</s>'s, and eyes like those of <s>Garuḍa</s>. // Rcūm 16.70 //
Tinged, made to flow, and properly endowed with transmuting power,
this [mercury] becomes a sound-piercer, like <s>Śiva</s>, all-facing. // Rcūm 16.71 //
By the <s>Manthānabhairava</s> and other [texts], spread over hundreds of millions [of verses],
and by millions [more] entirely, these great qualities of mercury

children.text: śakyaṃ tenaiva saṃstotuṃ taraṅgā iva sāgare // Rcūm_16.72 //
children.translated_text: can be praised only by him — like waves in the ocean. // Rcūm 16.72 //
Due to the practitioner's inadequacy, due to <s>Śaṅkara</s>'s disfavor,
due to improper knowledge of medicines, due to incorrectly obtained drugs, // Rcūm 16.73 //
due to ignorance of the <s>gandhavatī</s> [technique], and due to improper practice,

children.text: na sidhyati kalau sūtaḥ saṃśayena prakurvatām // Rcūm_16.74 //
children.translated_text: mercury does not succeed in the <s>Kali</s> age for those who proceed with doubt. // Rcūm 16.74 //
{Characteristics of wing-clipped [mercury]}
Unable to rise or fall, with its path obstructed, not trembling,

children.text: jīrṇābhrako bhavetsūtaḥ chinnapakṣaḥ sa ucyate // Rcūm_16.75 //
children.translated_text: mercury with digested mica — that is called 'wing-clipped' (<s>chinnapakṣa</s>). // Rcūm 16.75 //
{Mercury: 'age' according to mica [digestion]}
With equal mica digested, it is an 'infant'; with double mica, an 'adolescent';
with quadruple mica consumed, a 'youth'; with sixfold mica digested, // Rcūm 16.76 //
an 'elder' and an 'advanced elder' — that is with eightfold mica.
The 'infant' acts on body and metal through [particular] formulation. // Rcūm 16.77 //
The 'boy,' having attained the cake-state (<s>piṣṭatā</s>), becomes effective for body and metal.
Mercury made to flow with gold, the 'youth,' produces <s>siddhis</s> (perfections). // Rcūm 16.78 //
The 'elder,' having reached the ash-state (<s>bhasmatva</s>), acts on body and metal.

children.text: ativṛddho raso vṛddho vaktrasthaḥ sarvasiddhidaḥ // Rcūm_16.79 //
children.translated_text: The 'advanced elder' mercury, placed in the mouth, bestows all <s>siddhis</s>. // Rcūm 16.79 //

children.text: tatra bālaḥ kumāraśca neṣyate tu rasāyane /
children.translated_text: Among these, the 'infant' and 'boy' are not desired for rejuvenation (<s>rasāyana</s>);
the 'youth' is for disease-destruction and also for body-protection; // Rcūm 16.80 //
both the 'elder' and 'advanced elder' are effective for body and metal [transmutation].

children.text: {mercury:: influence of jīrṇābhra on phys. properties}
children.translated_text: {Mercury: influence of digested mica on physical properties}
Digested with equal mica, it becomes somewhat fire-resistant in appearance. // Rcūm 16.81 //
Mercury digested with double mica does not turn to smoke [when heated].
The lord of mercury with triple mica attains binding like curd. // Rcūm 16.82 //
Mercury digested with quadruple mica produces bodily perfection (<s>dehasiddhi</s>).
Mercury digested with sixfold mica bestows a lifespan equal to <s>Brahmā</s>'s. // Rcūm 16.83 //
Mercury digested with sevenfold mica grants longevity with vigor;
when eightfold mica is digested, it bestows a lifespan equal to <s>Śaṅkara</s>'s.
{Measures against undigested feeding (<s>grāsājīrṇa</s>)}

children.text: grāsājīrṇarasaṃ pātya punaḥ saṃdīpya jārayet // Rcūm_16.84 //
children.translated_text: Mercury with undigested feeding should be sublimated, re-kindled, and [then] digested. // Rcūm 16.84 //

children.text: tataḥ śulbasya tīkṣṇasya kāntasya rajatasya ca /
children.translated_text: Then the seeds of copper, steel, magnetic iron, silver,

children.text: suvarṇasya ca bījāni vidhāya parijārayet // Rcūm_16.85 //
children.translated_text: and gold should be prepared and digested [into the mercury]. // Rcūm 16.85 //
{Mercury: digestion with copper}
By the method described for mica, the melting and digestion [is done] similarly.
The tinging agent for mercury is declared to be the digestion of steel, magnetic iron, and <s>arka</s> (Calotropis). // Rcūm 16.86 //
One should carefully proceed with sweating by appropriate alkalis and acids.

children.text: śatadhā daradavyūḍhaṃ tāmraṃ hi triguṇaṃ rase // Rcūm_16.87 //
children.translated_text: Copper, deposited a hundredfold with cinnabar, in triple [proportion] to mercury, // Rcūm 16.87 //
through digestion, produces [a mercury] resembling melted ruby;
mercury [made] powerful with copper, with prowess equal to the sun. // Rcūm 16.88 //
This mercury, having utterly annihilated the three <s>doṣas</s>, restores life amply.
This mercury consumed for a month, measured daily as one <s>guñjā</s>,

children.text: kuryādbhīmasamaṃ martyaṃ mukte ca bhuji vikramam // Rcūm_16.89 //
children.translated_text: makes a mortal equal to <s>Bhīma</s> in strength, and in wrestling, [equal to him in] prowess. // Rcūm 16.89 //
{Mercury: digestion with steel}
Transmuting power (<s>krāmaṇa</s>), digestion (<s>jāraṇā</s>), piercing (<s>vedha</s>), tinging (<s>rañjana</s>), and velocity-production (<s>vegakāritā</s>) —
[all these] arise in mercury from the feeding of steel deposited with a hundred [parts of] cinnabar. // Rcūm 16.90 //
Mercury with steel digested in equal proportion, consumed in a quarter-[<s>guñjā</s>] measure for two months,

children.text: karoti martyaṃ gatamṛtyubhītiṃ mahābalaṃ dhvastarujaṃ suputram // Rcūm_16.91 //
children.translated_text: makes a mortal free from the fear of death, of great strength, free from disease, and blessed with good sons. // Rcūm 16.91 //
Mercury digested with steel in double, triple, quadruple, and fivefold [proportions] —
who on this [earth] can describe the ever-increasing qualities of each successive [stage]?
{Mercury: digestion with magnetic iron}

children.text: kāntajīrṇarasaś caivaṃ guṇaiḥ koṭiguṇaṃ bhavet // Rcūm_16.92 //
children.translated_text: Mercury digested with magnetic iron likewise becomes ten-million-fold in qualities. // Rcūm 16.92 //

children.text: dviguṇajaritakānto vyādhibādhāṃ hinasti harati ca rasa uccairvyādhivakraṃ kṣaṇena /
children.translated_text: Mercury digested with double magnetic iron destroys the affliction of diseases; the mercury swiftly removes the host of diseases in an instant;

children.text: valipalitavikāraṃ duḥkhadāridryamṛtyuṃ janayati varaputraṃ saccaritraṃ rasendraḥ // Rcūm_16.93 //
children.translated_text: the lord of mercury destroys wrinkles, grey hair, deformity, suffering, poverty, and death, and produces an excellent son of good character. // Rcūm 16.93 //
{Mercury: digestion with gold}
In one-quarter proportion, in half proportion, in three-quarter, in equal proportion,
in double and triple proportions, and also in fivefold proportion — // Rcūm 16.94 //
gold deposited a hundredfold with <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrites), digested [into] the great mercury,
it becomes worshipped by the three worlds, with powers equal to the wish-fulfilling gem (<s>cintāmaṇi</s>). // Rcūm 16.95 //

children.text: {viḍa:: for jāraṇa of mercury with gold}
children.translated_text: {Alkali flux (<s>viḍa</s>): for digestion of mercury with gold}
With alkali extracted from the five parts of the <s>mūlaka</s> (radish) plant, [mixed] with washed cow's water,
sulphur triturated a hundred times — [this is] the alkali flux (<s>viḍa</s>) for the digestion of gold and other [metals]. // Rcūm 16.96 //
{Mercury: digested with equal gold: medicinal properties}
Mercury digested with equal gold, supremely worshipped for all its powers, consumed daily for one day's cycle in a <s>māṣa</s> measure,

children.text: bahuvidhagadamuktaṃ hanti vārdhakyamuccaiḥ vṛkajaṭharadṛḍhāśauddāmam agniṃ ca kuryāt // Rcūm_16.97 //
children.translated_text: destroys manifold diseases, greatly eliminates old age, and produces a digestive fire fierce and unbridled, like the stomach of a wolf. // Rcūm 16.97 //
The disease of barrenness and all incurability of a man

children.text: vinihanti na sandehaḥ kuryācchatadhanaṃ naram // Rcūm_16.98 //
children.translated_text: it destroys without doubt, and makes the person a hundredfold wealthy. // Rcūm 16.98 //
